title: Zac Taylor Sets Injury Table Following 2026 Bye Week, First Ravens Matchup Next
full_text:
The Bengals returned to practice Monday afternoon after the 2026 bye week. Zac Taylor spoke with the media following that session and gave the latest health update on his team.
Beyond the injured reserve list, Cincinnati looks pretty healthy as it enters a break-less stretch of the 2026-27 regular season. Just about every player on the 53-man roster reportedly got some type of work in on Monday. Cashius Howell (sick) was the only notable absence.
"I think he's progressing along, and so we'll kind of see where he's at," Taylor said about Kyle Dugger (quad), who entered the bye week-to-week. He also confirmed Howell missed today's session due to sickness.
Cincinnati is entering its most important game week of the season against Baltimore. The AFC North standing margins are razor-thin right now, with every team holding at least three wins and two losses.
The Bengals already lost a frustrating game against Pittsburgh; starting 0-2 in the division would be a tough hole to climb out of.
"It's exciting. I think our guys are really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but every point in Baltimore in a divisional game is a fun one to get out for, and our guys will be up for it," Taylor said.
Cincinnati will have to replace Tanner Hudson as a key member of its pass-catching depth. It may be showtime for 2026 seventh-round pick Jack Endries (one offensive snap this season) or just added burden on the other parts of the TE room.
"He's Mr. Dependable, whether he's on the practice squad, whether he's on the roster; he's going to show up," Taylor said about Hudson this season. "He's been who we thought he was. Tanner shows up and makes plays, never complains. Erick (All) goes down for a play; he's in. Mike (Gesicki) goes down for a play; he's in. He knows them all; he can play them all. I just need the defense to decide who he is, so we know if we're going to get base or nickel when he's in there."
Cincinnati has Tuesday off before three straight practice days this week.

title: Latest AFC North Projections Favor Bengals Ahead of Ravens Showdown
full_text:
The Bengals have emerged as the projected AFC North favorites entering Week 7 after the Browns pulled off a massive upset win over the Ravens on Sunday. The Bengals are the favorite to win the division at 40.7%, while the Ravens' chances dropped to 39.2% according to ESPN analytics.
The Steelers have a 15% chance to win the division and the Browns have a 5.1% chance, despite being 4-2 on the season.
The Bengals now face a crucial three-game stretch, with a chance to win in Baltimore this week. Should they beat the Ravens, they then face the Titans before traveling to Madrid to play the Falcons in Week 9.
Given the current state of all those teams and the Bengals having had time to get healthy over their bye week, they could realistically go 3-0 this stretch. The Browns and Steelers play each other in Week 8, while the Ravens go on to play the Bills in Buffalo and welcome the Jaguars to Baltimore in Week 9.
If the Bengals handle business against the Ravens, they could enter Week 10 with a 6-2 record. That would set up a game that could ulitimately decide the winner of the division against the Steelers on Sunday Night Football.
Pittsburgh could enter that game with a 6-2 record as well, with a game against the Saints next week, with the clash with the Browns after.
The toughest opponent in the division for the Bengals remains the Ravens even after they fell to the Browns. Baltimore has been without Lamar Jackson for the last two weeks, and all signs point to his return this week when Joe Burrow and company travel to Baltimore.
Regardless of the Browns' and Steelers' current records, the Ravens have the most potential to threaten the Bengals. Jackson has only lost to the Bengals three times in his career, with 11 total victories. Derrick Henry, meanwhile, has run all over the Bengals during his time with the Ravens, with 320 rushing yards and three touchdowns over four meetings.
If the Bengals are going to compete this season, they have to at least show they can slow down Jackson and Henry. Adding Dexter Lawrence this offseason should help, as he should have as big an impact in this upcoming game as he has at any point this season so far.
Should they successfully defeat Baltimore and stop Henry and Jackson, the momentum they would carry into the next two weeks would be massive.
Sinking the Ravens to a 4-3 record, while defeating them in their own stadium, should set the team up for a great run in November and December. That, in turn, could be the turning point that helps the team regain the AFC North crown and make a deep playoff run.

title: Bengals Standard Betting Underdogs Against Ravens in First 2026 Season Matchup

title: Bengals' Meeting With Ravens Gets Even Bigger After a Chaotic Week 6
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals had Week 6 off, but that didn't stop the rest of the AFC North from creating absolute chaos.
The Pittsburgh Steelers took an overtime victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, while the Cleveland Browns shocked the Baltimore Ravens with a last second field goal. We live in a world where the Browns lead the AFC North at 4-2, with the Ravens and Steelers also at 4-2, and the Bengals still at 3-2, placing them last.
Yes, the Bengals may be last in the division heading into Week 7, but the outcome of the Browns-Ravens game was exactly what Bengals fans should have been rooting for, and one that makes the Week 7 matchup even more important.
The Bengals are getting the chance to come into a physical divisional contest fresh, due to the bye week. They will also have the chance to get ahead of the Ravens in the division with a win.
After stumbling in their first division game this season against the Steelers, this meeting with the Ravens was already massive. Now, the Bengals have a chance to put the Ravens behind them in the standings, just before they take on a Tennessee Titans team that just picked up its first win.
Coming out of the bye week on the right foot would be huge for this team's playoff implications. It also could be the start of a winning streak that will keep the rest of the division on their toes.
Getting a victory in the AFC North is never easy. It's been especially difficult for the Bengals when they've played the Ravens in recent years.
The Bengals are 1-5 in the last three years in the regular season against the Ravens. Want to change the thinking around the league about your team? Then you have to beat the Ravens.
It's not the Bengals who are facing an injury at quarterback when these two teams meet on Sunday. (Knock on wood)
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the team's last two games after suffering an ankle sprain in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans.
Obviously, Jackson potentially being out is a huge impact on how this game could shake out. But something tells me the Bengals are going to planning for the former MVP to be on the field this Sunday.
The opportunity is here. Are the Bengals capable of answering the Challenge?

title: Cris Collinsworth Reveals What Bengals Must Change to Win AFC North
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' offense has been the main topic of the franchise since they selected quarterback Joe Burrow.
Burrow was given the keys to a franchise that was starving for success and helped lead the team to a Super Bowl appearance in the 2021 season. However, the superstar quarterback didn't do that alone.
The Bengals have given Burrow the weapons to have one of the most dangerous offenses in the league, this year is no different. But there is one unit on the offensive side of the ball that has to catch up to the rest if the Bengals are playing on making another deep postseason run.
The Bengals' run game has hindered the offense this season. After five games, the Bengals are averaging 82 yards per game on the ground. That puts them in the bottom ten of the league in that category.
Recently, Cris Collinsworth and his son, Jac Collinsworth, discussed how the run game has to get better for the Bengals to be able to compete in the physical AFC North.
"The Cincinnati Bengals are going to have to establish [the run] if they're going to knock off the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Baltimore Ravens," Collinsworth said .
Jac also made a great point about the other elite quarterbacks in the league having a talented backfield and using that to their advantage.
"Look at Kansas City and what they do with Mahomes," Jac explained.  "It's Kenneth Walker. Josh Allen; they're running the ball like crazy with (James) Cook."
The younger Collinsworth also pointed out that it felt like Samaje Perine gave the Bengals that throwback running style the team has been looking for in their win over the Miami Dolphins.
It would be coaching malpractice if the Bengals didn't try a way to get the run game going moving forward.
Everyone in that Bengals locker room knows that if the team begins running the ball with success, this offense becomes nearly unbeatable. But are Perine and Chase Brown enough to get this run game going?
To say time is running out when we're only in Week 6 must seem like an exaggeration, but really, there's no time to waste in the NFL.
If the Bengals want to be in the playoff race in December, they must find a way to find success on the ground, and it starts against the Baltimore Ravens in two weeks.

title: Bengals Offensive Line Cementing Among NFL's Top Half as Bye Week Rolls Forward
full_text:
The Bengals offensive line is cementing itself as one of the better blocking units in the league this season. Entering their Week 6 bye, Cincinnati is ranked 13th on Pro Football Focus's latest weekly OL ranking.
They jumped up one spot from the previous week as the continuity from last year is paying off in a big way.
"Four of the Bengals’ five starters on the offensive line have garnered PFF pass-blocking grades above 60.0, and the lowest-graded of the five, Ted Karras, has only been slightly below that mark at a 59.2. Right guard Dalton Risner is having an impressive season as a run-blocker, ranking third among right guards with an 80.7 PFF run-blocking grade," Gordon McGuinness wrote .
The raw PFF grades drive home what could be an even higher ranking. Cincinnati is now sixth in the NFL in PFF pass-blocking grade (70.8), while the run blockin g leaves more to be desired (17th, 62.7 grade).
It's not just PFF that loves the Bengals' blockers; Pro Football Network has the unit ranked 12th overall in its impact rankings . They've seemingly pulled off the long-time goal of blocking competence surrounding Joe Burrow.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor knows his team can keep getting even better, including the offensive line.
"There's a lot of moments where all the units played really well and did some really good things to build on," Taylor said on Monday. "And so coming out of Week 5, I think we recognize some things that we're doing really well, and then there's a couple of things that are really easy to clean up, real easy. So the good news is it's not a concern that Oh man, this is unfixable. We got a real problem here on this part of a scheme or a player, and we don't feel that at all. It's just a couple of things that we gotta get cleaned up going into the next division game."
Cincinnati's allowed one of the five lowest pressure rates this season as well.

title: Browns Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost With Four Weeks Left
full_text:
The Browns are in first place after beating two divisional opponents in three weeks. The roster is filled with exciting young talent, with reinforcements on the way in next year’s draft.
The offense has not been pretty and the defense looks suffocating. In order to keep up the winning ways, Andrew Berry should take a look at these realistic targets at the November 10 trade deadline.
The Cardinals upgraded their running back room in the offseason, and Conner dropped to third on the depth chart. They are not going to win their division or compete for the wild card, so they may want to acquire assets for next year. Conner has been productive in the league, and the amount of carries he would get would be spread out with the other running backs. He would be obtainable for a very low pick.
Fant was a first-round pick in 2019 and has bounced around the league since. He is a backup in New Orleans and only has nine catches this season, but three of those went for touchdowns. The Browns have Harold Fannin Jr., but no real talent behind him. Deshaun Watson has not developed chemistry with Fannin Jr. this season and the offense needs production from the tight end position.
The pass-catching tight end can provide another outlet for Watson and a stagnant offense. He can be had for a late-round pick if the Saints continue to lose and see their contention chances slip.
Every team is seeking offensive line help at the trade deadline and the Browns could use some depth after a complete rehaul in the offseason. They have not played great in the early portion of the season and Penning can help down the stretch. He has only played in three games this season, but would not cost much capital to obtain.
It is no secret that the Browns’ offense has struggled to run the ball this season. Both running backs who played in Sunday’s game were not with the team at the beginning of the season and the offense could use a reliable back. Pollard is averaging four yards per carry and would immediately upgrade the positional group. He is on an expiring contract and the Titans sit in last place in their division.
Dylan Sampson is set to return at some point, but Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders hit the injured list . Berry has three first fourth-round picks in next year’s draft and Pollard could be had for one of them.
The Chargers are in a tailspin at 0-6 and Mack is 35 years old. He signed a one-year, 18-million-dollar contract last offseason. He has three sacks and could bolster a surging defensive line. Due to his age and contract, the Browns would not have to give up too much to get him as a late-round pick should do it.
The downside would be that the compensation could get too high with other teams outbidding each other. The acquisition would also put the Browns over the salary cap.
The Browns’ roster has arrived early and Berry has some interesting options to upgrade the team right now. However, he has stacked draft picks for a deep draft next season and should not compromise good draft picks for the team this year.

title: Two Browns' Players Who Have Earned More Snaps After Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns sitting at 4-2 and leading the AFC North Standings after six weeks has to be one of the feel-good stories over the first half of the season.
However, work is far from finished.
Head coach Todd Monken’s group must still navigate the remaining 11 games, including rematches against the also 4-2 Steelers and Ravens, two games versus the 3-2 Bengals, in addition to improving the team’s current struggles, primarily in the ground game and at the quarterback position.
Here are two players -- on on offense and one on defense -- who should see their snap count incremented over the next few weeks based on what they’ve shown so far, along with the players that could see their minutes reduced, as the Browns will attempt to close out the 2026 regular season as successfully as they have started it.
Listen, I realize this might be an overreaction, but there’s really nothing to lose.
Over the course of the last three weeks, McLaughlin ripped off a 28-yard touchdown run in his only carry versus the Steelers -- second carry all-season long -- and followed that with a nine-carry 41-yard effort on Sunday, with starter Quinshon Judkins out of the lineup .
Even with such a minuscule sample, McLaughin leads the team with a 6.5 yard-per-carry average, success rate (54.5) than Judkins (41.1) or Raheim Sanders (33.3), as defined by Pro Football Reference.
Maybe McLaughlin will earn more carries out of pure desperation, as Sanders also missed last Sunday’s game, while second-year pro Dylan Sampson has yet to log an offensive snap this season, but at least McLaughlin has earned a larger share of the workload based on what he’s shown on limited carries.
So far, McLaughlin has played on 17.65 percent of the team’s offensive snaps, compared to Judkins’ 49.73 percent and Sanders’ 27.01 percent. Newcomer Audric Estime has already seen 5.08 of the offense’s snaps after joining the team last week , wasting no time in scoring his first touchdown for the Browns.
But regardless of when Judkins, Sanders and Sampson are ready to reappear for the team -- “Hopefully we’ll get Samp back this week and we’ll get Q back. We’re hopeful to get two,” stated Monken after the win over the Ravens regarding his backfield -- and how much of a factor they can be coming back from their respective energy, McLaughlin has made a solid argument in favor of, at the very least, a running back by committee approach.
While Sanders’ could see some of his snaps taken away as the team’s primary backup, the Browns need to consider taking away snaps from Judkins in favor of McLaughlin.
“J. Mac ran hard, man. He ran hard. He ran with a passion and a mission,” said Monken about McLaughlin’s performance versus Baltimore.
McLaughlin won’t solve the Browns’ ground game issues by himself, but at least there’s a spark there. It would be a shame to see it go to waste.
Grant Delpit’s first quarter head injury sustained against the Ravens might be the catalyst for a change here. Before Week 6, Delpit had participated in 100 percent of the defensive snaps in four out of the five first games, while logging a 97.2 percent in Week 4 versus the Steelers.
Along with Delpit, Ronnie Hickman has also been on the field almost on every defensive play, including a 100 percent snap count in five matchups and a 95.4 percentage in Week 4 against the Bucs.
This had left McNeil-Warren playing around 32 percent of defensive snaps before he set a personal best of 94.7 against the Ravens in Delpit’s absence. Nonetheless, the rookie out of Toledo has been spectacular over the first six games of his pro career, and is currently graded as the top safety in the NFL by PFF.
Combine that with the fact that Delpit has been playing at a subpar level, and Hickman has had an up-and-down season, there’s no reason to keep McNeil-Warren on the sidelines even if Delpit makes it back fast from his concussion.
Now factor in how much slot cornerback Myles Harden has struggled at times, just like Mekhi Blackmon, and it’s obvious that McNeil-Warren needs more time on the field, even if it’s in big nickel formations along with Delpit and Hickman.
The second-rounder has been a little overshadowed by all the offensive rookies from this year’s draft, but McNeil-Warren’s been more than living up to those hefty expectations.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Biggest Need Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
So far this season, the Cleveland Browns have surprised many people with their game results.
However, there still is one big issue that the Browns need to address with the trade deadline coming up.
The Browns Offensive Line Cannot Hold Up To The Ravens Rush. Deshaun Watson Is Just Trying Not To Get Sacked. This Browns Team Has Looked Ridiculous The Last 5 Quarters. Total Collapse. 😬 pic.twitter.com/yHTaCozrS1
Let's put it plain and simple, the Browns offensive line is not good.
This season, Deshaun Watson is the most sacked quarterback in the NFL after being dropped 24 times through the first six games.
While some have been to the fault of Watson, the offensive line has not given him much help at all.
Clearly, there needs to be improvement made to the unit going forward.
This past week, Watson was only able to throw for 164 yards. Watching the film, he was never able to get comfortable in the pocket. Most plays, Watson was forced to flee and try and make the play himself.
Lots of credit to Watson for having the ability to make those plays, but thats not what the Browns need.
It is incredibly hard for a quarterback to build confidence when he is constantly under attack from four-man pass rushes.
Going forward, the Browns need to either make some changes internally or bring in some help to try and bolster the passing game. Some of the plays up Todd Monken's sleeve cannot be run at the moment because they do not have enough time to develop.
As much as the pass game has been weak, the worst part of the Browns' offense this year has been the run game, without a doubt.
Historically, Cleveland is always super strong on the ground, no matter the state of the team. In the current day, some critics are putting the blame on Quinshon Judkins .
However, if you go back and watch the film, the bigger holes needed for the bigger back in Judkins are not there like they were last season.
Sure, faster running backs like Jaleel McLaughlin are able to get through the initial holes slightly better, but film shows that the run blocking overall needs work.
Cleveland seriously needed to take some time at the trade deadline to look at their current line group.
Maybe, they first try and switch some guys around. All five of the starters are brand new in 2026, so while they are getting used to the new team maybe get them used to a new side of the line.
If not, maybe they turn to a rookie like Parker Brailsford .
If that won't work, turn to free agency. While they don't have an insane amount to work with, the $15 million dollars in cap space should be enough to go out and sign a veteran lineman. While some fans may not like it, Jack Conklin is available.
Lastly, of course you could go for a trade. The main issue there is what you would have to give up and for who. If there's a chance to go out and get a solid starter for years to come, maybe then they should use some draft capitol to make it work.
However, I don't like the idea of giving up draft picks for a temporary fix, especially when Cleveland has been able to hit on draft picks like Austin Barber.

title: Where Deshaun Watson Needs To See Major Improvements Moving Forward
full_text:
While the Cleveland Browns took down the Baltimore Ravens 13-10 in their week six matchup, Deshaun Watson did not look great.
That is, until the fourth quarter.
Here are some areas where Cleveland's starter needs improvement:
Deshaun Watson 164 YDS / 0 TD / 0 INT No QBgami. That stat line has happened 21 times before, most recently by Bo Nix on Oct 17, 2024.
On many occasions, Watson cost the Browns plays and even drives due to his inability to get the ball out quickly.
Whther its entirely Watson's fault or poor play designing, something needs to change.
If Watson is going to keep holding on to the ball and being forced to roll out every play, teams are destined to sniff it out and create big plays defensively.
Not only can the Browns generate a more consistant offense with Watson getting the ball out fast, but they can also build his confidence.
Part of the reason why Deshaun Watson has been so good only in the fourth quarter is because it takes him the entire game to get comfortable with his offensive line and opposing defenses.
Especially as the season progresses, the Browns have to get their guy more comfortable faster.
Similarly to the last point, there have been too many times this season when Watson costs the Browns drives because he takes a sack or dumps the ball off to somebody else who gets tackled for a loss.
If nothing is there and you won't be penalized, just throw the ball away. No gain is better than a loss, ten times out of ten.
While turnovers thankfully have not been a big issue, this method limits those turnovers as well.
It all comes down to taking care of the football and extending drives.
This play deserves a little more love 3rd & 4 after Carson Schwesinger's forced fumble. Need a Touchdown badly. Deshaun Watson with a perfectly placed ball over Nnamdi Madubuike to KC Concepcion for 15 Yards... TD a few plays later #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/GDyXNulYRR
The glaring issue with Watson's play this season has been the fact that he is only hot for a small portion of the game.
As we get further into the season and even potentially into the playoffs, Watson needs to perform at a higher level throughout the entire game.
For example, in the first half against the Ravens, Watson went three for nine, with 32 total yards.
In each of the Browns' wins so far this season, head coach Todd Monken did one thing that helped Watson out tremendously. He kept it simple.
Until late in the game, Watson doesn't need to be taking shots down the field.
While it would be nice, Watson can execute the offense just fine with shorter passes. Ultimately, that's going to allow receivers to make plays, drives to consume more time, and confidence to be found.
Its great to win games, and Watson does deserve lots of credit for the Browns' success.
There are just a couple of factors that, if worked on, could take Cleveland to the next level going forward.

title: Deshaun Watson Says the Browns Have Yet to Play Their Best Football
full_text:
Deshaun Watson has made the late game dramatic moment very familiar in Cleveland this season. Following the Browns' 13-10 comeback win over the Ravens, Watson said the confidence the team has in those scenarios is a product of the work they do all week.
"This is what we practice for ," Watson said. "We practice it all off season. We practice it every week."
Cleveland were still struggling with consistency on the day offensively as Watson admitted. 16 of 26 passes completed for 164 yards, no TDs, no INTs and 29 yards on the ground. When they needed a play late though, Watson found Jerry Jeudy on a 33 yard completion which put them in a great position to win.
Deshaun said he'd been given the advice by Jeudy as to the route. Having spotted the late shift in the defense he went to the in-cut and found Jeudy down the field.
“He did a good job getting his depth and I put it on time,” Watson said. “He caught it, got the extra yards and put us in a position to win.”
Watson says he takes over in those moments, reminding the lads that their opportunity is going to come.
"I take charge and look at every single one of those guys in the eyes and let them know that, hey, opportunity is going to come. Let's finish it. Let's go win."
The QB also gave credit to the Baltimore defense for making the game so tough. Watson said they were constantly mixing up their coverages and pressure schemes which forced Cleveland to make adjustments and get the ball out quicker.
Even with the offense still working through those adjustments Watson feels there's still room for improvement. The Browns improved to 4-2 and moved into first place in the AFC North. Watson noted that you can certainly learn from a close win prior to the next two divisional games.
"We haven't even played our best football," said Watson.
For now the division leading Browns are finding ways to finish games. Watson pointed out that the more you see players encouraging each other through the missed opportunities and the tough stretches, the more belief you start to get. The challenge for Cleveland will be to find a way to bring that 'we'll finish' mentality into the game earlier on.

title: Browns May Have Beaten Ravens, But Deshaun Watson's Struggles Put Team in Difficult Spot
full_text:
The late great John Madden used to say that “winning is the greatest deodorant”, but the AFC North leading Cleveland Browns might be considered an exception.
Even standing at 4-2 and owning the first two tie-breakers over the Ravens courtesy of their Week 6 victory at Huntington Field on Sunday, 13-10 , Deshaun Watson has been stinking it up at the quarterback position.
Against Baltimore, Cleveland had all of 11 passing yards at the halfway mark, at which point Watson had completed just 3 out of 9 pass attempts, and had been sacked three times. At halftime, Baltimore was leading 10-0, and over the course of the following two quarters did everything in their power to end up with the “L”, but that doesn’t erase just how awful Watson was playing up to that point.
In the third quarter, Watson went 5 for 5 for 46 yards before finding a little rhythm late with an 8 for 12 fourth quarter for 94 yards, bringing his final stat line of 16 for 26 for 164 underwhelming but at the same time deceiving yards against the Ravens, while also getting sacked two more times over the final half. His QBR for the game was a miserable 22.8.
The Browns have been winning despite a subpar performance by Watson all season long. Yes, he’s been able to engineer four game winning drives so far , but the fact remains that Cleveland’s offense has barely resembled a professional outfit throughout most of the team’s six games to date.
And while there are several issues on offense that don’t depend on Watson -- like the team’s still struggling ground game -- the quarterback is literally putting the Browns behind the 8-ball. Before today’s game against the Ravens, Watson had been sacked a league-leading 19 times, most of them his responsibility.
Out of those 19 sacks, eight had come on first down, and 13 of them with 10 or more yards to go, including three on third and 10+ to go. Among today’s five sacks, one came on first and 10, another on second and 10, and the other three on third down, including a third and 14 to go.
Another interesting split is that before today’s game, he was completing just 47.2 percent of his throws on third down. Facing Baltimore, he managed to convert three times out of 16 pass attempts on third downs for the game.
Watson entered today’s matchup ranked 26 out of 33 qualified passers in Total QBR, while the Browns are currently third in the league with 31 punts so far, including all five first half drives against the Ravens today.
A win is a win, there’s no denying that, and any Cleveland Brown will appreciate it. But the current trend of winning despite Watson is unsustainable.
To make matters worse, there is no Plan-B ready to go for the Browns.
Cleveland went all in with Watson when the team decided back in preseason that they were sticking with the 31 year-old veteran as the starter after not playing an official game in almost two years. After all that has transpired since second-year passer Shedeur Sanders led the team to three victories over the second half of last season, including the firing of Kevin Stefanski as head coach and the hiring of Todd Monken to replace him, and a quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson that nobody expected -- while leaving fellow second-year passer Dillon Gabriel on the sideline -- only to hand Watson the starting gig, the only way to sit Watson now is to do it in a definitive manner.
The Browns have been overselling Watson so hard throughout the last few months, that Cleveland can’t bench him unless it’s for good, and that won’t happen while the victories, no matter how narrow, keep coming.
On one hand, Watson has at least shown enough resiliency to bring those four wins home. On the other, the Browns don’t seem to have a plan anymore for Sanders -- nor Gabriel, for that matter.
So it’s become Watson or bust for the Browns, and with the team installed in first place of the AFC North, some would say you don’t need to fix something that isn’t broken. However, the team’s offense, especially at the quarterback position, is evidently broken -- just not broken enough for Cleveland to be losing the games that would inch them closer to one of the top quarterback prospects for next year’s draft .
In that sense, winning despite Watson playing so poorly has become Cleveland’s most recent quarterback curse, because if we’re being honest, how long do you expect to continue to win with this caliber of play at the trigger. And if you do continue to win a few more games, are you really entertaining the idea of extending one of the worst contracts in league history, with what Watson has been showing so far?
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Where's the Extension? Browns' Andre Szmyt Deserves One After Game-Winner vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have one of the league's best kickers under contract.
Yet, the 28-year-old, Andre Szmyt, sits on just a one-year, $1.015 million deal.
On Sunday, Oct. 18, Szmyt added to an already impressive resume that he has built up over the last two seasons, smacking through a 37-yard field goal to walk off the Baltimore Ravens at home, 13-10. His game-winner was his second made field goal of the day, with his first being a 48-yard attempt.
Leading him down the field to give the Browns the win was starter Deshaun Watson, who has routinely put Szmyt in positions to help propel the team to a win.
This season, Szmyt has made 12 kicks on 13 attempts, making him one of the more consistent legs in the league.
Now, especially after Sunday, would be the perfect time for the Browns' front office to reward the second-year pro.
Nobody is asking them to give him a four-year deal or break the bank, but extending him for another year would at least give him more comfort. Such a decision would also show loyalty from the organization.
Szmyt walked into Sunday's outing against the Ravens needing just five made field goals to tie the franchise record for the most consecutive field goals made. He had 24; Browns legend Phil Dawson had 29.
He would start off the day making his first kick, an attempt from 48 yards, but would later go on to miss one from the same distance, thus ending his chance at breaking Dawson's record.
Just four kicks back from tying the record at a mark of 25, though, Szmyt showed remarkable consistency. He now sits third in the Browns' all-time rankings in consecutive made field goals.
Routinely, Szmyt has been called upon to make a kick to give the Browns the lead or tie the game.
Across the past two seasons, he has had four game-winning kicks , two of which have been in the last three weeks. He walked off the Pittsburgh Steelers just a few weeks ago during a Thursday Night Football showdown, giving the Browns a 27-24 edge.
The best part, too, is that Szmyt isn't afraid of situations like that. He understands the pressure, but welcomes the opportunity.
"No, it doesn't; it's exciting," he said following Sunday's game-winner. "It's a love-hate feeling when you go out there for it. It's obviously a lot of pressure, but that's what we train for; that's what we prepare for.  You want to be in those situations, walking it off."
Caught up with Andre Szmyt in the locker room after hitting the game-winning, walk-off field goal in the #Browns 13-10 victory over the Ravens. Asked him if it ever gets old. I'm sure you can guess the answer. "No, it doesn't; it's exciting. It's a love-hate feeling when you go… pic.twitter.com/E5vY6Ne6Zh
And while Szmyt being as good as he is justifies a contract extension on its own, the fact that the Browns have struggled to find a consistent leg over the last few seasons does as well.
Since Dawson left the team way back before the 2013 season, the team has shuffled through kickers left and right. Back in the 2022 NFL Draft, the front office even tried to land the future at the position with a fourth-round pick. Ultimately, it didn't end up working out.
Finally, it seems like they have a long-term option.
Why risk the chance of him leaving in the offseason?
While the Browns have been cheap in recent years, mainly due to the contractual obligation following the trade for Watson, it feels hard to imagine the front office will ignore just how impactful Szmyt has been over the course of the last two seasons.
Returning to the gridiron on Sunday, Oct. 25, the Browns and Szmyt will look to continue chasing the top spot in the AFC North as they take on the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville.
The two sides will collide at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Deshaun Watson Extends League-Leading Statistic As Andre Szmyt Comes Up Clutch Again
full_text:
It wasn't a pretty day... not by any means.
But yet again, somehow, someway the Cleveland Browns have won another football game.
"Our guys are a scrappy group," said head coach Todd Monken.
On Sunday, Oct. 18, the Browns took down the Baltimore Ravens at home in a Week 6 in-division clash , 13-10. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, who began the season strong before falling off in the last few weeks, struggled mightily throughout the contest.
He finished with just 164 passing yards on 26 attempts, completing 16, but led the team to a game-winning drive that saw a 33-yard connection to wideout Jerry Jeudy.
He now leads the league in game-winning drives with four.
The game was then capped off by Browns kicker Andre Szmyt knocking through a 37-yard field goal to push the Browns to 4-2 on the season.
"It's been the last five weeks. It's been an unbelievable credit to our team," Monken said. "Especially our defense, early on, you know, after 10 points, shutting them out...it gives us a chance to win...
"Just the way our guys work and the way they believe, there's just something about this group that makes them special... We have a lot to work on and we'll go back to work tomorrow...But that was pretty cool."
Szymt had his initial attempt to win the game blocked, but Ravens defensive back Keyon Martin was ruled offsides.
For the Browns, it was a big sigh of relief.
Earlier in the contest, Szmyt, one of the league's most consistent kickers, had missed wide left on a 48-yard attempt that would have put the team up 13-10. Fortunately, he got his redemption.
Now, on the campaign, the 28-year-old is 12-for-13 on field goals while also making eight of his nine tries on PATs.
It is obviously a great sign to see Cleveland establish a consistent and reliable leg, but such circumstances show just how rough the offense has been this season. Both the passing and rushing attack have been incredibly inconsistent, which has led to the Browns having to rely on Szmyt far too often.
As a team, the Browns finished with a combined 237 yards of offense, 144 of which came from the passing game. The other 93 came from the rushing attack, with Jaleel McLaughlin leading the charge, taking nine carries for 41 yards.
With injuries and inconsistencies smacking the Browns left, right and center, players like McLaughlin are going to have to continue stepping up to try and light a spark for the offense, even if you'd rather see your $230 million quarterback do it.
He has simply not lived up to expectations over the last two weeks, throwing for a combined 319 yards and one score. He has also completed just 52.5% of his tries.
The Browns can scrape and claw to wins all they want in the early parts of the season, but when the playoff-deciding games start to arrive in a few weeks, teams are going to be at their best. And if the Browns want any chance of playing competitive football beyond the regular season, the offense is going to need to be better , Watson included.
“We just got to flatten out some of the other ups and downs that we have … It’s a we thing, not an individual thing," Monken said Sunday.
Returning to the field on Sunday, Oct. 25, the Browns will have a chance to reestablish the offense in an outing against the 1-5 Tennessee Titans.
The two sides will play at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville.

title: How the Browns' Week 6 Injury Report Will Make or Break Matchup with Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to host the Baltimore Ravens in week six of the 2026 NFL season.
For the Browns, they have had some key players go down with injury. Let's look at the full report and break down how each injury will affect the team.
For the first time this season, the Browns will have to play without their starting running back Quinshon Judkins .
Judkins finished the game last week against the New York Jets, but ultimately is out with an ankle injury.
So far this season, Cleveland has already struggled to find offensive production through the running game. Now, they will have to try to run the ball without their starter against a top-10 run defense in the NFL.
The good news for Browns fans is that Judkins did practice on Friday, but he ultimately still needs more time before he gets back on the field.
Along with Judkins, Schwesinger finished last Sunday's game against the Jets but is also dealing with an ankle injury.
Despite only getting one limited practice in on Friday, Schwesinger is going to suit up against Baltimore.
For the Browns, it is huge to have their defensive anchor out there on the field, but they do need to be careful. With such limited reps, you can't risk worsening the injury and putting even more of the season at risk.
Mason Graham has been out since week four, when he injured his knee and ankle against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
While limited, the good news for Cleveland is that Graham was able to practice on Friday.
It still may be another game or two, but the team's sack leader is slowly getting back out there on the field.
For the Browns, they have done a great job on the field of still getting pressure and sacks without their top guy. Maliek Collins deserves some major flowers after his great performance a week ago.
Browns - Ravens Friday injury report https://t.co/fGHYpgS4vj pic.twitter.com/aa3ndpPXW4
For the Browns, they continue to go without their other running back, Dylan Sampson.
Sampson was placed on IR after week one with a knee injury, but was back at practice this week with limited reps on Thursday and Friday.
One big injury, or really the lack thereof, that most people are overlooking is the fact that KC Concepcion won't miss this game.
Last week, Concepcion took a controversial hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick to the head and was instantly ruled out of the game. While many thought the 2026 first-round pick would miss extended time, he is good to go in the very next week.

While this is a focus on Browns' injuries this week, the Ravens have the biggest loss with Lamar Jackson being ruled out once again.
While it is by no means a free win against Tyler Huntley, the Browns must take advantage of one of the NFL's best being out.
A win here is incredibly important, especially since this is a divisional battle.

title: Browns Still Without Mason Graham, Make Moves To Fill Void Ahead of Sunday
full_text:
For a second straight week, the Cleveland Browns will be without standout second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham.
On Saturday, Oct. 17, the Browns announced that Graham, due to a lower-body injury, was questionable for Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens . The 23-year-old suffered his injury in the Browns' Thursday Night Football showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers just a few weeks ago.
Along with Graham's absence, the Browns will be without defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Kalia Davis.
Each has been slowly but surely recovering, but to be safe, the front office has made a few moves to fill their voids.
In the wake of Graham's "questionable" diagnosis and Hall Jr. and Davis being ruled out, the front office has elevated defensive tackles Chris Williams and Sam Kamara to the active roster.
This isn't the first time the Browns have had to use either, though.
Kamara waltzed out in front of a packed MetLife Stadium last weekend, recording three tackles and the first sack of his NFL career. Williams, on the other hand, didn't get in the stat sheet, but will continue to help the Browns' depth at the position.
While both weren't able to do enough to guide the Browns to a victory over the Jets last weekend, they did receive praise from head coach Todd Monken.
The first-year leader shared that they both provided the team with valuable time on the field.
“Those guys that got elevated really gave us some valuable minutes,” Monken said following the 27-20 loss.
The defensive line is now expected to see the likes of Williams, Kamara, Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington. On the outside, Jared Verse, Sam Williams and Isaiah McGuire will eat up a majority of the snaps.
The line is certainly banged up , more than it has been in quite a while in Cleveland, but that shouldn't stop the young, hungry group that is available from putting together a strong showing against the Ravens.
It is never good to see a player injured, especially one as talented as Lamar Jackson, but with the Browns' recent injury spell, being able to face a Ravens squad that will not have him available is a big break.
Jackson is recovering from an ankle injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans back in Week 4. Since then, he hasn't practiced.
In his place, the Ravens will turn to Tyler Huntley to be the man under center, someone Cleveland is relatively familiar with. While he doesn't have the speed that Jackson does, he is pretty mobile, and the Browns' defensive line will have to be ready to track him down if he starts to roll towards the hashes.
With how Kamara stepped up last week, and the opportunity available in front of Williams, there should be little concern for how the Browns will look defensively.
As long as the rest of the squad does its job, they should be good to go.
The Browns and Ravens will clash from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Cowboys and Dolphins Considered Possible Trade Partners Amid Dallas' Defensive Woes
full_text:
If there is one certainty with the Dallas Cowboys this season, it's that their defense stinks.
Through six games, the Cowboys sport one of the worst units in the NFL. Dallas ranks 23rd against the pass, 32nd against the run, and the team is giving up the eighth-most points per game.
Dallas has problems at every level of the defense, but one of the most glaring issues is the pass-rush , which has mustered up just eight sacks, three of which came in Week 6.
And, of those eight sacks, only 2.5 of them have come from the team's edge rushers, so it goes without saying the Cowboys should be looking to add there before the trade deadline.
In an article identifying 15 players who could get moved before the trade deadline on Nov. 10, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame listed Miami Dolphins defensive lineman Zach Sieler among them.
Verderame also mentioned the Cowboys as a potential fit for the veteran lineman.
"Sieler is an interesting trade chip. On one hand, he’s already 31 and he’s signed through 2029 with base salaries of $12.6 million, $15.4 million and $16.2 million, respectively. In short, he’s not cheap to acquire," Verderame wrote.
"Conversely, none of that money is guaranteed, and he could be traded for and then released for no dead cap charge if things don’t work out. For Miami, it makes sense to move on, but what’s the right price point? Since 2023, Sieler has 27.5 sacks."
"Potential fits: Lions, Cowboys," Verderame added.
Sieler has proven to be an effective pass-rusher during his career. He has 27.5 sacks dating back to 2023, and in that span he has tallied 10 sacks twice.
He has two sacks this season, which would be tied for the most on the team, and he had 5.5 in 2025.
The problem, however, is the 6-foot-6, 300-pound veteran is an interior lineman. Granted, he has lined up as an edge rusher, but that's in a 4-3 defense and the Cowboys run a 3-4 , which means they need an outside linebacker, something Sieler is not.
Now, if the Cowboys were to completely strike out at the deadline on traditional outside linebackers and it's between someone like Sieler and nobody, Dallas might spring for a trade for him, but Miami would have to eat a ton of money for the Cowboys to consider it.
Sieler would amount to an upgrade over Otito Ogbonnia when it comes to pass-rush ability, and he has historically been a strong run defender, although he has struggled mightily in that area this season, as evidenced by his Pro Football Focus grade of 31.6.
An interior trio of Sieler, Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams would be quite formidable and no doubt one of the best in the NFL, and that trio might be able to offer the much-needed boost in the pass-rush the Cowboys need.
All that said, we find it very hard to believe Sieler will ever end up in Dallas, barring a catastrophic injury to Williams or Clark.

title: Cowboys Week 6 Stock Report: Joey Porter Jr. Leads 3 Rising, Caleb Downs Among 6 Falling
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys enter Week 7 of the 2026 campaign in a rut after yet another loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday that pushes Dallas to a 2-4 record.
If there's one positive we can point to for the Cowboys amid their putrid season, it's the NFC East, which has been a total disaster .
The Giants are the only team in the division with a winning record, and to show you how awful the NFC East has been, it became the first division in NFL history to see each team fail to win a single game in back-to-back weeks, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .
But it's even hard to get excited about that. Even if the Cowboys find a way to win the division, this team isn't going to do anything in the playoffs, so it would just be delaying the inevitable, which is another disappointing finish to a season.
But let's justt focus on the now for now. Here's the biggest risers and fallers in our Week 6 stock report.
It unfortunately came in a loss, but Williams had his best game of the season in Week 6.
Williams recorded his second sack and had five pressures in total, the second-most on the team, and he had a pair of run stops and tackles for loss.
When it was all said and done, Williams' 86.2 defensive grade,  according to Pro Football Focus , was the highest on the team.
This is what the Cowboys thought they were getting when they traded for Williams, and then signed him to an extension . Now, Williams has to stack good games.
Prescott has seen better days than the one he had against the Packers on Sunday.
Prescott completed 34-of-54 passes for 258 yards and one score to two interceptions, although one of those picks was the result of CeeDee Lamb simply falling down in the middle of this route.
Even still, Prescott was not sharp and he didn't appear to pick up the blitz all that well. We will say, however, that head coach Brian Schottenheimer's play-calling is not helping at all.
One of the biggest changes on Sunday was Spann-Ford getting the start over Jake Ferguson. However, Ferguson still ended up out-snapping Spann-Ford, 42-36.
That said, Spann-Ford still played the highest percentage of snaps he has seen this season, and he recorded better offensive numbers than Ferguson with four catches for 35 yards.
Ferguson took a back seat to Spann-Ford in terms of getting the start, and rightly so because he has been bad this season, both in the passing game and as a blocker. But, as we said, he was still on the field for a higher percentage of plays than his fellow tight end.
Ferguson didn't do much with his snaps, with the veteran tight end recording just two catches for 13 yards on three targets. Ferguson is fortunate the Cowboys don't have another viable tight end on the roster or else his playing time might dwindle.
With a post-June 1 out in Ferguson's contract in 2027, he could be on the chopping block after this season if he doesn't get his act together.
Porter played a season-high 36 snaps and, according to PFF, he was targeted four times but did not allow a reception. Porter had three tackles, including one for loss, and two passes defensed.
While he hasn't had a full workload yet, Porter is already making a big impact. One thing to watch is his ankle, which Schottenheimer said limited Porter to 36 snaps on Sunday. With how awful this defense has been, the Cowboys need more.
Downs moved back into the slot for the majority of his snaps on Sunday after playing more safety in recent weeks because of injuries.
His return did not pan out well, as the Packers picked on him all game long, and had success doing so. Downs allowed seven receptions on all seven targets thrown his way for 76 yards.
We definitely aren't panicking about the first-round pick, but his struggles are certainly worth noting.
After starting over the first five games, Ezeiruaku took a back seat to Malachi Lawrence, with the rookie starting over him . Ezeiruaku also played a season-low 54.7% of snaps.
The good news for Ezeiruaku is, Lawrence didn't do anything with his increased role other than recording a pass break-up. Even still, Ezeiruaku didn't earn his way out of the dog house after posting just one tackle.
The second-year edge rusher hasn't had a sack or QB hit since Week 1 in what has been a disastrous sophomore campaign so far.
We don't need to rehash what Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker are doing wrong because it's the same stuff every week. We're over both and if the Cowboys decided to fire them, we wouldn't bat an eye.
Sadly, there is no change like that coming after Stephen Jones once again expressed confidence in both. Where that confidence comes from is anyone's guess, but what we do know is we won't hold our breath for Parker or Schottenheimer to lose their jobs.

title: Cowboys Get Unexpected Lifeline From Historically Bad NFC East
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are bad this season , but their division is even worse .
Once seen as a prominent division in the NFL, the NFC East is suddenly in the midst of a terrible stretch of futility. All four teams have gone at least two weeks now without a win, something that hasn’t happened since the 1970 merger .
The NFC East is the first division since the 1970 merger to go winless in back-to-back weeks with every team playing. pic.twitter.com/G2ZBiRoblG
As bad as that sounds, it’s even worse when you realize two of these teams played one another in Week 5, and still no one won. Instead, the Washington Commanders and New York Giants played to a shocking tie.
With every team struggling, the Cowboys have been given an unexpected lifeline and a shot to salvage their season. With the stage set, let’s check out the current standings and how each team looks entering Week 7.
We need to give Dan Quinn some credit because his Commanders defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. That remains their only win, but they did fight back from a 23-3 deficit against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night to make it a 23-17 ending.
Still, they have just one win and are 0-2-1 in the division. Right now, Quinn has one of the hottest seats in the NFL.
At 2-4, the Cowboys should feel hopeless. That’s not the case, however, since they’re tied for second place with the Eagles. They’re on the wrong side of the tiebreaker but that could change if they find a way to defeat the Eagles , who are without Jalen Hurts, on Monday Night Football.
Dallas did show some signs of life against the Packers on defense, which is encouraging. Dee Winters had an interception, Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark each had a sack, and Joey Porter Jr. was lights out. If they can build on that and get the offense back on track, they could make a run.
Philadelphia has lost four in a row and will likely be without Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season due to blood clots in his lungs. It’s a scary situation for Hurts and his health is the top priority. That said, the season is going in the wrong direction and the Cowboys have a chance to kick them while they’re down this week.
John Harbaugh and the Giants shocked Dallas in Week 1, but since that win, they’ve only defeated the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans. They lost to the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints while tying the Commanders.
Losing quarterback Jaxson Dart has been devastating for the Giants, and they’re in line for a tough game in Week 7 against the suddenly surging Houston Texans. They’re in first place now, but that might not be the case for long.

title: Dallas Cowboys 3 Biggest Concerns Entering Week 7 Showdown Against Eagles
full_text:
Another week brought us another embarrasing loss for the Dallas Cowboys.
In Week 6, it was the Green Bay Packers who defeated the Cowboys, handing them a 23-13 loss on Sunday Night Football . That score is misleading since a late touchdown from the Cowboys made it seem closer than it actually was.
In reality, the Cowboys were outplayed from the opening drive and enter a Week 7 showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football with several concerns to address. Here we look at three of the more pressing issues that need attention.
Last year, Javonte Williams ran for 1,201 yards and averaged 4.8 yards per attempt. Through six games in 2026, he has just 317 yards while averaging 3.7 yards per carry and is still looking for his first 100-yard outing of the season.
Dallas was supposed to have an explosive offense with a running game capable of carrying the load. As they prepare for Monday Night Football in Week 7, that rushing attack has been non-existent making this one of the primary concerns against the Eagles. If they can get Williams going, everything will become easier on offense. If not, Dak Prescott might be asked to throw it 50-plus times again, which isn't typically a recipe for success.
Dak Prescott has feasted historically when blitzed. He's been phenomonal at identifying where the rush is coming from and finding the open player. Over the past two weeks, that hasn't been the case.
Prescott has put together his two worst performances of the season as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers made life difficult on him with their pressure. In Week 5, Tampa Bay blitzed on 43% of of the plays and as Jon Ledyard writes, that led to a major drop in Expected Points Per Play .
"On non-blitzed dropbacks, Prescott had a +0.09 EPA/play, a number that fell to -0.31 EPA/play on blitzed dropbacks. That means the Cowboys were losing about a third of a point on every Bowles blitz," Ledyard wrote.
Green Bay blitzed 35.71% of the time and Prescott again struggled as he finished with two interceptions and just one touchdown in each game. Following those two games, Cowboys insider Bryan Broaddus expressed concern about Prescott's current struggles with the blitz.
What's going on with Dak Prescott against the blitz? @BryanBroaddus : "The quarterback hasn't been very good (against the blitz). He got fooled tonight. This is the second week in a row (he's struggled against it)." pic.twitter.com/SpNFzmJy5N
In Week 7, the Cowboys will face a Philly team that doesn't blitz often under Vic Fangio . That said, he's an experienced defensive coordinator who will switch things up if needed. Expect Fangio to use more blitzes than typical as he tests whether Dak has fixed the issue. If he hasn't, it could be disastrous for this offense.
At this point, there's no phase of the defense that Dallas should have faith in. They're struggling in coverage, struggling against the run, and absolutely abysmal on third downs. On Sunday, the Packers were 11-of-18 and are now surrendering a first down 54.67 percent of the time on third downs.
Those conversions are one of many reasons the Cowboys have given up at least 20 points in 13 consecutive games. That's the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest in franchise history.
Dallas still has a chance in the NFC East since the division is a mess as a whole, but they have to start winning to take advantage. That begins with the defense figuring out how to play at a higher level.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Explains Why Dallas Cowboys' Offense Lacks Creativity
full_text:
Six weeks into the 2026-27 NFL season, the Dallas Cowboys still have not figured things out . In fact, it has gotten worse.
We knew that there would be growing pains for the Cowboys after an offseason full of rebuilding the roster and revamping the defense , while bringing in a new coaching staff, but then everything went completely off the rails.
Injuries started to pile up, and there was no cohesiveness, so we were back to watching a completely disjointed defense trying to figure out a game plan. Unfortunately, the defense isn't the only problem. Dallas' offense has also regressed, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer seems completely over his head .
The Cowboys' offense has become predictable and stagnant. The team can't figure out how to get anything going against the blitz because it is one-note. Schottenheimer was recently asked why the Cowboys' offense has fallen off over the past few weeks , and he turned the blame back to the defense.
DAL's motion/motion at the snap rates the last two seasons. Why the change? https://t.co/wNCJLWEkL6 pic.twitter.com/ad3rawYAbW
Dallas' motion rate has completely fallen off, which is part of why George Pickens' stat line has taken a dip, but Schottenheimer explained that's because the offense is always playing from behind.
Once again, it's a lack of accountability , which is an increasing issue when evaluating Schottenheimer as a head coach.
"You're trying to go fast. You're trying to keep the defense on their heels . You're trying to extend the game for as long as you can and get as many ops as possible, because you don't know what's going to happen," Schottenheimer said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . "So that's the No. 1 thing. When you shift in motion, obviously the play clock and the game clock go down, and so that limits your ops.
"That's a big reason why, when you see teams go no-huddle, usually receivers don't change sides. Usually you're moving one guy, maybe the back, and one guy, and you're trying to do that to stay ahead of the clock."
Schottenheimer does have a point. When you're playing from behind, it dictates how you have to play in order to stay in the mix. Playing catch-up is not where anyone wants to be, and unfortunately, Dallas' defense is doing the team no favors.
Ultimately, the entire team needs to step up, because no one has been getting the job done. And if the coaching staff doesn't figure things out quickly, there could be some major changes at the end of the month ahead of the NFL trade deadline. For Schottenheimer, whose seat is getting increasingly hotter, that could be some bad news.

title: Cowboys Offer Encouraging DeMarvion Overshown Injury Update
full_text:
Injuries have been a problem for the Dallas Cowboys on defense this season and they saw another key player go down on Sunday. Dee Winters, who recorded an interception in the first half against the Green Bay Packers, suffered an Achilles sprain and is expected to miss time.
Winters had his best game of the season, earning a 90.9 overall grade from PFF , making the timing of his loss even more unfortunate. If there is any good news, though, it's the update Stephen Jones and Brian Schottenheimer gave on fellow linebacker DeMarvion Overshown.
The former third-round pick out of Texas has been dealing with a hamstring injury suffered in Week 1, but is nearing a return. Jones said they have been cautious with Overshown's injury, but added that he could be back against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7.
“It’s just wanting to make sure. Those hamstrings can be tricky. Sometimes they take longer than you hope," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan according to Joseph Hoyt . “Unfortunately it’s not quite there yet, but we think he has a great chance to play this week.”
Brian Schottenheimer also spoke on Overshown's status while meeting with reporters on Monday. He said that they "expect" Overshown to be back on the field on Monday Night Football.
#Cowboys Brian Schottenheimer says they “hope” and “expect” DeMarvion Overshown to be back this week for MNF vs the Philadelphia Eagles.
Overshown had seven tackles in the season opener before suffering his hamstring injury. He's struggled to stay on the field throughout his career, but was a difference-maker in 2024 when he was able to play in 13 games. That year, Overshown had 90 tackles, eight tackles for loss, five sacks, and one interception. Right now, their defense is desperate for game-changers and Overshown has the chance to prove a much-needed spark.
Philadelphia is also navigating through several injuries. They were without two of their biggest stars on Sunday, with running back Saquon Barkley out with a hamstring injury and Jalen Hurts missing the game with blood clots in his lung .
There's a chance Barkley could play against the Cowboys, but Eagles expect Hurts to miss the remainder of the season. That means Tanner McKee will make his second start while former Cowboys Joe Milton III will be the QB2. Like Dallas, the Eagles enter this one 2-4 and somehow both are still in the mix for the NFC East title.

title: Brian Schottenheimer's Frustration Boils Over After Cowboys Loss to Packers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered yet another embarrasing loss , this time to the Green Bay Packers during Sunday Night Football. Following the loss, fans are beginning to vent their frustrations with the organization, with many fingers being pointed at head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
Fans aren't the only ones who are angry, however. At least not according to Schottenheimer. While speaking with reporters on Monday, the second-year head coach said that he and the players were "pissed off" and ready to win.
"I'm pissed off. (The players) are pissed off too. We're ready for a win," Schottenheimer said via Jon Machota.
Schottenheimer's comments are somewhat concerning, if we are being honest. This is a team that has struggled to keep its emotions in check and he's starting to let his anger seep through. His "ready for a win" comment also comes off as somewhat desperate, which is the last emotion a team needs to be feeling.
Then again, this fits with the way things have been going in Dallas the past two years. Super Bowl winner Teddy Bruschi said they are the most "reactive" team in the NFL , claiming they don't ever find problems before they arise. While good teams are proactive, according to Bruschi, the Cowboys wait for the sky to fall, then let their emotions dictate how they respond.
Despite the outside criticism, the Cowboys remain confident in Schottenheimer. On Monday, Stephen Jones backed the head coach, saying the front office likes the players as well as the coaching staff. Cowboys On SI's Mike Moraitis called these comments delusional , and for good reason.
As for Schottenheimer, he wasn't ready to dive into the comments from Jones. Instead, he said the focus is solely on turning things around.
"I'm focusing on the process of turning this around for myself and the players. Certainly not good enough. We're disappointed with where we're at," Schottenheimer said. "We know we need to play better. We know we can play better. I think we have the right guys to do that."
It's fair to say Dallas has the right players to contend, especially on offense. There's more than enough firepower to outscore anyone and they have the pieces to be an average NFL defense, which is all they need to contend. Through six games, they've fallen short on both sides and that's 100 percent on the coaches, beginning with Schottenheimer.
So while he can be as pissed as he wants, that anger needs to be directed at himself before anyone else.

title: Dee Winters Injury Update is Bad News for Dallas Cowboys Defense
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are coming off another embarrassing loss, as they fell to the Green Bay Packers in a 23-13 finish at Lambeau Field on Sunday night.
But to make matters worse, the Cowboys lost starting linebacker Dee Winters to an injury during the game.
Winters has an Achiles strain, an injury that will force him to "likely miss" Week 7's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, per Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
The injury timing is unfortunate for multiple reasons.
Winters is coming off a game against Green Bay where he had his first interception of the season, one that he appeared to return for a touchdown before replay went back and ruled him down.
But on top of that, the Cowboys are still without linebacker DeMarvion Overshown due to a hamstring injury. Fortunately, there's a chance he makes his return from a five-game absence in Week 7 against the Philadelphia Eagles, but hamstrings can be tough to fully bounce back from, especially for a player with an injury history like Overshown's.
The Cowboys defense is already dreadful as is, so they can't afford to have a starter like Winters miss extended time. Hopefully the team gets him back sooner rather than later.
So far this season, Winters has started all six games while posting 35 total tackles (23 solo), one fumble recovery and one interception.
With Winters out, fans should expect rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham take on an even bigger role than he already had, but this will also impact the depth behind him.
Schottenheimer praised Shemar James and Justin Barron while speaking with the media on Monday. Both players could take on larger roles with Winters set to miss time.
"We're getting a lot of guys reps. Shemar James, like I said, is doing a really good job," Schottenheimer said. "Justin Barron last night did a really good job. We put him in on a couple passing situations. They actually tried him on a little wheel route immediately when he came in the game and he played it beautifully. That's a position that normally gets dinged up and beat up a little bit, and both those guys Shemar and Justin have played really well for us."
The Cowboys and Eagles will kick off from Lincoln Financial Field on Monday Night Football in Week 7 at 7:15 p.m. CT/

title: Cowboys First-Round Bust Gets Shot With Packers Day After Dallas' Ugly Loss
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys flew out of Green Bay after an embarrassing loss to the Packers on Sunday Night Football , but one former member of the team is just arriving.
On Monday afternoon, former first-round pick Mazi Smith visited with the Packers as he continues to attempt to revive his career. Smith was recently released by the Miami Dolphins after spending the first few months of the season on the team's practice squad.
Smith was the Cowboys' No. 26 overall pick in the 2023 draft, but he lasted just two and a half seasons with the team and never found his groove. He was ultimately sent to the New York Jets as a throwaway piece in the Quinnen Williams trade .
Now, he will be getting another opportunity to revive his career with the franchise that just embarrassed the team that gave up on him before his rookie contract ended.
ESPN NFL insider Rob Demovsky was first to report that Smith tried out for the Packers . Before his release from Miami, Smith had appeared in just one game for the Dolphins.
Not only did Smith try out for the team, but Demovsky noted that the " Packers are planning to sign him to the practice squad ." So while Smith still has to earn his spot on a 53-man roster, he is getting another chance.
Despite being on his fourth team in four years, Smith is still only 25 years old.
Smith may not have worked out with the Cowboys, but no one has over the past few years. As a result, the Cowboys' defense has been putrid against the run and they have never found their groove.
Three defensive coordinators later, nothing has changed, so Smith may have never actually been the problem. Through six weeks this season, the Cowboys are ranked No. 30 overall in total defense and dead last in run defense, so things are just as grim as they were during life with Mazi.
Total Defense : The Cowboys rank No. 30 in total defense following Sunday's loss to the Packers. , allowing 382.5 yards per game and 18 touchdowns. The only teams to allow more yards per game are the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions.
Pass Defense : Dallas ranks No. 23 in pass defense, allowing 232.7 passing yards per game and 11 touchdowns through the air.
Run Defense : The Cowboys' run defense has been dreadful, ranking dead last in the league. Dallas has allowed 149.8 rushing yards per game, 10 yards more than anyone else in the league, and seven touchdowns on the ground.

title: Broncos Stock Report: 4 Risers, 4 Fallers Entering Week 7
full_text:
The Denver Broncos weathered the storm of their first six-game stretch, getting out to a 4-2 start, which is about as good as anyone could have expected.
The Broncos' overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks afforded them a three-day "mini-bye," a needed breather to rest up before preparing for the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. The last few weeks have seen several players rise in relief of injured players, especially on defense.
Coming out of this mini-bye, let's break down the Broncos' biggest risers and fallers.
Barron has helped keep the Broncos' passing defense afloat while Patrick Surtain II has missed the past two-plus games. While he's given up completions, Barron has been physical and sticky in coverage, competing hard at the catch point.
Throw in his reliability as a tackler this season — which is huge, given that Denver co-leads the NFL in missed tackles — and it's safe to say the Broncos have a real player on their hands. All that summertime "bust" talk should be thrown completely out the window.
This former first-rounder has been playing up to his draft pedigree.
Like Barron, Abrams-Draine has been relied upon to help cover for the absence of Riley Moss. Although Moss dressed and even played 20 snaps last week, Abrams-Draine saw the lion's share of the snaps, tasked with covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.
Abrams-Draine's fourth-quarter interception against Seattle was huge, and it illustrated the confidence this kid is playing with as a cover corner. I'd like to see his tackling improve drastically, but he's never been the most physical defensive back.
The NFL's biggest talking point over the past four days has been Nix's slump and whether the Broncos should bench him. However, at 4-2, head coach Sean Payton made it clear on Monday that Nix's job as the starter is still secure.
That doesn't mean the Broncos are blind to Nix's struggles, though. The buzz out of Broncos HQ is that Nix is still quite bothered and affected by his ankle, which he fractured in the playoffs last season.
The Broncos say the ankle is healed, so it sounds like Nix is still struggling with the mental recovery. But now that the worst of the initial schedule is behind them, the third-year quarterback could be poised to get back on the horse, and give fans more than a glimpse of the dynamic player he was before his January injury.
Robinson is on a roll, and the Broncos are going to need him to stay on it. He co-led the team last week against Seattle with six QB pressures, notching his second sack of the season.
With Jonathon Cooper returning and Jonah Elliss dealing with what could be a severe leg injury , Robinson's role should be unchanged moving forward. Robinson has been one of the Broncos' best surprise players of 2026.
Dobbins looks indecisive and lacks burst. The Broncos have fed him over the past several weeks, but it hasn't led to much production.
Dobbins did score his first and second touchdowns of the season over the past two weeks, but he's otherwise been ineffective overall as a between-the-tackles runner. He seems to believe that the schedule had a lot to do with his lack of success early on, and if that's true, we should see him take some measurable steps forward.
Sutton is in line for a career-worst season. Granted, much of that has to do with Nix's slump and the Broncos' disjointed passing offense, but Sutton isn't blameless.
The veteran wideout isn't fighting for the ball at the catch point as we're used to seeing, and he's struggling to create separation as a route-runner, leading some to wonder whether Father Time has caught up to the ninth-year pro. Sutton needs to step it up.
Although he's still on the practice squad, Rapp came in handy last week against the Seahawks with Talanoa Hufanga sidelined with an injury. Rapp played 65 of the 85 total defensive snaps last week, and he was very good for the Broncos, helping to limit JSN and Kupp.
Rapp totaled six tackles and seemed perfectly comfortable and natural playing next to Jones. The Broncos have found their No. 3 safety, it would seem, but when Hufanga comes back, they're going to have to promote Rapp to the 53-man roster eventually, which will mean parting ways with JL Skinner or Tycen Anderson, in all likelihood.
I get it. Wide receiver is a quarterback-dependent position, but Waddle's impact could already be much greater than it's been.
He's dropped to many passes and I don't like the body language I'm starting to see from him. Right now, the Broncos need to fall in line and close ranks around the beleaguered Nix, and for guys like Waddle, when his number is called, he has to answer the bell.
Look for Payton to start opening up this offense moving forward. That should benefit Waddle.
