title: Broncos Have Several 2027 Restricted Free Agents—Only One Is a No-Brainer
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 4-2 , with several players set to be unrestricted free agents in 2027. We've updated the outlook for each of those players six games into the season, and now it's time to examine the Broncos' 2027 restricted free agents.
Restricted free agents are eligible for a first-, second-, or original-round tender, which represents the draft-pick compensation the Broncos would receive if an outside team signed the player to an offer sheet. If it's an original-round tender and the player was undrafted, the team that loses the RFA doesn't get a draft pick as compensation.
The Broncos have five players set to become restricted free agents in 2027. We'll look at what the future likely holds for each after six games of the 2026 season, along with an early prediction.
Tillman has excelled as a depth and rotational player on the Denver defense. He has 28 pressures and nine sacks in his career, with four pressures in five games this season.
This will be an easy decision for the Broncos. Tillman needs to get a second-round tender so the Broncos can keep him for another year. The estimated $6.261 million salary is worth it.
Verdict : Second-round tender.
Jackson hasn't seen a lot of playing time the past couple of seasons. The Broncos mainly kept him for depth purposes, but other players have surpassed him on the depth chart.
Jackson won't be tendered, but there's a small chance that the Broncos will re-sign him to a one-year deal. However, that depends on how much the Broncos like players such as Sai'vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim.
Verdict : No tender, might not re-sign.
Key excels at special teams ( first-team All-Pro last year ), and he's shown he can do some good things on defense. He played a significant number of defensive snaps against the Seattle Seahawks because Talanoa Hufanga was out with an ankle injury, though Taylor Rapp received more.
There's a chance the Broncos will give the second-round tender to Key, even if they re-sign Brandon Jones. Another option is a two-year deal, like what the Broncos gave to offensive guard Alex Palczewski this past offseason.
Verdict : Second-round tender or re-sign to a short-term deal.
Badie has stuck around on the depth chart because of what he brings to special teams. He's shown he can be a productive back when called into action, but he's not somebody you want to rely on as a top option.
Badie isn't worth tendering. However, the Broncos like what he brings to special teams, so they could re-sign him to a one-year deal at the veteran minimum to compete for a roster spot.
Verdict : No tender, likely to re-sign.
Crum was the swing tackle and sixth offensive lineman last season after Matt Peart's season was cut short because of injury, and Palczewski stepped in at left guard for multiple games.
Crum did some good things last year, but he struggled in the preseason and is currently on injured reserve. He's unlikely to be tendered, but the Broncos might be willing to give him a one-year deal to let him compete for a roster spot.
Verdict : No tender, likely to re-sign.

title: What it Would Take the Broncos to Trade For RB Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
After losing to the winless Tennessee Titans, the Indianapolis Colts fired their 10-year GM, Chris Ballard , on Monday morning.
The Colts are only two games behind the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars, but Indy is a mess right now.
If you're the Denver Broncos, it begs the question: Could Colts Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor be available?
The NFL trade deadline is on November 10 , so the Colts have plenty of time to take some calls and look for the best possible offer for Taylor, if they're of a mind to blow it up. He's only 27, and he's coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns with 1,400-plus rushing yards.
Meanwhile, the Broncos' ground game is still looking for lift-off. The Broncos not only re-signed J.K. Dobbins this past offseason, but the $8 million per year they gave him represented a 4x raise.
Dobbins hasn't been four times better, and he's been far less effective than he was in his 10 games last season. While he's angling for a career-low yards-per-carry average (3.3 YPC), it's important to factor in the caliber of defenses he and the Broncos faced through the first six weeks. The Broncos will be looking for his numbers to climb now that their initial six-week gauntlet is behind them.
That being said, Dobbins has to be better, but so does the Broncos' offensive line — a unit that has also underachieved thus far. It's hard to point to any individual or collective on the Broncos' offense that hasn't failed to meet expectations this season.
That's why Taylor suddenly looks very appealing. However, the financial factors could inhibit a possible trade.
The Colts just signed Taylor to a two-year, $44 million deal in August, and he's on the books this season for a $16.1 million salary-cap hit. In 2027, that number climbs to $21 million and $22.98 million in 2028.
The Broncos have several of their own free agents to worry about after 2026, so any potential trade would have to be balanced against those demands. There's also the reality of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle's cap number ballooning from $4.8 million this season to $27 million in 2027.
Then there's Bo Nix. All the scrutinty around his second contract has gone from a matter-of-course eventuality to a holding pattern amid his slump to start this season, but he's eligible for an extension next spring.
If Nix turns the ship around this season, and the Broncos not only make the playoffs but strike deep again, his financial future will come back into focus. The going rate for a franchise quarterback starts around $40 million per year, and only goes up.
While that's a lot to budget for a quarterback, if conditions led to the Broncos signing Nix to a sizable extension, the bulk of the salary-cap ramifications wouldn't set in until 2029, assuming the team also exercises his fifth-year option.
The Broncos have ways to trim the salary-cap down; saying goodbye to left guard Ben Powers and right tackle Mike McGlinchey after this season would free up enough money to offset the absortion of Taylor's contract, for example, but the team would need viable options ready to start in 2027.
Kage Casey at left guard and Alex Palczewski at right tackle could be those options.
The Colts would likely start the Taylor conversation with an asking price of a second-round pick, plus late-round compensation. A desperate team might pay that, but given the high mileage on Taylor's tires (1,652 career carries) since entering the league in 2020, the Broncos could potentially negotiate it down to a third-round pick, plus maybe a 2028 conditional Day 3 pick.
However, that might be wishful thinking since Taylor is still well under 30. His new contract will expire just as he's about to hit 30, so any team that took him on could feel confident in the next two-plus years of production.
As always, the compensation would also be influenced by supply and demand. If the Colts have a big market for Taylor, it'll only drive the price up, but if the calls are few and far between, that's where the Broncos could potentially slide in with a third-round offer, plus a conditional late-rounder.
People will point to the Christian McCaffrey trade as a potential precedent in 2022. The San Francisco 49ers gave up a king's ransom to the Carolina Panthers for McCaffrey, relinquishing a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick.
At the time, McCaffrey was a year younger than Taylor is now, and he was already a two-time Pro Bowler and All-Pro. Factor in his draft pedigree as a former top-10 pick, and the 49ers' needs, and the Panthers were able to come away with a big return in the trade.
Taylor has way more mileage than McCaffrey had and is older, so I have serious doubts that the Colts could command a similar haul that Carolina did. But it make take as much as a second-rounder to pry Taylor off Indy's hands.
Would Taylor be worth such an investment? That's what the Broncos would have to decide. Given their current circumstance, my answer is yes.
Given how often the Broncos run out of the shotgun, they'd need to tweak their run game a bit to give Taylor the runway he needs to get up to speed. But that wouldn't be the worst thing — getting Nix under center more and building the run game and play-action passing attack around it.
Taylor would be an immediate impact player, though. A three-time Pro Bowler and a one-time first-team All-Pro, he led the NFL in rushing in 2021 and has paced the league in rushing touchdowns twice.
On a struggling team, Taylor has rushed for 492 yards and seven touchdowns already, but he's only averaging 4.0 yards per carry. He's on pace to finish with 1,394 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Do you know the last time the Broncos had a 1,000-yard rusher? Phillip Lindsay in 2019. That was a long time ago. But it sure would be nice for Nix to have rushing reliability behind him in the Broncos' backfield.
Unfortunately, Dobbins and RJ Harvey haven't provided that consistency this season. But the Broncos believe the worst is behind them and that offensive improvements are right around the corner .
Given the Broncos' investment in Dobbins and the imminent return of rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman, I have my doubts about them making a move for Taylor. The financial components and trade compensation would also play a role, and after giving up a first- and third-round draft pick to acquire Waddle, which has yet to pay dividends, the Broncos might be a bit gunshy.
Sean Payton loves Dobbins, but if the Broncos made a move, they could get out of his contract painlessly after this season. Meanwhile, Harvey already has a key role in the offense as a 'joker' weapon in the passing game and as a change-of-pace back.
The Broncos also believe in Coleman, but he's been on injured reserve since Week 2. They might want a longer look at Coleman before making any kind of push for Taylor.
One thing I can say for sure is that Taylor would be an immediate upgrade over Dobbins. We have a few weeks until the NFL trade deadline, so we'll be keeping our ear to the floor for any possible buzz.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Details OLB Jonathon Cooper's Return to Play
full_text:
It was reported following the Denver Broncos' Week 6 win over the Seahawks that starting outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper was being removed from the commissioner's exempt list and could return to play for Sunday's road matchup at Arizona.
On Monday, as the team turned its attention to the Cardinals, head coach Sean Payton praised Cooper for taking the requisite steps with the NFL to see the field in 2026 following his domestic violence-related arrests over the summer.
“He initiated the steps right away himself," Payton told the media via conference call. "I won’t go into detail all the things that he felt were important. I think the league was on the same page, the club. A lot of it becomes a league issue at that point. To his credit, he didn’t back away at all from what he felt like was necessary.”
Cooper had been on the exempt list since Aug. 30, days before Denver's regular-season opener while awaiting a trial, which directly impacts when he can play football again. ESPN's Jeff Legwold reported on Oct. 16 that "he was in Douglas County (Colo.) court last week for a motions hearing and has a March 2-4 trial scheduled in his case, with a pretrial hearing set for Feb. 19."
Legwold also noted that "his time on the exempt list -- the first six weeks of the regular season -- would count toward any league-mandated suspension in the future. If suspended, however, he would have to return the weekly game checks he has received because suspensions from the personal conduct policy are without pay."
Cooper — whose conditions to return this season included meeting with a therapist — attended weight-lifting sessions, participated in meetings, and was generally active inside the Broncos facility during his stint on the exempt list, Payton revealed in August.
“We wait on the league," he said on Aug. 31. "In the meantime, the difference now is he’s in the facility, he’s lifting, he’s in the meetings. He can’t practice, and then we just wait for this process to play out.”
The Broncos were granted a one-week roster exemption for Cooper's impending return to the active roster, from which the club must make a corresponding move, as it's at the 53-man limit. That move is likely to come in short order.
Even on a limited snap count — it'll be his first meaningful action since January, after all — Cooper should slide back into his old starting job opposite Nik Bonitto, especially with OLB Jonah Elliss nursing a leg injury from last Thursday's victory in Seattle.
Cooper, who's amassed 31.5 sacks across his six-year career, also gets a plus matchup against pocket-passing Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Brisett has been sacked 12 times in six games — and was taken down five times in Arizona's Week 5 loss to Detroit.

title: Bench Bo Nix? Broncos HC Sean Payton Gives Definitive Answer
full_text:
Bo Nix has been put through the wringer since the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football .
Throwing for just 107 yards against Seattle — on the heels of back-to-back lackluster performances against the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Chargers — Nix has been under fire in the media and on social media. There have been open calls to bench him — both from the local and national perspective — and no small number of Broncos fans have joined in.
After enjoying the fruits of a three-day mini-bye, Broncos head coach Sean Payton held court via Zoom on Monday morning, and his answer to whether he's considering benching a quarterback who's won 18 of his last 21 starts was as definitive as it gets.
“To answer your question, no," Payton said.
Payton said Nix's performance, far below the standard he set in his first two years, is a "byproduct" of all the little things the Broncos aren't executing on offense. The veteran coach believes that as the Broncos fix these things, Nix will improve as a "byproduct" of that process.
"He’s going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved," Payton said of Nix. "The improved play from our offensive line, the more efficient we are relative to balance, running the football. That’s our jobs as coaches here. We talked after the game about we’re excited to get that win, and yet at the same time find that improvement we need in all areas. So, it starts with all of us.”
Payton says that he hasn't paid attention to the tsunami of Nix criticism in the press of late, but we know the veteran coach gets on X and keeps an eye on social media. He's been a strong defender of Nix publicly, including on social media, so it's hard to believe Payton hasn't seen at least some of the recent shade, but he said that his focus has been elsewhere.
“I try to focus on the next day here," Payton said of the Nix criticism. "We’re trying to focus on getting ready to play Arizona. That’s kind of where our attention is.”
On one hand, it's easy to see that Nix hasn't gotten a lot of help from his supporting cast. On the other, a franchise quarterback is supposed to be the tide that raises all ships, making everyone around him better.
We certainly saw that from Nix in his first two seasons. After going four years without eclipsing the 1,000-yard receiving mark, wide receiver Courtland Sutton crossed that milestone in his first year with Nix, and repeated it last season with the added accolade of a Pro Bowl selection.
The Broncos' offensive line has been widely viewed as one of, if not the, best units in football — at least, going into this season. Nix had a big impact on that perception, too. Only one quarterback has been sacked fewer times than Nix since he entered the league in 2024.
Beyond the individual level, Nix obviously raised the Broncos' ship as a whole. This team went from missing the playoffs for eight straight years to earning a wildcard berth his rookie year.
Nix's Broncos followed that up in 2025 with a 14-win season, an AFC West crown, and the No. 1 playoff seed in the conference. Nix had the Broncos on the doorstep of the Super Bowl — hosting the AFC championship game — when he suffered a broken ankle.
So in every way possible, Nix has already proven to be the tide that raises all the ships around him. That's what has made his Year 3 performance so troubling.
All we can do is speculate on why Nix hasn't looked like himself, and beyond the obvious changes at offensive coordinator and play-caller with Davis Webb, the only explanation that makes any sense is that he's still dealing with the effects of his ankle injury. But both Nix and the Broncos have maintained that he's 100% recovered from the ankle injury, even if the eye test would beg to differ.
Even if Nix's ankle is fully healed, is his psyche? We've wondered about that, but one of the intangible traits that attracted the Broncos to Nix in the 2024 draft was his mental toughness and resilience. Fans can only hope that Nix's mental mettle can help him get through what appears to be a serious obstacle.
“This is a tough league. We hit every aspect, and I think that’s one of the things that attracted us to Bo in the beginning is we had seen his ability to climb through adversity," Payton said. "It’s not just Bo that feels that. Right now, offensively, I feel that, our players feel that and we’ll improve.”
Payton remains adamant that Nix and the Broncos' offense will improve. Payton has taken ownership of the offense in his public remarks and by reclaiming the play-calling duties.
Payton didn't say "we'll try to improve." He said "We'll improve."
Fortunately, the Broncos are through the brutal gauntlet of their first six games, coming out as well as anyone could have hoped at 4-2. The schedule eases up a bit now, with a trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals (who just beat the Los Angeles Rams, by the way).
But that Cardinals road game will be followed by a rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs at Mile High. Then it's a road game against a better-than-expected Carolina Panthers team, followed by the Broncos' Week 10 bye.
I suspect things will be looking much better offensively by Week 11. Payton has changed Webb's verbiage back to his terminology , which certainly hasn't helped Nix from a mental bandwidth perspective, but those kinks are being worked out on the hoof.
Payton is a coach who loves to get the last word. When Jacksonville's Liam Coen beat the Broncos in Denver last year, then talked some smack at the podium, Payton circled Week 2's rematch this season, telling Coen at the NFL owners meetings that he's coming for him . Denver won that game.
After Mike Macdonald's incendiary comments about Payton were caught on a hot mic a few weeks back, you can believe the Broncos' head coach double-circled Week 6. Payton won that game, too.
Payton can't miss all the hate being fired at his quarterback. It's about continuing to win games, sure, but you can trust Payton to double his efforts to get Nix and this offense rolling.
And when that day comes, Payton will stand at the podium and smirk, relishing the ridiculousness of being asked whether he'd consider benching a quarterback with a .700 career winning percentage. Yeah, you can believe Payton looks forward to that day, and it might not be too far off.

title: Broncos' 2027 Free-Agent Progress Report: Who Stays & Who Goes
full_text:
We're six games into the 2026 season , and while there are 11 games left to play, we can notice some trends regarding the long-term future of some of the players on the Denver Broncos' roster.
Multiple Broncos will be either unrestricted or restricted free agents after this season, which means the team will have decisions to make.
Today, we're going to look at the Broncos set to become unrestricted free agents in 2027 and examine what the future may hold for them. We'll determine how these players are trending, whether it's a priority to re-sign them, possibly re-sign them, or allow them to depart.
In future installments, we'll look at the players set to become restricted free agents and players whom the Broncos may have decisions to make about their contracts.
Jones has been a solid contributor as the starting free safety and he's come at a reasonable salary. He's not a top safety, so it's not likely the Broncos will have to break the bank to keep him.
It's not out of the question for Jones to be re-signed but it may not happen before the end of the season. Whether he returns in 2027 will most likely come down to his asking price.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
McMillian has been invaluable as the slot corner and a player who can be utilized in blitzes. He has thrived in Vance Joseph's scheme.
Because slot corners don't command a lot of money, the Broncos could get McMillian re-signed at a reasonable price. The Broncos should try to get a deal done before the end of the season.
Verdict : Priority re-signing.
Moss has continued to play well, with five pass breakups in five games. That puts him on pace to have 17 for the year, not far from the 19 pass breakups he had last season.
While his play warrants Moss sticking around, will the Broncos be able to afford his price point? There's also the presence of Jahdae Barron, who has shown promise since Moss and Pat Surtain II went down with injuries. One can't rule out Moss staying, but there are factors that may mean he moves on after 2026.
Verdict : Likely to depart.
Mims missed a couple of games because of injury. Since his return, he's seen snaps on offense and special teams. However, he hasn't had many explosive plays .
While Mims is a talented player, it's not a given he'll be re-signed at this point. The Broncos might be content to look elsewhere rather than commit money over multiple years.
Verdict : Likely to depart.
Uwazurike has started five games, but has just two pressures. He's shown he can be a good rotational player, but his play hasn't quite been what you expect from a starter.
Sai'Vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim are likely to be in the mix next season for more snaps, and if the Broncos are happy with how they are developing, they will likely let Uwazurike move on.
Verdict : Likely to depart.
Powers enters the final year of the four-year deal that he signed back in 2023. He has a void year for cap purposes, added after he restructured his contract in 2024.
Powers isn't playing as well as he was last season before he got injured. It's not hard to see the Broncos not move on from Powers, especially if they believe Kage Casey and Alex Palczewski can compete for a starting job.
Engram signed a two-year deal in 2025, and the Broncos added a void year for cap purposes. He's had his moments, but it's clear his best years are behind him.
The Broncos will almost certainly allow Engram to leave and look to either free agency or the draft to get another receiving tight end.
The former 2023 sixth-round pick has mostly contributed on special teams, though he has a handful of defensive snaps. It's special teams where Skinner has done his best work.
This is a case of a player the Broncos won't re-sign during the season, but there's a good chance they will get a deal done with him just before free agency or during that period after he's tested the market.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
The former 2023 seventh-round pick has started six games. Forsyth has been solid but appears to be better suited as a depth player than as a starter for multiple games.
Still, you always want quality depth on the offensive line, so it would make sense to keep Forsyth around. As with Skinner, Forsyth won't get re-signed during the season, but the Broncos might do so closer to free agency or after letting him test the market.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
Stidham has shown throughout his career that backup quarterback is his ceiling. He is somebody that is respected in the Broncos locker room, though, which means you can't rule out him sticking around.
Much of this will come down to his asking price. Stidham is getting $6.5 million this season and will likely seek a bump above that in a new deal. Also, the Broncos might opt to keep another player (who will get to in a minute) and draft a quarterback to compete for the backup job.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
The rest of the pending unrestricted free agents are LS Mitchell Fraboni, WR Lil'Jordan Humphrey, TE Nate Adkins, C Michael Deiter, FB Adam Prentice, OT Matt Peart, IDL Matt Henningsen, QB Sam Ehlinger and S Tycen Anderson.
Among these players, Fraboni, Humphrey, Adkins, Prentice and Ehlinger could all be brought back on one-year deals, with the idea that they would compete for roster spots, and in a couple of cases, get added to the practice squad if they don't make the 53-man roster.
Peart is another possibility, but the Broncos might let him walk if they are fine with the other offensive tackles they have to serve as a a swing tackle.
Deiter and Hennigsen, who were both placed on season-ending injured reserve, will likely be allowed to depart. The same may happen with Anderson, as he hasn't stood out thus far.

title: Broncos' Mini-Bye Player Grades: MVP, Standouts & Underachievers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 4-2 after their first six games, which nearly no one expected given the toughness of their initial schedule.
It hasn't always been pretty. The Broncos' offense has struggled, outside of a few moments, and the defense has been mostly great. Still, they got out to a 4-2 start , tying four other teams for the third-best record in the AFC.
Both of the Broncos' losses came at the hands of the only two remaining undefeated teams entering Week 6: the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers.
With that first six-week gauntlet now in the rearview, we're taking a look at how the individual Broncos have graded out. After every game , I grade each player on a snap-by-snap basis, but this "mini-bye" was a great opportunity to look back at the season so far.
To qualify for a grade, a player needed at least 175 snaps. Only 10 Broncos on offense and 15 on defense qualified.
These grades will cover the Broncos' MVP on both sides of the ball, the highest-graded players, the quarterback, the second- to fourth-highest-graded player on each side of the ball, and the three lowest-graded players on each side of the ball. So, let’s get into it.
This season, Meinerz has allowed six total pressures, tied for the seventh-fewest among 41 guards with at least 300 offensive snaps, and his pass-blocking efficiency is the same. Meanwhile, he has been the NFL's best guard in run blocking across multiple metrics.
Allen has been a monster at the start of the season, and while he has some down moments as a run defender, he still looks improved from where he was a year ago. He leads the Broncos with 26 pressures and leads all NFL interior defensive linemen.
Including edge rushers, Allen ties for the sixth-most pressures in the NFL. With defensive stops, he is tied for the fifth-most among all defensive linemen and edge rushers and is tied for third among interior defensive linemen.
This season has been rough for Nix, with his average depth of target dropping from 7.51 in 2025 to 5.56 in 2026 and his air yards per completion dropping from 4.74 to 3.6. He has taken a massive step back in his play , grown too comfortable in the dink-and-dunk game, and isn’t pushing the ball.
Nix's percentage of throws of 10 or more air yards has also dropped significantly. Denver is 4-2 and through the toughest part of its schedule, but this team needs Nix to be better.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 72.8
Bolles has allowed three pressures on the season, which is the fewest of the Broncos' starting five offensive linemen, and three fewer than Meinerz. Among 45 tackles with at least 300 snaps, Bolles is tied for the fewest pressures allowed and has the highest pass-blocking efficiency.
Nik Bonitto | OLB | Grade: 71.6
Bonitto has the second-most pressures on the team, but his impact was limited over the first four weeks. He totaled just a single sack over that span, 12 of his 20 pressures, and had serious issues as a run defender.
Bonitto has surged over the last two weeks, though, with eight pressures, three sacks, a forced fumble, and improved run-defense play.
Talanoa Hufanga | S | Grade: 64.7
Hufanga has had a good season, but not as good as last year. His run-defending issues and unreliable tackling have contributed to the Broncos' inconsistencies against the run.
Still, Hufanga has done well in coverage and is moving around a bit more to create confusion for opposing quarterbacks. He also has two interceptions, including a pick-six, which helped swing Week 3's victory over the Los Angeles Rams.
Malcolm Roach | DL | Grade: 63.9
Roach has the third-most pressures on the team, the fourth-most stops, and leads in batted passes, but his seven missed tackles are the fifth-most. He's had some huge moments in the passing game and has improved as a run defender each week after a terrible season opener.
Jaylen Waddle | WR | Grade: 59.7
The second game of the season highlighted Waddle's upside, but he has struggled since then. He has four drops through six games, and he needs to clean that up.
However, Waddle's routes have been clean, and his 3.5 yards of average separation is the 15th-highest among 74 receivers.
Ben Powers | LG | Grade: 55.6
Powers has been hit or miss and has allowed the second-most pressures on the Broncos, with 13. His run blocking has helped his grade some, but this still isn’t ideal for a six-game sample size.
Powers is the fourth of 10 offensive players who qualified for a grade over the first six games, with him being 0.3 points higher than tight end Evan Engram and 2.2 points higher than wide receiver Courtland Sutton, before getting to Nix and those in the negative group.
Adam Trautman | TE | Grade: 43.1
Trautman has been rough this year, and his issues as a receiver and blocker have been a detriment to the offense. Nate Adkins has outplayed Trautman, falling short of the snap count for the overall grade, but in the three games Adkins qualified for a grade, he was in the 70s. Trautman's season high was 55.2, and he finished four of the six games under 50.
Eyioma Uwazurike | DL | Grade: 44.7
The Broncos gambled on Uwazurike as a key piece, but he has been mostly a liability on the field. He has easily been the Broncos' worst defender this season, and is having maybe two good or great plays a game, which isn’t ideal for someone averaging 37 snaps per game.
Maybe it's time to get Tyler Onyedim involved on defense. The rookie has been a healthy scratch all season, despite being the Broncos' first pick in the 2026 draft.
Luke Wattenberg | C | Grade: 48.5
Wattenberg has been bad, allowing the third-most pressure on the team and the second-most among 25 centers with at least 300 snaps. His pass-blocking efficiency is tied for second-lowest.
Wattenberg's run blocking has been an even bigger detriment to the offense, and he ranks in the bottom three in almost every run-blocking metric for centers.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 51.1
Elliss is a technical player, but he isn’t overly explosive, which hurts in the modern NFL where explosive plays and explosive potential matter so much. He's had some awful moments, but overall he was solid, though he showed he isn’t a starting-caliber player but rather a solid depth piece.
Elliss's injury against Seattle looked severe , but at least the Broncos are getting Jonathon Cooper back . In other positive developments, Que Robinson vastly outperformed Elliss in five of the six games so far.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 52.9
McGlinchey has allowed the most pressure on the team with 14, which is tied for the 15th-most among 45 tackles with at least 300 snaps. He has always been a bit inconsistent as a pass protector, with his run blocking as a strength, but he's been even more inconsistent in that area this season.
Ja’Quan McMillian | CB | Grade: 53.1
McMillian has made some big plays in big moments, both in his career and this season, but he hasn’t been the most consistent player. His lack of size has been a detriment in the slot, as opponents have looked to take advantage of it both in the passing game with bigger slots and in the run game.
McMillian's missed tackles stem from his lack of size, and opponents have generated multiple explosive plays targeting him. That said, he's been solid, and a 53.1 grade is slightly above average; he just finds himself in the negatives because most of Denver's defenders have been good or great.

title: Insider Reveals Sean Payton's Latest Move to Revive Bo Nix
full_text:
During Denver Broncos training camp, we heard from head coach Sean Payton and a few players that new offensive coordinator Davis Webb had tweaked the verbiage.
Payton spoke publicly about Webb's verbiage tweaks this past summer. Payton made the changes sound like no big deal — a few simple tweaks to streamline the play-calling and help Bo Nix get to the line of scrimmage faster.
Alas, Webb's run as the play-caller was much shorter-lived than expected, as Payton took back the responsibilities after the Broncos' Week 4's loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Payton acknowledged the terminology changes as a factor he had to get accustomed to now that he was calling the plays again.
Fast forward to Week 6, and the Broncos are 4-2. Denver won both games in which Payton has called the plays, but Nix has not looked any better than he did with Webb making the calls. On Sunday, FOX Sports ' Jay Glazer reported that Webb's terminology changes were far more extensive than the Broncos let on, and that Payton has also gone back to using his own terminology.
That's a big shift. These on-the-hoof changes to the offense have only consumed more of Nix's mental bandwidth amid his ongoing slump.
"I asked a bunch of people at the Broncos about that [Nix's struggles], and I didn't know this until this past week is that when Davis Webb took over, he completely changed the terminology on the offensive side of the ball for Bo Nix," Glazer said on FOX NFL Sunday . "Now that Sean Payton has taken it back over, it's like going back to a whole different language that you used to know."
What Glazer reported may be true, but I question the timing of it. Nix has been under fire , with open calls to bench him coming from both the local and national media. Even many Broncos fans have pounded the table for the bench since the team's 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Nix only passed for 107 yards against Seattle, and although he didn't turn the ball over, he and the Broncos' offense were a non-factor in the second half.
This feels a bit like a PR move to ease some of the pressure on Nix and quiet the noise, at least somewhat. That doesn't mean it's not true, though.
I guess what I'm saying is that Payton, who keeps his cards extremely close to his chest, especially during the season, opted to tell this to Glazer at this time for a reason.
However, Payton also believes this reversion to his offensive terminology will help Nix return to his 2025 form.
"So I think at this point, man, his head is just spinning," Glazer said of Nix. "You guys know, an offensive terminology, it's like learning a whole different language out there. But Sean Payton is like, 'I have confidence that he's going to get back to the Bo Nix that we saw the last couple of years.'"
If Webb's terminology changes really were wholesale, I question Payton's wisdom in changing it in-season, let alone co-signing on doing it at all. But if it's true, and Nix is now having to dump all this Webb information on the fly and replace it with past verbiage, that can only slow down his processing.
NFL On Prime 's James Palmer reported that Webb changed " about 30% of the terminology ." That could be more than enough to throw a wrench in things for Nix, from a processing perspective.
Given that it's information Nix has mastered before, it shouldn't take him long to relearn it. For that reason and more, I can buy into Payton's confidence in Nix returning to form.
However, Nix has looked off this whole season, not just since Payton took back the play-calling, so there's obviously much more going on than just the changes in terminology. Hopefully, Payton can get to the bottom of that stuff, too.
The Broncos continue to win games, but it's been with minimal help from the offense, while weapons like Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, and Evan Engram are squandered. Nix is on pace to pass for under 3,000 yards this season and 17 touchdowns, both of which would obviously be career-low numbers and far, far from the big Year-3 leap Broncos Country expected to see.
Still, I don't believe the Nix who passed for 7,500-plus yards and 50-plus touchdowns, while winning 24 games, over his first two seasons has just disappeared, never to be seen again. That quarterback is still in there somewhere, so at the very least, fans can only hope Payton reaches him soon.

title: Film Room: Broncos Aren't Panicking About Bo Nix—Tape Shows Why
full_text:
The discourse around Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is at a fever pitch . The offense hasn’t been playing well over the first six weeks of the season, and his poor play has been at the forefront of the conversation.
Expectations were high for Nix entering Year 3, especially after leading the Broncos to the AFC championship game in 2025. He showed tremendous growth down the stretch last year, and his ability to manufacture game-winning drives when the chips are down has been nothing short of spectacular over his first three NFL seasons, including 2026.
But consistency issues have plagued Nix this season, and he doesn’t look like the same player he was before he broke his ankle in the playoffs. Between two offseason ankle surgeries, a new play-caller to open the 2026 season, and his incessant need to avoid negative plays, his performance has almost hurt the offense more than helped and put the team in some bad situations.
It’s not all bad, though, and the two touchdown drives Nix led against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night showed that with a little better execution, this offense isn’t far from getting back on track. If these drives had settled for field goals instead of touchdowns, the Broncos don't beat the Seahawks in overtime, 17-14 .
Let’s break it down in this week’s film room.
Look what happens when you finally execute! pic.twitter.com/HOzESGQh3r
Fans have been critical of the play-calling this season because the Broncos run so many screens. Sean Payton has always used screens as an extension of the running game, and the offense usually executes them well.
This first play is a great example of that. Watch center Luke Wattenburg and left guard Ben Powers release out and pave the way for running back RJ Harvey to get the drive going. Nix does a nice job of hanging tough to let this play develop in front of him, and Harvey does the rest.
It may not move the needle very much in terms of a spectacular play, but finding and maintaining execution like this is going to be a major key in turning the ship around offensively.
I like where Bo's eyes are on this play. Looking to Waddle draws the safety and opens up the shot to Mims. Shame they can't connect, but that's good process. pic.twitter.com/oJXXhYMlUB
A couple of plays later, Payton dials up a shot play to Marvin Mims Jr. near midfield. I like this play call, because it signals that Payton intended to go for it on fourth down regardless of the outcome of the play. That kind of aggressiveness can help boost morale for your offense, signifying a certain level of trust in your guys to get the job done.
Despite missing on this connection, the process of the play is well done for Nix. Jaylen Waddle is running a pivot route to his right side, and Nix flashes his eyes that way to draw the deep safety in that direction and open up the shot to Mims on the post. Nix hits his back foot and lays out a good ball to Mims, who nearly makes the catch in tight coverage.
Taking these shot plays can help open up the defense, even if you don’t connect. Nix hasn’t been taking these kinds of shots down the field often enough, so it was great to see him air it out against a tough Seattle defense.
Take what you can get on 3rd down. Jones gets too much depth in the hook zone, opening up Engram for a 1st down. Nice job, Bo. pic.twitter.com/QqyxsYSlez
On the ensuing third down, Nix takes what is given to him on a quick throw to tight end Evan Engram underneath. This isn’t anything special, but it's the right play to keep the offense on track. It’s alright to hit the checkdown when you need to.
Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones gets drawn up the field by Courtland Sutton running an in-breaker, opening up a soft spot in the zone for Engram to release into. This is easy pitch-and-catch.
I like that Bo doesn't look flustered with the pocket collapsing on this throw to Sutton. If he can keep this kind of composure in the pocket, he can start to open things up downfield. pic.twitter.com/EK0ecPOl0z
This next play is probably the most promising throw Nix made, because it’s the right read, on time, and allows  Sutton an opportunity to run after the catch over the middle of the field.
Seattle is in man coverage across the board, and the Broncos run a natural pick play with Sutton on the shallow crossing route. Nix hits his back foot and delivers a good ball to Sutton with pressure in his face. Running back Tyler Badie does a great job of picking up the blitzing linebacker, and Nix shows composure to deliver the ball, with right tackle Mike McGlinchey getting pushed into his lap.
Nix’s pocket presence has been rough this season. He’s been vacating clean pockets and running himself into pressure too often, so it was good to see him stay in the play despite having little room to throw.
Bo see's Okada vacate to the middle on the rotation, so he takes a shot to Waddle. Bad ball, but good process. He needs to take more of these shots and good things will happen. pic.twitter.com/jsD9KMlKpb
On the next drive, Nix takes another shot downfield, this time to Waddle.
I love this decision and the process behind it. Seattle has two safeties deep, but they’re in man coverage across the board, and they rotate into a single-high look at the snap. Nix sees safety Ty Okada bail to the middle of the field, opening up one-on-one coverage against Waddle on the go route.
Even though Nix misses on the throw, I like him being aggressive against Devon Witherspoon in coverage. Witherspoon is an incredible cornerback, but Nix trusted Waddle’s playmaking ability to give him a chance downfield.
Again, taking these shots more often can help open up the offense simply by making defenses have to respect the deep passing game.
4 things can happen on a pass play, 2 of them are good for the offense. Reception or penalty. Keep taking shots. Good things can happen. pic.twitter.com/rDK3IgTfsk
The other added benefit of taking those shots is drawing penalties. There are four outcomes to a passing play, and two of them are positive for the offense.
You either make the catch or get a penalty. This shot to Sutton put the Broncos at the 1-yard line due to a Witherspoon pass interference penalty in the end zone.
Nix identifies Sutton against Witherspoon in man coverage and lays it out there. Even though Sutton has struggled in contested-catch scenarios all year, trying to let him make a play for you is a great decision in the red zone. The Broncos would score their second touchdown of the game one play later.
Rumors are flying throughout the media of a possible Nix benching here soon, but that would be a massive mistake. Sure, he needs to play better and within the scope of the offense as it is designed. His inefficiency and lack of willingness to take chances with the football are a big part of the offensive play through six games.
But there is some good in there. It’s not all bad, nor is it all Nix's fault.
Cleaning up some execution , staying in the pocket and allowing plays to develop, and taking some chances can go a long way to improving his play as a whole. With the way the defense is playing this year, the Broncos could start scoring 30 points a game and blow teams out down the stretch with these improvements.
The Broncos' offense is getting extra possessions nearly every week thanks to defensive takeaways. Nix and company need to do a better job of taking advantage of that and sustaining some drives.

title: Concerning Jonah Elliss Injury Development Emerges After Broncos Win
full_text:
Jonathon Cooper's return from the commissioner's exempt list couldn't have come at a better time. On Thursday night, third-year outside linebacker Jonah Elliss suffered a lower-leg injury late in the fourth quarter of the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks.
As Elliss turned the corner on his pass rush, Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton laid a hit on Sam Darnold, and the pair fell into Elliss's lower right leg. In a gritty heads-up move, Elliss was able to hobble off the field, one-hopping it to avoid a timeout that would have stopped the clock.
He was carted from the sideline to the locker room and did not return on Thursday night. We've heard no updates on Elliss's status.
However, on Saturday night, Elliss was at Folsom Field to root on his Utah Utes against the Colorado Buffaloes and was pictured with crutches and a boot on his right leg, courtesy of CBS Colorado 's Romi Bean.
Jonah Elliss in a boot and crutches at the Colorado Utah game last night. https://t.co/lCAMTesL20 pic.twitter.com/c64QW3ZbhI
Sean Payton will hold a zoom press conference on Monday afternoon, which will be our first chance to potentially hear an update, but knowing the Broncos' head coach, he's extremely unlikely to spill the beans on Elliss or any other injured player.
Elliss's boot-and-crutches combo implies a more serious injury, but perhaps we shouldn't rush to judgment. Remember, after Jaylen Waddle was seen exiting Empower Field at Mile High in Week 2 in a walking boot , Payton said later that it's much more common than people realize. Waddle practiced that week and played in Week 3.
Elliss has the escalating factor of the crutches to go with the boot, though. It doesn't look good, but that only makes Cooper's return all the more timely.
Elliss has started in place of Cooper in all six games thus far. Elliss has been a solid relief starter, but has lacked the consistency as a pass rusher.
Against the Seahawks, though, Elliss totaled six QB pressures and notched his first sack of the season. In one game, he nearly matched his season total in pressures, so he may have been turning a corner. That makes this injury uniquely sucky for Elliss.
A 2024 third-round pick out of Utah, the Broncos have been looking for ways to get him on the field more, even exploring a few packages with him at inside linebacker . Cooper's legal troubles solved that problem for Denver, with Elliss taking over as a starter.
With Elliss injured, it will be interesting to see how the Broncos work Cooper back into the rush linebacker rotation. The seventh-year veteran is playing on his second contract and has totaled 27 sacks over the past three years as a starter.
Que Robinson has become a consistent impact player, and while I know many Broncos fans would love to see him start opposite Nik Bonitto, the team stood behind Cooper amid his off-the-field legal troubles for a reason.
The Broncos love Cooper, and even if Elliss hadn't gotten hurt, he was always going to step right back into his starting role opposite Bonitto. Now, that doesn't mean that Denver will throw Cooper straight into the fire; he'll likely be eased back into full starter's snaps, but he's the guy, and he's a highly paid veteran.
The Broncos' pass rush has begun to come alive over the past two games. Elliss has been a part of that resurgence, especially in Week 6.
The Broncos get a one-game roster exemption with Cooper's return, but it wouldn't be a surprise if Elliss ends up on short-term injured reserve. With Cooper back, the Broncos have a healthy Bonitto, Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman, so the edge-rushing party can continue.
We'll keep you updated on what happens next with Elliss.

title: Mike Valenti Shares Bold Feelings About Lions Not Landing Joey Porter Jr.
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were not able to land one of the top available cornerbacks and frustrations are mounting, as Kelvin Sheppard's pass defense is the worst in the National Football League.
Among the critics of general manager Brad Holmes not being able to land a player that would significantly upgrade the defense is 97.1 The Ticket sports talk radio host Mike Valenti.
He expressed his views earlier this week after witnessing Porter Jr. perform well in coverage against Packers wideout Christian Watson.
"Man, you really f'd up not getting Joey Porter Jr. Watching last night really encapsulates it," said Valenti. "And again, I think the dimwitted take would be, 'Well, Dallas isn't winning.' Their defense didn't cost them that game last night. Joey Porter Jr. locked up on Christian Watson, who's been a top five receiver this year. That's a big player. That's a 6'3, tall, rangy, big-bodied receiver. Porter was tasked with playing Watson most of the night with no help.
"Watson had his quietest game of the year. Multiple PBU's. Yes, there was one penalty, but Joey Porter Jr., they were helping everyone else, not him."
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Packers Enter Week 7 With Josh Jacobs, Without Micah Parsons
Against the Cowboys, Watson secured only three receptions for 64 yards, below his season average entering the Week 5 contest.
"You put that guy on this Lions defense, allowing D.J. Reed to have help. Man, what a difference it would make. You really f'd up," Valenti said. "That was the guy. That's the best corner that's going to get dealt. That's the guy. And you saw it living color last night. You did not lose that game because Joey Porter Jr. got dusted. They didn't. And again, a corner can only do so much. The pieces have to work together. The two games he's played for the Cowboys, I think he had poopy pants last week. He had to leave the game sick. He's been excellent. You f'd up."
It has been a completely smooth transition for the former Steelers defender. An illness forced him to miss a game already for the NFC East squad.
"I really just couldn't hold anything down," he said, via the Cowboys team website . "You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn't hold in deep down. So, that's when they made the call to send me home."
Despite his best efforts to attempt to play, he was unable to suit up against the Buccaneers.
"On my way to the game, I was throwing up outside of my Uber," Porter explained. "It was brutal. I'm not gonna lie. You go into the week thinking you're gonna get more of a workload, and you're ready to go, and then that's ultimately what doesn't happen. It was very frustrating . I was prepared to play all week. My mindset was on playing, the mindset was to get the dub, and obviously I didn't get to do that, and we didn't get the dub. I was pretty pissed."

title: Lions 2026 Playoff Standings Update: Divisional Showdowns Loom Large
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are exiting their bye week and entering into what could be a season-defining set of games.
Through the first six weeks of the NFL season, the NFC North is looking like one of the toughest divisions in football yet again. It's one of only two divisions in football where every team has a winning record, with the other being the AFC North.
Because of the heightened levels of competition, every week is an urgent one for all four teams including the Lions. This is especially true for Detroit in its upcoming two games , as they will play their first two divisional games of the season.
Both games will be at home, which will be a big boost for a team that has had lots of success in its two games in front of their home crowd. This could be a big advantage as these two games against the Packers (Week 7) and Vikings (Week 8) could be season-defining for a team looking to win its third division crown in four years.
Green Bay has won two games in a row after a tough start, and are getting running back Josh Jacobs back at running back after being taken off the Commissioner's Exempt List. Additionally, quarterback Jordan Love appears to be rounding into form and his connection with wide receiver Christian Watson has been dangerous for opposing defenses.
After that, the Lions will take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings, who would enter that matchup 6-0 if they defeat the Indianapolis Colts this upcoming week. Through five games the Vikings' defense, led by wunderkind coordinator Brian Flores, has allowed just 64 total points.
Because of how competitive the division is, the Lions must at least take one of the two in theory to remain in the mix for the division title. With the NFC East and West divisions off to slow starts, the North could send multiple teams to the playoffs and as a result a Wild Card spot would still be within reach even if Detroit falls to 3-4.
However, the Lions under Dan Campbell have always held a home playoff game in high regard, and the only way to earn one would be to win their division. As a result, these games will hold the utmost value moving forward.
Currently, the Lions hold the seventh and final playoff spot in the NFC through six weeks. Seattle is right behind them at 3-3, as they haven't had their bye week. Beyond them, the Atlanta Falcons, New Orleans Saints, Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys, Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams are all 2-4.
Detroit will have another big stretch with games against all three of their divisional foes within a four-game stretch to end the year, with all three of those being road contests. By winning these two upcoming matchups, it puts them in an advantageous positions for those late-season tilts.
Here is an updated look at the NFC North and NFC playoff standings after six weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
1.) Minnesota Vikings (5-0). 2.) Green Bay Packers (4-2). 3.) Chicago Bears (4-2). 4.) Detroit Lions (3-2).
1.) San Francisco 49ers (6-0). 2.) Minnesota Vikings (5-0). 3.) Carolina Panthers (3-2). 4.) New York Giants (3-2-1). 5.) Green Bay Packers (4-2). 6.) Chicago Bears (4-2). 7.) Detroit Lions (3-2).

title: Dan Campbell Makes Surprising Admission About 2025 Detroit Lions Season
full_text:
The bye week provided Detroit Lions head coach an opportunity to reflect on the roster, the coaching staff and where he feels the team is at, through the first five games of the 2026 NFL season.
Speaking with local reporters, the former NFL tight end shared an interesting revelation about the team coming out of the bye this year.
Campbell noted he feels better about the team this year than last year, coming out of the bye week, when asked if the success of the offensive line is critical to finding the identity of the team this year.
“It's very critical. Oddly enough, there are elements of when you think about, our bye's earlier this year than last year. Last year was one of those rare years where we had it really right in the middle. But that being said, we went in and I don't remember what we were, but we had just won and seems pretty good," said Campbell. "But there were some things that you could feel a little bit. And that in some regards I feel better going into this bye than even I did last year, because I know we're ascending and we're young and we're growing and that's exciting."
Additional Lions Insider Analysis: Coaching Staff Still Trying To Figure Out Playing Time For Returning Players
Last season, their were issues with offensive coordinator John Morton, resulting in Campbell making the decision to take over play-calling duties. Morton was not a fit and likely upset the locker room by publicly blaming players making mistakes for offensive woes.
Detroit's rushing attack was not efficient and there were signs the offensive line was not gelling propery.
"Sometimes you feel like you're topped off and maybe you're beginning to deteriorate because of issues worn down, age, whatever it is. So that's exciting. I do feel like we're on the rise here a little bit. We've just got to keep getting better," Campbell said. "We've got to keep testing ourselves . And look, we're in for the long haul now and it's really about to get geared up and the competition is about to really raise up another level, and it starts with Green Bay.”

title: Lions Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost With Four Weeks Left
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking to win a third NFC North title in four years.
After missing the playoffs last season, Dan Campbell's team has started 3-2 in 2026. Coming off their bye week, they have big divisional matchups against the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings in their next two weeks.
The Lions have had some success, but their defense remains a detracting factor as far as their long-term viability. They will have an opportunity to add talent in this area ahead of the trade deadline, which is set for Nov. 10, and doing so in the defensive backfield appears to be the best path forward.
For general manager Brad Holmes , there are multiple intriguing options that could be available after the first six weeks of the season.
Here is a list of candidates that could be intriguing trade targets at the Lions' biggest area of need with less than a month remaining until the trade deadline.
1.) Philadelphia Eagles CB Riq Woolen
Woolen signed a one-year deal with the Eagles this offseason after a strong start to his career in Seattle. However, with the Eagles now sitting at 2-4 and quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, things are trending down and as a result they could wind up being sellers.
While he doesn't have the flashiest numbers in his six games to start the year, Woolen is a veteran who won the Super Bowl last year in Seattle. He's also a rental, so the price to acquire him shouldn't be astronomical.
2.) Kansas City Chiefs CB Kristian Fulton
Fulton is a player who has been linked to the Lions for several weeks. In the final year of his current deal with the Chiefs, he's part of a logjam at cornerback in Kansas City that features veteran L'Jarius Sneed and first-round pick Mansoor Delane.
Because of their depth, the Chiefs could view Fulton as expendable despite their undefeated start to the season. He would instantly slot in as Detroit's second-best option behind D.J. Reed, giving the Lions another solid veteran option.
3.) Tampa Bay Buccaneers CB Zyon McCollum
Tampa Bay has had a difficult start to the season, now sitting at 1-5 after an overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. As a result, they could look to deal some of their expensive options that have some value such as McCollum.
It wouldn't be a cheap add for the Lions, as McCollum is under contract through the end of the 2028 season as part of a three-year, $48 million contract extension. The Lions still want to get deals done with Sam LaPorta and Brian Branch, so adding another big contract to the books through trade may create some challenges.
4.) Los Angeles Chargers CB Donte Jackson
Jackson has missed the last two games due to a hamstring injury. However, he's a veteran journeyman who has experience in different schemes, and if healthy would be a worthwhile addition for the Lions.
The Chargers have sputtered out of the gate to an 0-6 start, and so the Lions could also inquire about defensive backs Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart. Jackson, a veteran who is in the final year of his contract, is the most likely of the group to be available.
5.) Philadelphia Eagles CB Kelee Ringo
Ringo would be a buy-low option for Detroit in the event that other top targets go off the board. He has played almost exclusively on special teams this year, and hasn't had much in terms of proven defensive production throughout his career in Philadelphia.
This is a player that was billed as one of the top corners in the 2023 draft at one time, and perhaps the Lions could get some value out of making a deal and giving him an opportunity. He'd be another rental option, and might be best as a supplemental addition.
1.) Arizona Cardinals S Budda Baker
The Lions just got an up-close look at Baker last week in their win over the Arizona Cardinals. In that game, Baker started the game with a big play as he timed up a blitz perfectly to sack Jared Goff.
Baker's credentials are among the best of any player expected to be available. He's an eight-time Pro Bowl selection and a two-time First Team All-Pro, and would bring some serious versatility to Detroit's secondary.
He's under contract through next season, which would give the Lions some stability moving forward or an opportunity to create some cap space if they don't see a benefit of keeping him into next year.
2.) Atlanta Falcons S Jessie Bates
Bates is in the final year of his contract with the Falcons. Atlanta is still in the mix in the NFC South, even at 2-4, but could look to be sellers at the deadline in an effort to add some draft capital. He doesn't have an interception this year, but has notched 27 total across his career.
With the uncertainty surrounding Kerby Joseph, Bates is a proven takeaway generator who could give the defense a spark.
3.) Tennessee Titans S Amani Hooker
Hooker signed an extension prior to last season, and is under contract through the 2028 season. The Titans are sputtering at 1-5, and he could wind up being one of their most valuable trade pieces as they look to rebuild in Robert Saleh's first year as head coach.
He's another option the Lions could look to to fill Joseph's void, or at the very least supplement their depth at safety.

title: Former Lions DB Apologizes For Spitting, Accused Again by 49ers Fullback
full_text:
Former Detroit Lions defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson again finds himself in the news for conduct deemed inappropriate out on the football field.
The Buffalo Bills safety was ejected from the Week 6 game against the Las Vegas Raiders for apparently spitting on tight end Brock Bowers.
The 28-year-old spent one season in Motown, but unfortunately missed the majority of the 2023 regular season with a torn pectoral muscle. He was able to appear in all three postseason games after rehabbing all season.
Gardner-Johnson, who at times wanted to be addressed as "Ceedy Duce," has issued an apology on social media for his actions.
“I want to take a moment to address my actions and sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me. My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed. The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game.”
There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard. To my opponent, I sincerely apologize. We compete hard between those lines, but respect should always remain at the forefront.”

One moment does not define my character, but how I respond to that moment matters. I will learn from this, grow from it, and continue to lead with the integrity, passion, and respect that have carried me throughout my career. I love this game , I respect this game, and I will always protect the integrity of this game. My actions will speak louder than my words moving forward.”
After catching wind of the ejection, San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk accused the Bills defender of similar actions against him last year.
Juszcczyk shared on social media, "This is the least surprising thing ever. @CJGXXIII spit on me last year when we beat Chicago."

title: Lions Still Trying To Figure Out Playing Time For Returning Players
full_text:
The Detroit Lions face an interesting dilemma this week with the return of two key players.
Safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays are set to make their 2026 season debuts, after rehabbing injuries throughout the offseason and training camp.
Head coach Dan Campbell indicated, in his first media session after the bye week, it was not really realistic to expect Branch to play 70 defensive snaps this week.
"I think that would be asking a lot to say he is going to play 70 plays," said Campbell. "We feel like there's, we do feel like he can handle quite a bit here. We're going to push him in practice here early. That is one of the reasons we are practicing tomorrow and not Wednesday, so we can push some of these guys just a little bit. Knowing that they are going into a day off.
"I think that will help a little bit," Campbell added further. "We will have a really good idea by the time we hit the game. We are already, you know, kind of have a range of what we are looking at for him and for Cade a little bit. ..."
The added dilemma involves how to utilize Juice Scruggs, who is currently ranked as the top PFF-graded in the league.
Mays was given a lucrative contract in free agency, but the Lions coaching staff does not want to discount the solid start to the season from the former Houston Texans lineman.
"We are still a little back and forth on what we do with him. Do we work he and Juice (Scruggs) in and out? The center position is a little bit different than a guard. That is someone that is constantly touching the football," said Campbell. "Either way, barring anything negatively happening , between now and the game, we plan on playing both of those guys (Mays and Branch)."
Scruggs has made the coaching staff really discuss and evaluate how to utilize him moving forward.
"He's done a good job," Campbell explained. "He has gotten better every week. Juice is a freakin team guy. Does not mean that he, if it comes to that (playing Mays), that he does not like that, because there is an argument to keep him rolling. He is playing good football. He is a team guy. He is all-in. He will do whatever we ask him to do. ..."

title: Ranking Detroit Lions Players Most Likely To Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are expected to be buyers, not sellers, ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
At 3-2, the Lions are bracing for a massive showdown with the Green Bay Packers in Week 7, followed by a battle against the Minnesota Vikings. Those two games ahead of the deadline should offer a great glimpse into the ceiling of this team and whether or not they should make a splash at the deadline.
If that stretch doesn't go as planned, the Lions could pivot and look to sell. While the roster is built to contend, there are some veteran options that could be available in the event the Lions struggle.
Here is a ranking of five of the most likely players to be traded on the Lions roster in the event that they look to become sellers at the trade deadline.
A starter at the beginning of the year, Ya-Sin has seen his role diminish in recent weeks due to a combination of poor performance and the emergence of Ennis Rakestraw. The Lions are expected to target the secondary before the deadline, and as a result Ya-Sin could be expendable.
While he may not have the most robust market, Ya-Sin could fetch a late-round pick from a team looking for more cornerback depth. The veteran does have special teams experience and would help a team in some capacity.
The Lions elected to retain Onwuzurike after he missed all of last season, but the play of Tyleik Williams and Skyler Gill-Howard has lessened the need for more production on the interior defensive line.
While Onwuzurike has struggled with injuries throughout his career, when healthy he's shown that he can have a legitimate impact. He's down the depth chart for the Lions, but another team could see him as an ideal option due to his versatility along the defensive line.
Scruggs has been a great addition to the Lions, and the only reason he's on this list is because there is a change coming with the return of Cade Mays. The Lions could get Mays back as soon as this upcoming week against Green Bay, which could push Scruggs out from the center position.
Before the season, Scruggs was expected to compete for the left guard spot with Christian Mahogany. However, while Scruggs has played center Mahogany has played exceptionally well as the team's left guard.
As a result, assuming Mays reclaims the center spot and plays well and Mahogany keeps up his solid production, Scruggs could be without a starting spot. Though he'd be great depth, there could be a team that
The Lions' linebacker room took a big hit with the injury to Devin White, which likely moves Rodriguez up to the third option behind starters Jack Campbell and Derrick Barnes. However, Rodriguez is on a one-year contract and could have some suitors around the league.
Detroit is very deep at the linebacker position, with Trevor Nowaske and Jimmy Rolder also in the mix. If the Lions decide to commit more snaps to Nowaske and Rolder, perhaps Rodriguez would be deemed expendable.
While the Lions view LaPorta as a cornerstone player and want to get a deal done with him, reports indicate that the two sides are currently not close on an extension. There are avenues the Lions could take to keep him, such as the franchise tag, but if they aren't close the team could entertain a trade.
LaPorta would be the biggest realistic trade piece the Lions have on their roster given the current contract situation. If things go south out of the bye, the Lions may be more inclined to listen to calls based on what they could get in return as well as how tough it may be to climb back into the playoff race in a loaded NFC.

title: Detroit Lions Are Small Betting Favorite Against Packers in Week 7
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will finally begin division play in Week 7 at Ford Field.
After a Week 6 bye, Dan Campbell's squad have opened as a three-point betting favorite against the Green Bay Packers, according to DraftKings sports book .
Detroit's division rival is arriving with a record of 4-2 and having defeated the Dallas Cowboys, 23-13, on Sunday Night Football.
Despite a solid performance against the Arizona Cardinals, the former NFL tight end expressed last week the coaching staff was planning to evaluate all three phases, to clean up the mistakes that will be costly, if they continue the remainder of the season.
"I think it's important we look at the whole thing. We played much better. It's one of our best games. It was our best game this year. But to say that, 'Well, there we are, we've arrived,' that would not be wise. So no, my plan is to look at all of them," said Campbell. "Like I told those guys, I don't need the numbers. I don't need the, 'Well, here's where we're at at third down percentage.' I don't need all that. I know what that is. I need to know schematically, what can we improve on? What are some things that defenses are offering like they've got a tendency on us that we need to adjust."
Another aspect the coaching staff is looking for is identifying the players they can trust in critical moments of games.
"What players are really making big plays for us across the board in critical moments? We need to know who those are. We've got a pretty good idea of who they are for us," said Campbell. "But there's some guys that may pop a little bit like, 'Okay, we need to use this guy a little bit more. This is somebody we can really count on.' And then, 'Hey, this guy's really good until you get in critical moments. And then we get in critical moments and this guy's killing us.' Well, we need to keep him out of critical moments. It's little stuff like that and it makes a difference.
"So, those are the things I want to look at, and we're going to look at it in totality," Campbell added further. "We've got a pretty good idea. I mean, we just went through the four weeks of things that weren't so good. But we're going into the bye on a positive note, and we've got things to clean up. And I mentioned this last night, that's a step in the right direction. But to think that's going to be good enough for Green Bay, it's not. We still need to clean up more than, we need to clean up a lot more than that, and we can, and we will.”

title: Detroit Lions Face Returning RB, Will Avoid Micah Parsons
full_text:
Coming off the bye, the Detroit Lions will be tested right away against one of their fiercest rivals: the Green Bay Packers . The Packers, led by eighth-year head coach Matt LaFleur, are winners of two in a row (at time of this publication).
And they'll be equipped with their star running back , Josh Jacobs, for the first time this season.
Jacobs has been on the commissioner exempt list since Aug. 30, following the filing of misdemeanor battery and criminal property damage charges against him in May.
The seventh-year back is set to be removed from the list Monday, allowing him to practice and play against Detroit next week. Yet, the NFL's investigation into Jacobs remains ongoing, leaving open the possibility that he could still be suspended and miss additional games this season.
Jacobs should provide a significant boost to the Packers’ ground game , which has averaged a measly 3.1 yards a carry heading into Green Bay's primetime affair with Dallas in Week 6. That average, by the way, is the second-worst mark among all 32 NFL franchises.
Jacobs, meanwhile, averaged 4.0 yards per carry, and amassed 929 yards and 13 touchdowns on the ground in his second season with the Packers in 2025. He was also productive in his two games against the Lions a season ago, notably rushing for 83 yards on 17 carries in a Week 13 win against Dan Campbell's squad.
Unquestionably, Jacobs is an integral member of LaFleur's offensive attack, and he's likely to provide plenty of fits next Sunday to Detroit's pedestrian run defense.
While Green Bay will be getting Jacobs back, it will not have superstar EDGE Micah Parsons at its disposal for its Week 7 tilt at Ford Field.
Parsons, who has been on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list since the end of the exhibition season, is still in the process of working his way back from a torn ACL and meniscus injury he suffered last December. And he has still yet to be cleared to return to practice, meaning he will remain sidelined a week from now against the Lions.
Kickoff for the Packers’ Week 7 contest in Detroit is scheduled for next Sunday at 4:25 p.m. EST.
