title: Eagles Refused to Give Tanner McKee the Support He Needed Most in Week 6 Start
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Good friend DeVonta Smith was back for Week 6 after missing two games and was useful. Dallas Goedert is a good buddy too, and a solid security blanket, and he was both of those things. The quarterback’s best friend, however, is supposed to be a running game.
The Eagles didn’t have one in their 25-14 home loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Tanner McKee could have used his best friend. Instead, he was forced to throw the ball 45 times. In just his third career start.
It’s like the coaches just said, “Hey Tanner, go win us this game.” For all the talk about everybody playing their part, the Eagles sure put a lot on McKee’s shoulders.
OK, I get it. The Eagles running back room is a lonely place. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are on injured reserve. Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury. Then, as if that wasn’t bad enough, the Eagles lost Carson Steele to a shoulder injury in the first quarter.
Steele returned later. He took a couple of special teams reps but was then shut down for the second half. That left them with Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue, who was added to the roster on Saturday then parked on the bench when the offense took the field.
Reduced to just those two players - one, really, because there was, surprisingly, nothing in the game plan for Blue - doesn’t mean you just stop trying to run the ball, even with an offensive line that is patchwork at best.
You just don’t throw in the towel when the team on the other side of the ball brought with it the next-to-last run defense in the NFL, allowing 168 yards per game.
The Eagles couldn’t be bothered with trying to dent it. Pierce ran it 12 times for 35 yards. McKee ran once for 0 yards.
So, that’s 45 passes to 13 runs. Drunken sailors have better balance.
Nick Sirianni was asked postgame for his thoughts on the imbalance. The coach said something about being behind 19-7 and needing to play catch-up.
“We had to go fast with, I don't know, 12 minutes left or something like that,” he said. “Two possessions; you only scored seven points at that point. You gotta go fast to give yourself a chance to score, which we went down and scored, and then get it back, and that was the mode that we had success on, so we did it again.”
Never mind that on the first play of the game, McKee dropped back and was sacked for an 11-yard loss. Buried in a hole, two more pass plays were dialed up, including one on third-and-21. Neither worked, and they punted.
On their next series, the Eagles threw three more times, one of which was a 3-yard loss to Makai Lemon. That led to another punt. They threw four straight times on their third possession with enough success to at least get a first down.
They threw or tried to throw on their first 10 plays when the score was 0-0 and 3-0.
McKee was asked about playing without a quarterback’s best friend, too. He “um-ed” his way through the answer.
“I'm a quarterback,” he said, mixing in a couple of ‘ums’, “I am excited to execute the play that is called (more 'ums'). I love slinging the ball around. I know I can be better with things like that. I personally, I don't see that as a terrible thing.”
It’s not a winning formula to throw 45 times and run the ball 13 times. Not in the NFL. The best teams like balance in their offense. The Eagles do, too. They’ve shown that to be the case during the last five years when they’ve been to two Super Bowls and won a lot of games.
Sirianni relented a bit later in his answer about the imbalance.
“Obviously, right now we're not running the ball the way we want to,” he said. “You do whatever you gotta do to try to win the game. That's what that game called for. Obviously, we didn't win, but that's what that game called for, and there's circumstances that go to that.”
Barkley could be McKee's best friend, and getting him back could do wonders, but it's still not clear when that will be.

title: 5 Losers & 3 Winners After Eagles' Skid Extends to Four Games With Loss to Panthers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. – The Tanner McKee era got off to an uneven start. The backup quarterback, pressed into action for at least the next four games after Jalen Hurts landed on injured reserve for the first time in his career with a blood clot in his calf, did some good, but mixed in just enough bad to keep the Eagles winless in their last four games after a 25-14 loss to the Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field in Week 6.
Now, 2-4, the Eagles will prepare for a visit from the Cowboys on Monday Night Football next week.
The game was there to be won, with the Panthers hurting themselves with penalties and the Eagles' defense playing well enough for as long as it could, but the offense just couldn’t quite make it happen.
They made it interesting when McKee hit DeVonta Smith with a touchdown pass (h/t NFL) from 19 yards with 10:47 to play in the fourth quarter that brought Philly to within 19-14, but the momentum left when Jake Majors's bad snap went for a 12-yard loss after the Eagles got the ball at the 48 midway through the fourth, needing a touchdown to take its first lead.
Tanner McKee throws DeVonta Smith a perfect ball for the touchdown CARvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6xngV0MgMW
McKee probably did enough to earn a second start – really, what other options do the Eagles have?
He sprayed the ball high and wide on many of his 45 throws, but other times, when he got the ball out quickly, he was able to find a rhythm and lead a pair of TD drives. The first ended with a two-yard touchdown run by Dameon Pierce to pull the Eagles to within 10-7, a score that stood at halftime. The other was the nice throw to Smith.
McKee was sacked three times, and while his numbers will look decent, some of it was after the Panthers went up 11 points in the final quarter. He finished 26-for-45 with 215 yards, a TD, and no interceptions.
The play-calling was suspect, however. Rather than try to run the ball early, the Eagles dialed up six straight passes, which led to three-and-outs on their first two possessions of the game. They had five of them in the game.
The Panthers (3-2) were called for 13 penalties totaling 149 yards, all in the first half, which ended in Carolina’s favor, 10-7.
Not even the addition of McKee could help the Eagles find a way to score points in both the first and third quarters. They were shut out in both quarters again and have just three points in each of them this season.
DeVonta Smith: His return was most welcome, if not nearly enough to secure a win. He was targeted 14 times and finished with seven catches for 75 yards and a TD.
Jalen Carter: The defensive tackle rarely came off the field. He had two passes batted at the line of scrimmage and three tackles while seemingly playing most of the game.
Dallas Goedert: The tight end had six catches on eight targets for 61 yards.
Jake Majors: With momentum on their side, the Eagles' center had a bad, low snap that lost 12 yards. The Eagles had just gotten a three-and-out stop and took over at the 48-yard line. The Eagles couldn’t overcome the gaffe and punted with 8:30 left.
Special teams: The Eagles had a punt partially blocked after going three-and-out after Majors’s gaffe, giving Carolina good field position. It’s the second straight week the special teams have had a breakdown. Last week it was the kickoff return with eight seconds left that led to defeat. This one allowed the Panthers to open their lead to 11 points.
Running game: Dameon Pierce had his moments. His two-yard touchdown run to cut Carolina’s lead to 10-7 in the second quarter was his first TD since Jan. 5, 2025, while with Houston. He had two in that 2024 season. Still, the Panthers’ defense was next-to-last in the league at stopping the run.
Yet the Eagles managed just 35 yards on the ground, though they rarely tried to run. Pierce had 12 runs, and McKee scrambled for another rush. Carolina entered allowing 168 per game.
Moro Ojomo: The defensive tackle was called for encroachment early in the fourth quarter with the Panthers inside the five and lining up to go for it on fourth down. It was the second time this season Ojomo had a five-yard penalty on a team lining up to go for it on fourth down. The Panthers scored two plays later to open a 19-7 lead with 13:34 to play.
Cooper DeJean: The defensive back is not having the same kind of season he did last year. He committed an illegal contact penalty that gave Carolina a third down, and his inexcusable personal foul with seven minutes to play pushed Carolina deeper into Eagles territory at the 20. Carolina put the game away from there with a touchdown with 6:32 to play.

title: 3 Free-Agent QBs Eagles Must Call Immediately After Losing Jalen Hurts to IR
full_text:
It's been a rocky start to the 2026 NFL season for the Eagles, who are now without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for at least four games. Blood clot issues led to the veteran signal-caller's placement on injured reserve earlier this week, leaving backup QB Tanner McKee as the de facto starting option against the Panthers in Week 6 and for the foreseeable future.
Without Hurts, it remains to be seen if Philadelphia's quarterback room is good enough to turn the season around.
Despite flashes of potential here and there, McKee began Week 6 with only two starts under his belt, and even though the Eagles signed Joe Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad for help this week, he still hasn't started an NFL regular-season game. The same goes for rookie QB Cole Payton, who shouldn't see the field this year unless it's an absolute emergency.
With the aforementioned trio the Eagles' only QB options behind Hurts, general manager Howie Roseman might want to look at bringing in another veteran for help. Although the pickings are somewhat slim at this stage of the season, there are at least three options for the Philly front office to consider.
What's old could become new again.
Philadelphia traded for Andy Dalton back in March to acquire some competition for McKee. The three-time Pro Bowl passer impressed the Eagles enough throughout the offseason to win the No. 2 job from McKee, but his run didn't last long. Dalton attempted one pass that resulted in an interception against the Bears in Week 3 before eventually being released by the Eagles on Oct. 9 .
But now that Hurts is sidelined, the Eagles might want to bring Dalton back. He's already received some calls from other teams since his release, according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo, who added that "Dalton is an option to return for the Eagles."
Andy Dalton is an option to return for the #Eagles . He’s had a few teams check in with him since the team released him, per sources, though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return. https://t.co/bNeypdIjiO
Sometimes, familiarity trumps all, and that's what Dalton has with the Eagles. He might not want to learn another new system at this stage of his career, so running things back in Philly could be the most attractive option if the Eagles join the teams already in contact with Dalton.
If the Eagles prefer an option with a championship pedigree, Jimmy Garoppolo could be an interesting possibility for Roseman & Co. to consider.
The former 2014 second-rounder has won two Super Bowls throughout his career, both coming with the Patriots. Although Garoppolo didn't play a large role in either run, you can't take that experience away from him. He's since gained plenty of in-game experience on the West Coast, going 41-21 with a 67.4% completion rate, 15,138 passing yards, 91 touchdowns to 52 interceptions and a 97.2 passer rating in 65 games with the 49ers, Raiders and Rams.
Garoppolo hasn't started a game in nearly two years, but he likely still has enough left in the tank to at least be a reliable backup. His presence could also push young guys like McKee and Milton to step it up, all while giving Payton another veteran presence he can lean on for advice.
He wouldn't be the "Jimmy G" who went 13-3 while passing for almost 4,000 yards and 27 TDs in 2019, but there's a lot worse that the Eagles can do at this point.
The remaining QB options are less than ideal, but Bailey Zappe might be the best of the bunch.
A well-traveled journeyman, Zappe has made steps in New England, Kansas City, Cleveland and New York since being drafted 137th overall in 2022. His resume is far from perfect, but he's only one game below .500 in nine career starts and has completed 62.1% of passes for 2,223 yards, 12 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. That should be enough experience that Sirianni would feel comfortable putting him in a game if needed.
Additionally, Zappe may be motivated to prove himself after being released by the Jets last month. He's only 27 years old, so better days could be ahead, and joining a winning organization like the Eagles could be what he needs to bounce back. Of course, that would be a win-win outcome for both sides, adding to why Philadelphia should give it a shot.

title: McMullen: Eagles’ 2026 Season Has Become Its Own Goodfellas-Like 'Bust-Out'
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The cleanest analogy for the Eagles’ 2026 season is the iconic Goodfellas (1990) monologue in which Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) explains how Paulie Cicero (Paul Sorvino) bleeds a business dry once he becomes a silent partner.
“Now the guy’s got Paulie as a partner,” Hill says. “Any problems, he goes to Paulie. Trouble with the bill? He can go to Paulie. Trouble with the cops, deliveries, Tommy, he can call Paulie. But now the guy’s gotta come up with Paulie’s money every week, no matter what. Business bad? (EXPLETIVE) you, pay me. Oh, you had a fire? (EXPLETIVE) you, pay me. Place got hit by lightning, huh? (EXPLETIVE) you, pay me.”
The Nick Sirianni era’s sustained success is the original healthy business in this comparison. Reaching and then exceeding those heightened expectations is the weekly payment that now has to be made regardless of circumstance.
The “bust-out” is underway after significant adversity. The organization and the fan base have signed on as partners. There are no more free weeks in Philadelphia.
Lane Johnson retires? Three novices starting on the offensive line? Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith both out? (EXPLETIVE) you, win.
The bill is still due on game day, lightning strikes or not.
Maybe the Vatican won’t be chiming in, but the Eagles staying competitive against the Rams and Jaguars in Weeks 4 and 5—and still in position to win late in both—already qualifies as a minor miracle under the current conditions. Moral victories can't even bring temporary relief; however, never mind canceling the next installment.
The stress inside the Jefferson Health Training Complex hit a new peak this week once it became clear that Jalen Hurts could miss extended time as he landed on injured reserve with a blood clot. The organization is at its breaking point, and the next payment is due against the Panthers on Sunday.
Tanner McKee will start at quarterback. His running backs will be Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and Jaydon Blue. Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors are expected to make their second NFL starts, while Markel Bell is on No. 3, serving as the mixture of youth and duct tape . At least Smith is expected back, which removes one hurdle, but the overall picture remains bleak.
Through it all, the refrain does not change. The context does not get a vote. The Eagles are deep enough into the Sirianni-era success cycle that the only acceptable answer to every new problem is still the same two words: win anyway.
Right now, that's still the only standard that's acceptable and it's not realistic.

title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling Signing Might Mean Good News for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are adding Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad , and it's easy to interpret that they're expecting to call him up to the active roster as soon as possible.
Truthfully, we all should have saw this coming. Head coach Mike McCarthy hinted at it just hours before the report broke, and it felt obvious that Valdes-Scantling was the top option for this team.
"The biggest thing is just continue to develop. You're probably tired of hearing this, I know Omar [Khan] is too. I believe in the 68 guys that we have in the building. When opportunities are presented, that's who I prefer to go with, but I'm not blind or naive to the others, the men that are out there, especially if you work with individuals in the past or they have a past relationship here and so forth," McCarthy said during his weekly press conference. "You're always looking, and that's Omar's job, and our personnel department does a good job of it. I thought both [Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson] did some good things. They've just got to keep working. These guys have — they've busted their tail. They've earned this opportunity. We'll just continue to work."
Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson didn't play well enough for this team to believe they were the answers moving forward, and are now prepared to test out an old friend of the team's and Aaron Rodgers'. And while most fans seemed disappointed in the news, it may hint at good news for the Steelers moving forward.
Valdes-Scantling is coming to Pittsburgh to help fill the void left by Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot). Both are on Injured Reserve, and it's unknown how long they're expected to miss, with reports claiming Pittman Jr. might be out for a longer period of time this season.
The addition of a 32-year-old wideout doesn't move the needle in times of need, but maybe that's a good thing. Because it might be hinting that the Steelers are prepared to push through just a few weeks before getting at least one of their starting wide receivers back - and chances are, that'll be Wilson.
Wilson needs to miss another three games before being eligible to return to practice and eventually the active roster. That would make Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles the first game he could be back on the field for the Steelers, if he comes right off of IR and back onto the 53-man roster.
Maybe the Steelers are prepared to battle through three games with Germie Bernard and DK Metcalf being enough, and they simply view the addition of Valdes-Scantling as a better third option in a short span.
That would be great news for the Steelers, who finally found the light with Wilson this season. But it's not the only good sign for Pittsburgh.
Now, things can change and the trade deadline is still far enough away that general manager Omar Khan can go out and still make a splash move, whether that's a trade or a signing. But the addition of Valdes-Scantling certainly tells you that rookie Bernard is going to get the first opportunity to remain the focal point of the passing attack.
Both Bernard and Metcalf caught 11 passes in the team's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5, and look like the 1-2 punch Pittsburgh has been looking for.
Giving Valdes-Scantling the call over names like Tyreek Hill or maybe trades like Brian Thomas Jr. shows that this team has its two top options. They're simply looking for a rotational player who can help more than the ones they already have.
Again, great news for the Steelers, who have been searching high and low for a player of Bernard's caliber to walk into their wide receiver room in the last few years.
So, while disappointing to some, the Valdes-Scantling move might be good news for the Steelers. And while it's not splashy, this team may believe in what they have, and what they're going to get back, enough to push through some hard times.
That's a great indication that they've come a long way in their receiver options. Something every fan is thrilled to see.

title: Steelers' Jalen Ramsey Is Not the Same Player Anymore - And That's Great News
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey is not the same player he used to be. He's not even the same player he was when he first arrived in Pittsburgh before the 2025 season.
When the Steelers acquired Ramsey from the Miami Dolphins in the summer of '25, they anticipated getting a starting outside cornerback to pair with Joey Porter Jr. Instead, they landed a player who was still an excellent player, but wasn't quite fit for the role.
So far in 2026, however, Ramsey has arguably been the team's most impressive defensive player. Even more impressive is that he's achieving this in his newfound role as a hybrid safety and nickel cornerback. His game-sealing sack in overtime of Week 6 was the latest example of Ramsey making big plays for this defense.
It took some time, but it's clear now that Ramsey's transformation from All-Pro outside corner to an elite and versatile defensive back is complete.
Ramsey's play on the field speaks for itself this season. Through six games, he has 37 total tackles. He's recorded eight or more in a game three times so far this season, and 23 of his total tackles have been recorded individually. In addition, he has two sacks, two passes defended and a forced fumble.
Beyond his production on the field, Ramsey is undoubtedly one of the most respected voices within the organization. His winning pedigree and individual accomplishments set him apart from a majority of the defense, and it's clear that when he speaks, the team listens.
Ahead of their Week 5 contest against the Indianapolis Colts, Ramsey pointed out a slight "disconnect" between the players and coaching staff. He didn't mean it alarmingly, later clarifying his comments via social media. The problem, however, was that he was spot on. There was a disconnect between the players and staff.
That was rectified in Week 5, however. Defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, now down on the sidelines instead of in the booth on game days, was right alongside his players. As a result, the communication and performance improved. They allowed 332 yards to the Colts in Week 5, but limited them to just 22 points. In Week 6, they turned things up a notch, limiting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to just 224 yards and 19 points.
Over those two games, Ramsey recorded 19 total tackles, both of his sacks in 2026 and one pass defended. And he's done it all while recovering from a fractured wrist.
That's a veteran leading by example, not just by his words. He called for accountability on all sides, and everyone responded.
After the 2025 season, I would have called you nuts for suggesting that Ramsey could regain his All-Pro form. Even his Pro Bowl selection last year felt like an obligatory invitation more than one based on merit.
About to turn 32 years old and with over 150 games in his NFL career, it's fair to wonder how much he had left in the tank.
Ramsey is playing like an All-Pro defensive back. Call him a nickel cornerback, if you prefer. Call him a safety, if that feels more appropriate.
It doesn't really matter. What matters is that Ramsey is no longer the player he was when the Jacksonville Jaguars drafted him with the fifth overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft. The player he is now, however, is a versatile playmaker in the secondary. And it's exactly what this Steelers defense needed.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Re-Signing Aaron Rodgers' Former WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are reuniting with an old friend. According to The Athletic's Mike DeFabo, the black and gold and bringing back wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling as they try to help their depleted depth.
Valdes-Scantling spent part of the 2025 season with the Steelers, playing in five games with one start. He caught 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown while reconnecting with his former Green Bay Packers teammate, Aaron Rodgers.
Now, he's joining his former quarterback for one more season, and signing back to the Steelers as a midseason Hail Mary once again. However, unlike last year, Valdes-Scantling is looking to replace two injured starters instead of walking in as the team was desperate to find anyone who could produce.
Valdes-Scantling will sign to the team's practice squad, but his familiarity with the team and Rodgers should make him a quick call-up to the active roster.
The Steeles have placed wideouts Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on Injured Reserve over the last two weeks. Pittman Jr. is expected to miss a significant amount of time with his injury, while Wilson is hopeful to return shortly after his four-game milestone is complete.
Ben Skowronek missed Week 5 with a calf injury. It's unknown if he'll miss more time.
Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson were both called up from the practice squad in Week 5 to fill the gaps. Neither caught a pass, with Smith playing a very limited role offensively and Johnson being a last-resort for Pittsburgh.
So, they'll try to rebuild the group moving forward, and will start with the addition of Valdes-Scantling, who will now work alongside DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen in the wide receiver room.
The Steelers have two star players in Metcalf and Bernard. Both finished with 11 receptions in Week 5 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and are expected to remain the focal points of the team's passing attack moving forward.
Whenever called up to the active roster or used during game days, Valdes-Scantling steps into Pittsburgh's offense as a third option in the wide receiver room, and another addition to the passing game. Tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are amongst the top weapons for Rodgers at the moment, and Valdes-Scantling will likely fill in behind or within that group.
Once Wilson returns from IR, Valdes-Scantling may take a back seat to the third-year speedster and become the fourth wideout option, and possibly fifth behind Skowronek when he returns.
For now, though, he's a player who can spread the field and who brings plenty of speed and comfort with Rodgers. The two combined for over 2,000 yards and 10 touchdowns during their time in Green Bay together, and will look to have that chemistry again in Rodgers' final season.
Expect Valdes-Scantling to be the last wide receiver move for now . This team may continue to search for options near the trade deadline, but they'll likely give Valdes-Scantling a shot to fill the hole and prove his worth for a second season.
If he does, they will probably wait until Wilson returns from IR and settle with what they have currently at the position.

title: Steelers' Paris Plan: Travel Arrangements, NFL's Statement
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are very much aware of the protests that are currently ongoing in France and have a plan in place as they get set to face the New Orleans Saints in Paris in Week 7.
During his weekly press conference, head coach Mike McCarthy noted that the Steelers conducted a Zoom call with the league office, which is typical protocol for international games, and that the organization is confident in its plan as it heads overseas.
“I'm obviously very aware, that’s part or the normal planning anytime you go abroad," McCarthy said. "The team is excited about playing over there….we had a Zoom call today with the league office, that’s normal protocol. We have a lot of confidence in our plan.”
A string of anti-government protests have taken place throughout France recently.
According to USA Today , more than 2,000 people were arrested in the country for their roles in riots that ultimately became violent over the weekend.
The protests first began when high school and university students were seeking more funding from the French government for education while also wanting better conditions in schools.
Other groups later joined in, including labor unions, farmers and other workers' groups (as noted by USA Today).
The rising cost of living in France has also been a central topic within the protests.
The NFL put out a statement this past weekend, which noted that preparations for the meeting between the Steelers and Saints at Stade de France remain ongoing while the league works with local authorities to ensure all operational and security matters are properly tended to.
"Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said, per ESPN's Katherine Terrell . "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
Coming off a comeback 26-19 victory on the road over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime, Pittsburgh is now sitting at 4-2 and in a three-way atop the AFC North .
The Cleveland Browns hold a three-way tiebreaker over the Steelers and Baltimore Ravens, however, as they are 2-0 in the division while Pittsburgh is 1-1 and Baltimore is 0-1 after falling to Cleveland this past weekend.
As the Steelers look to build on their two-game win streak, they won't head over to France until later in the week, on Thursday, October 22. New Orleans, meanwhile, has already landed in Paris.
Pittsburgh followed the same plan ahead of its contest in Dublin, Ireland last season against the Minnesota Vikings, and it paid off with a 24-21 victory at Croke Park.
McCarthy explained that the Steelers' decision to hold off on heading to France for a few days came down to attempting to keep the entire process as normal as possible for the team while giving themselves the best odds of coming away with a win.
“Just like anything, when the schedule comes out we’re on a 7-day week flow here," McCarthy said. "Played yesterday in Tampa, had to travel back, so that factors into it... Whether you’re playing in the Super Bowl or you're playing in a Monday night game, you look at all of those things and the reality of it is I've always tried to stick to the basics. The hydration, the sleep, just to give the men the best opportunity to prepare and perform while staying in the normal flow of operation as possible."
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Most Important Defenders Emerge in Week 6 Victory
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers can be described in many ways - unpolished, frustrating, dizzying - among others.
But what you can’t use to describe the Steelers is the word ”loser.” Pittsburgh went into Raymond James Stadium and took down the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, giving the Steelers their first road victory under new head coach Mike McCarthy.
Three quarters of the win were downright ugly. They entered the final 15 minutes down 16-3 with little hope, but exited with a 26-19 win. While this game is largely one they want to move on from, the one thing they can’t ignore is how much this defense lives and dies by two unexpected players.
The Steelers are now 4-2 , and it’s all thanks to the play of veteran duo Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean. It’s clear now that the Steelers' defense goes the way of their championship-winning tandem.
What an absolute masterpiece of a performance from defensive back Jalen Ramsey. It’s been clear all season long that the former All-Pro and Super Bowl winner has a chip on his shoulder, and his performance in Week 6 was a thing of beauty.
He posted 10 total tackles, including four tackles for loss and two sacks. His second sack of the game was a victory-sealing play for the Steelers, yet another example of Ramsey taking care of business for the Pittsburgh defense.
Ramsey is turning back the clock in 2026. Playing through a fractured wrist, he’s been the team’s best defender. Through six games, he has 37 total tackles, two sacks, two passes defended and a forced fumble. He’s making an impact at every level of the defense, and it’s leading the Steelers to wins they desperately need.
After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys, the biggest question that emerged was how this secondary could take a step forward in pass coverage without their top cornerback.
The answer apparently was just waiting to get back on the field after missing Week 5. Dean was picture-perfect in his return to Tampa Bay. He recorded six passes defended and his first interception with the Steelers. He nearly took the interception back for a touchdown, only to be stopped at the 3-yard line by Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels.
It wasn’t just that Dean was unbeatable in coverage, it was how clutch his performance was. That fourth quarter interception put the Steelers in front of the Bucs late in regulation. The offense failed to fully capitalize, but Dean took advantage of a rookie quarterback’s mistake at the perfect time.
That’s what the Steelers have been missing. They’ve long had their outside linebackers creating splash plays and carrying the team to victory, but it hasn’t been enough. The Steelers also needed their secondary to prove they can steal a game for the team.
That finally happened in Week 6, thanks to Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey. And if it wasn’t abundantly clear before, this defense starts and stops with its veteran tandem in the secondary.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Where Steelers Stand in AFC North After Huge Comeback Win
full_text:
It wasn't easy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers mounted a 13-point comeback in the fourth quarter and defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime in Week 6 to move to 4-2 on the season.
After the game, Aaron Rodgers talked about how the victory may ultimately change the Steelers ' trajectory since it was a game they had to have in order to avoid being .500 at 3-3 heading into an international matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Paris during Week 7.
“The thing is, these are the most important moments for us as a team to grow. Because this is a trajectory-altering win today,” Rodgers said. “To go 3-3, we’ve got the Paris trip, that’s just not what you want to do.”
After capturing its first road win of the season, where does Pittsburgh sit in the AFC North standings?
The Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns faced off at Huntington Bank Field, though two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson was out for a second straight week for the former with an ankle injury.
Tyler "Snoop" Huntley started in Jackson's place for the 4-1 Ravens, and while he led the team to a win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5, that wasn't the case this time around.
Cleveland made up a seven-point difference in the fourth quarter and won as time expired on a 37-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt, moving it to 4-2 while Baltimore dropped to 4-2.
As a result, the Steelers , Ravens and Browns are all technically tied atop the division, while the Cincinnati Bengals, who were on bye, are a half-game behind at 3-2.
Because Cleveland is 2-0 in the AFC North, it holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh (1-1 in division) and Baltimore (0-1) at the moment.
"Cleveland won today, so now the three of us are 4-2...," Rodgers said. "To be 4-2 now, to win our first road game, to beat a team we should've beat. There's no two-ways around it, you gotta beat teams like that if you want to get where we want to get. Didn't look like a win for a long time, so I'm proud of our guys. Defense kept us in it, and offense finally made a couple plays."
It's shaping up to be quite the race down the stretch, and it's starting to feel a bit like 2023, when all four teams in the division finished over .500.
As Rodgers alluded to, the Steelers couldn't afford to let their game against Tampa Bay slip through their fingers. With the Bucs at 1-4 heading into it while having an undrafted rookie starting at quarterback in Jalon Daniels, those are the types of situations Pittsburgh has to take full advantage of if it wants to remain in playoff contention.
Now, the Steelers have to find a way to take down another NFC South squad in the Saints, who are 2-4, over in Paris this week before heading back to Acrisure Stadium and playing the Browns in Week 8.
The Cleveland contest in particular is crucial because of the AFC North ramifications, though New Orleans is one of the easier matchups left on Pittsburgh's schedule and is another opponent the black and gold must defeat before things really ramp up following their Week 9 bye.
From a Sunday Night Football showdown with the Bengals on the road in Week 10 to a Black Friday matinee at home against the Denver Broncos in Week 11 before hosting the Houston Texans on Sunday Night Football in Week 12 and hitting the road for Monday Night Football vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 13, the Steelers will face an absolute gauntlet of opponents immediately coming out of their bye.
That doesn't take into account the two contests it has against the Ravens in Weeks 15 (home) and 18 (road) either.
As a result, Pittsburgh would really benefit from stacking wins over New Orleans and Cleveland as a means of protecting itself against a pretty brutal stretch in the second half of its schedule.

title: Steelers' Germie Bernard Sets New Aaron Rodgers Record
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Germie Bernard has as much synergy with Aaron Rodgers as any other first-year wide receiver throughout the future Hall of Famer's career.
According to CBS' broadcast of the Steelers' 26-19 comeback overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Bernard's 11 receptions is the new single-game record for a rookie from Rodgers. It's also the most for any rookie in one contest in franchise history.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list while Ben Skowronek (calf) was also inactive vs. Tampa Bay, Bernard's been thrown into a starting role by Pittsburgh and has passed that test with flying colors up to this point.
Bernard's outing got off to a bit of a adverse start.
Rodgers found Bernard on a 4th-and-3 from the Buccaneers' 42-yard line with a little under four minutes remaining in the first quarter. Bernard was already past the line to gain upon catching the ball, though he ran backward and was ultimately spotted short of a first down.
Germie Bernard moved backwards on his own after making the catch, before any contact from the defender. As a result, the ball was correctly spotted short of the first-down marker. #PITvsTB pic.twitter.com/SjXVFxYt53
Instead of Rodgers' confidence in Bernard dropping or the rookie letting that situation get in his head, however, he quickly put that moment behind him and went to work.
Emerging as a favorite target of Rodgers and somewhat of a safety blanket over the past two games in particular, Bernard was consistently open and hauled in just about everything thrown his way all over the field.
The final product was an 87-yard performance on his aforementioned 11 catches, which included a six-yard touchdown in overtime that was ultimately the game-winner.
When Bernard played a combined 48 snaps in the three games DK Metcalf, Pittman Jr. and Wilson have played together (Weeks 1, 2 and 4) and had just three receptions for 25 yards over that span, no one really batted an eye.
After all, it's always taken Rodgers a while to warm up to rookie receivers throughout his career. Furthermore, the 42-year-old stated, "I think you need to temper expectations for sure with Germie," on Cam Heyward's "Not Just Football" podcast in September.
It's apparent that Rodgers has taken a liking to Bernard during their time together, though, even before his breakout the last two weeks.
After the Alabama product logged four catches for 35 yards in a Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots while Pittman Jr. sat out with a foot injury, Rodgers told reporters that even though "there was stuff to clean up," he was "really pleased" with Bernard.
As is the case with any rookie, there are still aspects of Bernard's game that he has to clean up long-term. That much was clear with his blunder on fourth down against the Bucs.
At the same time, he is way ahead of schedule and producing at a borderline star level for Pittsburgh, not even halfway into his first season in the NFL.
Bernard has already shown that he has both a high floor and ceiling, and there's still plenty of room for him to grow.
"There comes a time when the confidence starts to match the potential, and I think we're reaching that time with Germie," Rodgers said after the Steelers' win over Tampa Bay. "Very proud of him."
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Mike McCarthy Nearly Cost Steelers a Win
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers continued their disappointing trend to begin the 2026 season, performing poorly on the road for a third straight game to start their first campaign under a new head coach.
The Steelers’ 1-2 record away from Acrisure Stadium can be dealt with. Lots of teams deal with this type of situation year in and year out.
But one piece of this remains unaddressed and unresolved, like a ghost in the attic that refuses to depart. Once again, a coaching blunder cost the Steelers a victory in regulation. They got the win in overtime, but it could have been done earlier. Through the first six weeks of the season, Mike McCarthy is guiding this team to wins, but he's failing to live up to many of his training camp words.
A huge component of training camp was these supposed high-intensity moments during practice sessions. Wherever players were, when a certain signal occurred, everyone went to the main field for some type of truncated high-stress situation. Most of the focus was on two-minute drills and red zone opportunities.
The goal was to get this team ready for the adversity and tough moments an NFL game brings. McCarthy dubbed them “Franco Moments” at camp.
The Steelers had a golden opportunity to take what they focused on at camp and put it into action. With less than two minutes left in their Week 6 contest, the Steelers’ defense forced a turnover and gave the offense the ball inside the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ 5-yard line.
The strategy is rather simple in this scenario. The goal is to run out the clock while putting up points. That usually translates into a couple of handoffs with plenty of time in between snaps.
So, what did the Steelers do? They ran a play-action pass on first down, followed that up with a handoff to Jaylen Warren for a yard, and then went back to the pass on third down. Both passing attempts were incomplete, stopping the clock each time. The Steelers ended the drive with a field goal and the lead, but it left ample time for the Bucs to get into field goal range.
Asked after the game about what his considerations were when the offense took the field for that drive, McCarthy's answer was less than illuminating.
"Absolutely. You're talking clock. The first down, it was a boot," he said. "Then the second down, the run, we caught them with 10 on the field, so you know, it was a substitution and all of those things, but definitely was aware of the clock there."
Even quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have pointed out some of the blunders in his postgame press conference. The offense was stagnant for three quarters before coming to life in the final frames.
Part of the reason they struggled was the lack of tempo on offense. Despite showing some signs early in the game, Rodgers felt like they moved away from that strategy, and it cost them at different points in the game.
"You got to give credit to the defense. They kept us in it. There were a lot of opportunities for that game to get out of hand, especially at 13- 3," he said after the game. "They held them to a field goal, and we sputtered along there for a little bit, and then we kind of opened things up with some quicker stuff, on–the–ball stuff. Felt like we got into a rhythm there. Especially in the first half, and then we kind of went away from it in the third quarter, kind of went back to it in the fourth quarter, and moved the ball pretty efficiently at that point."
Okay, so you don't take as much time off the clock as you wanted to. That's not the end of the world. The Steelers had the chance to stonewall the Bucs before they tied the game up.
The defense failed. They gave up a big play immediately that brought the Bucs into field goal range.
But McCarthy's blunder came with how he managed the clock. With roughly 30 seconds left on the clock, the Bucs trotted their field goal unit onto the field. Instead of immediately calling timeout and stopping the clock, he allowed it to run down to 13 seconds before the officials stopped the game clock.
After the game, he chalked it up to a miscommunication between himself and the officials.
"Yeah, there was some miscommunication there," he admitted. "We were thinking right away (of calling timeout) there at 34, 35 (seconds). Then there was just some miscommunication between the referee and I. So, that's why it went down as low as it did. But, ultimately, it worked out."
Yes, it did work out for the Steelers. But only in spite of the decisions their head coach made.
The team did what McCarthy asked coming out of Week 5. The team stacked victories and improved to 4-2. They also stacked coaching blunders, which should be as concerning as the back-to-back wins.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers WR Search Heating Up: What It Means
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are well aware of the wide receiver issue plaguing their offense right now. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson both on the Injured Reserve, the offense has just two reliable targets for quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
Even though the Steelers made the most of things with a gutsy win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, the organization knows it cannot continue with this roster of receivers for the remainder of 2026.
Apparently, the organization isn't just sulking over the issue, they are actively trying to address it. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Steelers are "calling around" to upgrade their wide receiver room. On a recent update on his Substack page, The Sweep with Tom Pelissero , general manager Omar Khan is inquiring around the league, and two names, Jalen Tolbert and KaVontae Turpin, have some immediate ties to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy.
"Jalen Tolbert and KaVontae Turpin are the two guys with connections to Mike (McCarthy) that are on rosters now and know his offense," he wrote. "But I haven’t heard of anything on either front. I do know the Steelers have been calling around on veteran wide receivers since the injuries last week and I’d imagine that continues with two WR on IR."
Both of these names are being thrown out there because of their ties to McCarthy, and that makes sense. During his time as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys, both Tolbert and Turpin enjoyed career-best performances.
During the 2024 season, McCarthy's final year in Dallas, Tolbert produced in an anomalistic way. Over 17 games, he hauled in 49 receptions for 610 yards and seven touchdowns.
While Turpin didn't reach the same heights as Tolbert, he still had career-high numbers under McCarthy. During that same 2024 campaign, Turpin 31 receptions for 420 yards and two scores.
It's true that both receivers put up respectable numbers under McCarthy, and expecting either veteran to come to Pittsburgh and be a decent player is reasonable. It's not a guarantee, however.
Tolbert is the perfect example. Outside of his 610-yard season in 2024, he's never exceeded 300 receiving yards in a season. Now in his fifth year in the NFL, his ceiling is concretely set as a bottom-of-the-depth-chart player.
Turpin was slightly more productive after McCarthy's departure. In 2025, he posted just under 400 receiving yards and two more touchdowns. Still, it's the same type of production that Tolbert delivered.
The problem is that it doesn't solve the issue for the Steelers. Depth is wonderful and sorely needed for this injury-riddled squad, but it doesn't solve their problems. If anything, it continues them. Both veterans are solid, unexciting options that would only add to the sea of averageness taking up the Pittsburgh depth chart.
If the Steelers are truly trying to upgrade, they have to get creative and accept that it comes with a cost. That remains unlikely to be the case, so low-priced veterans are the route they will go.
But unless the Steelers want to give up a high draft pick to make a deal, they won't be getting that number one or two receiver to strengthen the position.
That leaves players like Tolbert and Turpin. Free agents like Marquez Valdes-Scantling. That leaves practice squad players like KJ Osborn and Xavier Gipson.
The Steelers are looking for receivers, that's certainly clear. It's just a matter of where they are looking that remains to be seen.

title: 5 Winners, 3 Losers From Steelers Comeback Win Over Bucs
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers looked out of sync for most of their Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Then the fourth quarter happened.
Down 13 points with just under 14 minutes left in the game, the Steelers fought their way back into it and even took a 19-16 lead with 1:21 left before Tampa Bay sent it into overtime.
From there, Pittsburgh drove 70 yards down the field and put seven points up on the board courtesy of Germie Bernard's first career touchdown.
The Steelers' defense turned the Buccaneers over on downs on the ensuing possession, moving them to 4-2 on the year heading into a Week 7 meeting with the New Orleans Saints in Paris.
With that, here are our winners and losers from Pittsburgh's comeback victory on the road.
After missing the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury, Dean was a hero in his return to Tampa Bay.
Facing the team that he won a Super Bowl with and spent the first seven seasons of his career playing for, Dean picked off Jalon Daniels with just under two minutes left in the contest while it was tied up at 16-16.
That set up Pittsburgh at the Buccaneers' three-yard line, and while it didn't punch the ball into the end zone, Chris Boswell made a 20-yard field goal that put the black and gold ahead before Tampa Bay sent the game into overtime.
Dean also posted six passes defended, per ESPN .
Watt has cooled down rather significantly over the past few weeks.
After recording 4.5 sacks through Week 4, he failed to record a single stat over 51 snaps vs. Indianapolis.
Then, against the Buccaneers, Watt had just two pressures across 37 pass rushing reps (per SumerSports ). He remains an elite run defender, but the Steelers simply need far more production from him.
Ramsey showed up in a big way for a Steelers secondary that had a bounce-back performance across the board.
He was all over the field vs. Tampa Bay, recording two sacks (including one on the last play of the game) and constantly getting into the backfield against the run, as evidenced by his four tackles for loss.
Ramsey also had the second-most tackles for Pittsburgh with 10, which was one less than Payton Wilson's total.
Iheanachor, after a dominant outing against the Colts last week, had a rough showing in this one.
Per SumerSports , the first-round right tackle gave up a sack to David Walker while also allowing four total pressures.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list while Ben Skowronek (calf) was inactive for this contest, Bernard stepped up for a second-straight week.
Aaron Rodgers could've lost some faith in Bernard after running backwards on a 4th-and-3 and being short of the sticks in the first quarter despite initially having the first down, but he didn't.
Instead, Bernard logged 87 yards on 11 catches and scored what ultimately became the game-winning touchdown in overtime.
Much like Iheanachor, Fautanu had trouble holding up in pass protection.
The third-year left tackle's day looked strikingly similar to Iheanachor's from a statistical perspective too, as he also gave up four pressures and a sack to Walker (per SumerSports).
At long last, Herbig came alive as a pass rusher and notched his first two sacks of the season in this game.
The 24-year-old also had four total pressures (per SumerSports) and picked up three tackles for loss.
It took time for him to get going, but Metcalf came up clutch when Pittsburgh needed him the most.
He logged six receptions for 51 yards in the fourth quarter as the Steelers made up a 13-point difference while also hauling in a 16-yard pass on 3rd-and-13 in overtime that kept the drive alive and helped lead to Bernard's touchdown.
When it was all said and done, Metcalf closed out the day with 11 receptions (his most in a single game with Pittsburgh) for 93 yards.

title: Seahawks Face Big X-Factor in Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III
full_text:
When the Seattle Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7's edition of Sunday Night Football , most of the attention will be zeroed in on one player in particular.
Kenneth Walker III won Super Bowl MVP honors with the Seahawks back in February and is the NFL's leading rusher for the Chiefs. Eight months later, for the first time since leaving Seattle in free agency , Walker returns to Lumen Field for a chance to take on his former team.
This is a game that has been circled ever since the schedule came out in May, and the stage is set for one of the biggest rivalry games of the year.
Walker has picked up where he left off in the postseason for the Seahawks. So far this season, in his first five games with the Chiefs, he has run for over 70 yards in every matchup. Walker has found the end zone in four out of his five games, including a pair in each of the last two games, both of which were wins against divisional opponents. Through five weeks, Walker has 665 rushing yards and six touchdowns.
Walker leads the league in rushing yards and is only behind Jamir Gibbs (Detroit Lions), Javonte Williams (Dallas Cowboys), Jonathan Taylor (Indianapolis Colts), Derrick Henry (Baltimore Ravens), and Josh Allen (Buffalo Bills) in rushing touchdowns.
If there is anyone who knows Walker's rushing tendencies, it's the Seahawks' defensive line that went up against him in practice for the first four years of his career. So far this season, the Seahawks have allowed just 96 yards per game to opposing running backs, which ranks in the top 10 of the NFL. It's the best rush defense the Chiefs have faced this season, and it should test Walker more than he has been over the past couple of weeks.
Walker has added a lot of dynamism to the Chiefs' offense, and we haven't seen them face adversity quite yet. Kansas City has relied on Walker because he's been playing about as well as anyone in the NFL. If the Seahawks can find a way to silence him, or at least contain him to a normal production rate, Seattle could exit the matchup with a major win to get them back on track.
Kickoff between the Chiefs and Seahawks is scheduled for Sunday at 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

title: Mike Macdonald Explains Why Seahawks Lost vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are turning over a new page as they get ready for their Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football.
In order for the team to move forward, they have to be honest with themselves about what went wrong in their Week 6 loss against the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke with reporters and explained what he saw after looking at the game film over the weekend.
"Based off the game, where my frustration lied, I think we talked about this after the game, but just the identity of us and Seahawk football. That feeling wasn't there," Macdonald said via the team's website.
"You're frustrated but also without the facts and without the objectivity behind everything, so that's what makes the problem-solving process interesting. That's part of the reason we like being coaches is because that's part of our process. So I'm proud of the couple days work that we put in. I think we had some honest conversations, an honest process. I think we're definitely more aligned as a team than we were a few days ago and I'm excited about where we can go, honestly."
The Seahawks loss against the Broncos had the ingredients for a victory. The Seahawks outgained the Broncos, 353-168, and the team had 24 first downs compared to Denver's 13. Still, it came down to the fact that the Seahawks couldn't score enough points. A pair of Darnold interceptions late in the game ultimately cost the Seahawks a win, along with a fumble earlier in the contest.
That being said, in an overtime game, a number of things could have gone differently to trigger a different result, and everyone needs to be held accountable for their actions.
The Seahawks are looking forward to another week of practice, during which they will look to clean up the mistakes they've made over the last two weeks that have cost them a pair of potential wins.
If the Seahawks can get back on track and beat the undefeated Chiefs at home, it should set them back on the right track for the second half of the regular season.

title: Seahawks Face First Must-Win Scenario of 2026 vs. Chiefs
full_text:
Eight months after winning the second Super Bowl in franchise history, the Seattle Seahawks are at risk of their worst seven-game start of the Mike Macdonald era when they host the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.
The Chiefs come in at 5-0, while the Seahawks (3-3) have lost three of their last four games after a solid beginning to 2026. Seattle has not begun a season 3-4 since 2022, and they went on to win just nine games.
Macdonald and the Seahawks are in must-win territory, especially with all the other storylines circling the matchup.
Former Seahawks running back and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III is leading the NFL in rushing yards (665), even though the Chiefs have already had a bye week.
Walker is averaging 6.3 yards per carry in KC, while the Seahawks are averaging 3.9 as a team between their multiple running backs. That’s probably been the biggest hole on Seattle’s roster this season, after Walker and Zach Charbonnet were one of the best tandems in the league from 2022-25.
The common criticism, of course, has now been that the Seahawks shouldn’t have let Walker leave in free agency. That notion is misguided, however, as Walker said he knew “sometime during the season” that he would sign elsewhere in free agency. Walker signed with the Chiefs quickly after free agency began.
Should the Seahawks have worked harder to retain Walker? Probably, but we aren’t privy to every conversation that happened between the two sides.
Either way, Walker is thriving with his new team, and the Seahawks are struggling to run the ball without him and Charbonnet on the field. That’s where both sides stand.
So, with the stakes of falling to 3-4 on the line and the storylines that would emerge from Walker running all over the Seahawks’ defense on Sunday, Macdonald and Seattle must beat the Chiefs.
Two things are working against each other: Walker is averaging 133 rushing yards per game, and the Seahawks haven’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in 35 games — the longest such streak in the NFL.
The Seahawks have given up just 96 rushing yards per game this season, as their defense has continued to be one of the best units in the league. Now their former teammate will give them their toughest test of the 2026 season.
In the scope of the standings, Seattle has to try to keep pace with the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers (pending the result of Monday Night Football). They also need to stay ahead of the Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams, who are both 2-4.
Expectations were high heading into this season, coming off a championship, and those expectations haven’t changed. The Seahawks have to prove they are still better than their rivals and that they can win without Walker.

title: Seahawks Might Have Starting RG Back vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have designated right guard Anthony Bradford to return to practice , the team announced on Monday.
Bradford, who started all 17 games for the Seahawks in 2025, has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury. He was placed on injured reserve and forced to miss a minimum of four games, and he's now missed five.
When asked on Friday whether Bradford could return in Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said there is a "really good chance" that he could play.
"If he has a good week, he's going to play a significant amount, if not the whole game," Macdonald told reporters on Monday , shortly after the team announced his return. "It's exciting ... I'm really happy for AB, the way he's approached this injury ... I think he's a better version of himself than he was before he got injured."
Seattle has started Christian Haynes at right guard since Bradford was sidelined, but rookie fifth-round pick Beau Stephens has also rotated in and out on offense at that position.
Haynes has played 53% of the Seahawks' offensive snaps, while Stephens has played 39%. If Bradford returns, there's a good chance that he would return to seeing 100% of the Seahawks' workload at right guard, as Macdonald alluded to.
The hope is that the Seahawks could have some return to normalcy in their run game, but Bradford returning is far from a guarantee of making that happen. He has been a better run blocker throughout his career than a pass blocker, but Seattle's issues lie as much with the running backs as they do with the offensive line.
"AB's played really good football for us. He's a physical presence for us at right guard, both in run and pass, so we're excited to possibly get him back," Macdonald added on Monday.
Regardless, the major positive is that the Seahawks are getting back to a healthy state on offense. More stability up front will only help the offense get better and become more consistent, and the latter is probably the unit's biggest shortcoming so far this season.
Last time Bradford played in Week 1, the Seahawks averaged their highest yards per carry (4.4) of any game this season. That may or may not show up in Week 7 against the Chiefs.

title: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo Could Be Headed to IR After Latest Signings
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks signed tight end Josiah Deguara and fullback Jackson Acker to the practice squad on Monday, releasing running back Dontae McMillan and wide receiver Malick Meiga to make room for the additions.
Although the extent of the injury is still unknown, the signing of Deguara appears to be a direct result of the shoulder injury that tight end Elijah Arroyo suffered against the Denver Broncos on Thursday. What is known is that Arroyo will miss time, so the Seahawks needed options at tight end.
The major question now: How long will Arroyo be sidelined, and how will that impact the Seahawks' offense?
When Arroyo left the game against the Broncos, Seattle's medical team was helping support his shoulder as he went to the locker room. Arroyo didn't have pads on when he came back out of the locker room, essentially ruling him out immediately.
Deguara is a former 2020 third-round pick out of Cincinnati by the Green Bay Packers. Including the Packers, he has spent time with six NFL teams prior to the Seahawks and was most recently with the Philadelphia Eagles this season.
Arroyo was primarily in a receiving role for Seattle, though his usage wasn't high. The 2025 second-round pick has only played 22% of the offense's snaps this season and has one catch for 17 yards.
Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo is expected to miss time with a shoulder injury suffered Thursday, per sources. Still determining severity but could be an extended absence. Hence, the Deguara signing. https://t.co/T7obfSBC3r pic.twitter.com/rdPEFcWwar
That means Deguara doesn't have to fill a receiving role and is more likely to be used as an extra blocker if he's ever elevated from the practice squad. In six full seasons, Deguara has 53 catches for 471 yards and three touchdowns, with most of that coming in 2021.
Regardless of whether Arroyo heads to injured reserve or not, it's not a huge hit to the Seahawks' offense. The only tight end on the roster that sees heavy usage is AJ Barner, and Eric Saubert has been No. 2 at that position. This will just be a depth addition for the team, but it does suggest Arroyo will be out for an extended period of time.
We may also see more of former undrafted free agent Nick Kallerup, who has played 16% of the Seahawks' offensive snaps this season. Barner, Saubert and Kallerup will be the top-3 tight ends moving forward, most likely.

title: Seahawks Rookie Report: More Misses Than Hits After Week 6
full_text:
It is still early to decide if the Seattle Seahawks' 2026 NFL Draft is a miss, but injuries and inconsistent play says otherwise. It doesn't help that the Seahawks encountered a Super Bowl hangover and there are signs that players and coaches are measuring up to their season expectations. The 2026 Draft class had mild expectations to contribute, but even those mild expectations aren't being met.
​The Seahawks are now 3-3 and coming off a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football. Only one rookie from the 2026 NFL Draft class participated in the game and they took reps more than normally would. There is still hope for this class to get better, but it is showing flashes of the 2013 or 2019 draft classes.
​It might be too far-fetched to say that the Seahawks and the 12 should be feeling good about guard Beau Stephens, but he is the only rookie consistently seeing the field. Stephens took 30 offensive snaps for the Seahawks against the Broncos. He continues to split the first-string right guard spot along with Christian Haynes while Anthony Bradford remains out with knee and hip injuries .
​The Seahawks’ coaching staff likes that Stephens is getting meaningful reps. The problem is that he is still struggling to find some consistency against NFL-caliber talent. Stephens has an overall grade of 4 8 by Pro Football Focus , which ranks 69th out of 75 eligible guards.
There is a good chance that Bradford could return for the Seahawks for Week 7 at home versus the Kansas City Chiefs. This would likely cut Stephens’ reps to non-existent unless he plays on special teams, where he has only played a handful each game.
​The Seahawks added former undrafted running back Robert Henry Jr. from the Washington Commanders’ practice squad on Oct. 6. It was likely too soon to play him in the Week 5 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but there was a great opportunity for him to play in the game versus the Broncos. Instead, the Seahawks barely utilized the running game and had quarterback Sam Darnold drop back 56 times. Henry remains on the 53-man roster.
​Another undrafted rookie they acquired much later after the Draft, cornerback Avery Smith didn’t play in the game against the Broncos. He played 16 special teams snaps against the 49ers, where he accounted for three total tackles. When Irv Smith Jr. got off IR , he took Smith’s place on special teams coverage.
​Not much changes from the rookies that remain on the practice squad roster. There aren’t any moves from the nine rookies on the practice squad due to the short week in between the 49ers and the Broncos.
​Seattle’s first-round running back Jadarian Price missed his third consecutive game while he is on IR with a chest injury. He will miss the Week 7 home game versus the Kansas City Chiefs. Price will be eligible to come off IR after the game versus Kansas City, but there is no indication that he will be back by then.
​The Seahawks’ third-round pick in cornerback Julian Neal is also on IR due to a hamstring injury. Week 6 was the second consecutive game that Neal missed. He will miss the game versus the Chiefs and the Week 8 road game versus the Chicago Bears. Like Price, there is no full indication that he’ll be back after the four-game minimum.
​The Seahawks’ first rookie to be placed on IR was safety Bud Clark, who suffered a broken ankle during the second preseason game versus the Tennessee Titans. Clark would’ve had some starting experience for the Seahawks due to Ty Okada’s injury. If he were healthy, Clark would be a reliable and dynamic weapon on defense and a player utilized all across the defense.

title: Seahawks Silver Linings: The Weak Conference May Save Seattle
full_text:
Every fan of the Seattle Seahawks carried their own expectations into 2026, the year after a super bowl win. But I feel fairly safe saying that the team is falling short of almost all of them so far. 3-3, with losses to teams heavily limited by injuries, was not on the docket. But the circumstances of the National Football Conference are softening the blow.
First of all, drouth is a rare, but accepted, spelling variant for the word ‘drought’. But more importantly, there are two divisions in the NFC that might, and I mean might, have a single playoff-caliber team between them. They’ll send two at minimum, of course, but both the East and South seem highly unlikely to produce a wild card team.
I have no idea who is winning the East, but it’s starting to feel like whoever does it will have a losing record. Which of course means that everyone in the division will have a losing record, making a wild card improbable. The South might have a decent Carolina Panthers squad (I remain dubious), but everyone else looks critically flawed so far.
The NFC North, however, is compelling. The Vikings are 5-0 with one of the worst offenses in the league, so their success is undeniable but still somewhat fragile. The Packers have come back to life after a miserable start, but I’m still not entirely sold on them given how bad their offensive line and run defense has looked. We’ll come back to that one.
The Bears and Lions are in similar spots to me, two good offensive squads with no defense. However, the Bears have a chance to improve on that side of the ball (and are showing some signs of such in recent games), while the Lions have a soft schedule that could produce a top record even if they can’t stop a good offense. All four teams are a threat.
Where this really gets interesting is in the NFC West, where the Rams have completely bombed the first third of the season, and at this point must be considered a bad team. They can obviously improve, but their schedule has many speed bumps the rest of the way. If they’re not a wild card team (and the Cardinals aren’t either), then there’s no one else left.
So, even if you concede the division to the San Francisco 49ers, and you assume that Seattle’s struggles persist, there’s a pretty clear path to the postseason even at 10-7, or possibly 9-8. Remember, the North will beat up on each other, so the odds of all four teams making it in are pretty thin. And no one will want to see this Seahawk team in January, wild card or not.

title: Seahawks' Best and Worst Case Scenario Before Bye-Week in Week 11
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are in their unofficial mini-bye week after playing a Thursday Night Football game. The Seahawks are coming out of the game with a 3-3 overall record and have lost three of their last four games. They’ve officially matched the same number of losses from last season in only six games played. Among Seattle’s biggest problems are its poor run game, turnovers, quarterback Sam Darnold’s crucial interceptions during crunch time and improper player usage , mostly on offense.
​The good news is that the Seahawks have some extra time to prepare for the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs (5-0 as of Sunday morning). The bad news is they have a lot to fix up if they want to develop good habits to maintain and develop during their bye week. Three of the four teams Seattle will face before its bye-week in Week 11 are teams that entered Week 6 currently projected to make the playoffs.
​The Seahawks have 10 days to prepare for the Chiefs at home, while the Chiefs have six after their win over the Los Angeles Chargers. There will be time for the Seahawks to implement the new idea and adaptations from the Seahawks’ four games. The Seahawks are not only facing an undefeated team, but they are facing their former starting running back/Super Bowl LXI MVP Kenneth Walker III .
​The Seahawks could give Walker and the Chiefs one of their worst performances of the season while redefining their issues in the run game and their turnovers. This would then give the team momentum to prepare for the Week 8 road game versus the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football.
​The Seahawks would then go on a manageable run in Week 9 and 10 in a home game versus the Arizona Cardinals and at the Las Vegas Raiders. The Seahawks will be mentally ready for the Raiders, led by their head coach and former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak. There is a good chance that Seattle will be 6-4 or 7-3 if they manage to get the offense’s communication and utilization problems adjusted .
​Just as there is always hope, there is a chance that the Seahawks continue their self-destruction. The miscommunication between the offensive coaches and players might be too much for the team to recover. Even if the Seahawks implement some changes to their team, all of that could go to the back of their minds if the Chiefs find ways to make the Seahawks.
​If Darnold continues to go through his patterns of poor decision-making that lead to late-game turnovers, the offensive line continues to get pushed at the line of scrimmage, or if the running backs turn the ball over or show poor vision, the Seahawks’ offense will be limited. They will find rare scoring opportunities against any of the upcoming four teams.
​Seattle could easily lose the next two games and then win against Arizona before losing to Las Vegas. This would put the Seahawks at 4-6 going into the bye week before they face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers (as of Sunday) in Week 12. The ultimate worst-case scenario would be for Seattle to lose to Arizona as well, to go to 3-7, leaving the highly unlikely chance to make the playoffs.

title: The Next 4 Games Will Make or Break Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are losers of their last two games , but their toughest tests have yet to come.
The next four games for the Seahawks leading up to their bye will have a big impact on the rest of their season and whether they can return to the playoffs for a chance to repeat as Super Bowl champions. Here's a look at each of their next four games and a look at what they need to do to get past this gauntlet in their schedule.
The Chiefs are one of three remaining undefeated teams in the league, and they're coming to Seattle fresh off a 22-6 victory against the Los Angeles Chargers. They are playing a really strong brand of football, and the Seahawks are going to need to step up if they want to compete with them. This is a winnable game for Seattle, especially with it being at home, but they are going to have to limit their mistakes and play at a higher level than they have over the last two weeks.
Limiting former friend Kenneth Walker III will be the biggest challenge for them. If they can stop the run and keep the ball in their possession, the Seahawks should have a good chance to be the first team to beat the Chiefs this season.
The Seahawks tap off their three-game run of prime-time matchups at home against the Chicago Bears, who just got Caleb Williams back from injury. The Bears are one of the better teams in the NFC, with a 4-2 record through six games. Only the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers, who are both undefeated, have a better record than them.
The Bears have shown that they can pile on points, but they also have struggled at points during the year. This game will be a big test for the Seahawks to see whether they are still one of the better teams in the conference. It will come down to the little things, and there's a good chance this game could come down to the final play or possession.
This game is a must-win for the Seahawks, as it is a home divisional contest. They beat the Cardinals back in Week 2 in Arizona, but their upset against the Los Angeles Rams this week is a perfect example of how a trap game can come to fruition.
The Seahawks should be favored in this one, but they will have to take care of business to cap off their home stand.
This game, going into the bye week, is a crucial one for the Seahawks, but it also comes with a lot of storylines. Klint Kubiak was the Seahawks' offensive coordinator last season, and now he will have a chance to face off against his former team, which he helped lead to a Super Bowl. If anyone knows the Seahawks' personnel and preparation well enough to build a formidable game plan to try and beat them on the road, it's Kubiak and the Raiders.
This is a game that could go either way depending on which personnel are playing and whether the Seahawks can counteract the ways the Raiders will try and exploit their weaknesses.
