title: Seahawks See Shake Up in NFC West Standings in Week 6
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are part of a shakeup in the NFC West, even though they were sitting on the couch on Sunday watching the rest of the NFL's Week 6 action.
The Seahawks saw one of the biggest upsets of the season so far, as the Arizona Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in the only NFC West game of the day. Here's a look at the standings now after the matchup.
The Niners are the final team to suit up for Week 6 as they take on the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. They are one of just three undefeated teams in the NFL, alongside the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, who were on a bye this week.
The 49ers can extend their lead in the NFC West to three games if they find a way to beat the Commanders in the prime-time matchup.
The Seahawks have lost consecutive games for the first time since Weeks 16 and 17 of the 2024 season. The team has lost all three of their games by a combined eight points, which has sparked a lot of frustration in Seattle, especially when it comes to the offense.
Luckily for the Seahawks , they aren't the only ones struggling in the NFC West, as the Cardinals and Rams sit behind them in the standings, having only won 2 games this season.
The Cardinals have two wins this season, both on the road at SoFi Stadium. They beat the Los Angeles Chargers to open the season but then suffered a four-game losing streak, which included a Week 2 loss against the Seahawks in their home opener.
They returned to Los Angeles to face the Rams, where they pulled off an improbable victory as time expired when kicker Chad Ryland knocked down a 43-yard field goal to win the game.
Many considered the Rams to be a Super Bowl favorite going into the season, but the first six weeks of the year have been nothing short of a disappointment. Some of their losses come against strong teams, including the 49ers, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but dropping a game at home against the Cardinals when they were favored by more than a touchdown is a big red flag.
Now they find themselves 3.5 games behind the NFC West lead and have some catching up to do in the coming weeks.

title: The 49ers Can Breathe a Sigh of Relief After Mike Evans Injury Update
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers can breathe a sigh of relief knowing Mike Evans' injury status.
Evans played in his third consecutive game while dealing with injuries, but in the Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders, he was also battling Achilles soreness on top of his broken ribs.
He made three catches for 94 yards before limping off in the first half. San Francisco was up 23-3 before the threat of almost losing the game. He was so influential that the 49ers nearly picked up their first loss of the season.
Unlike when George Kittle tore his Achilles, it was evident in that matchup when he went down and was carted off. Evans walked back to the locker room after receiving a questionable-to-return designation, then was ruled out.
That looked somewhat positive, given how nasty and gruesome Achilles injuries are. Head coach Kyle Shanahan provided positive news on Evans after the 23-17 victory .
"It's something that he's had before," Shanahan said. "It's something that bothered him throughout the week. So, when you have Achilles tendonitis like he does, it kind of is what it is. It flared up tonight, and I hope he recovers throughout the week, but you don't think it's a long-term thing.
"But right now, it almost cost him this game and ended up costing him two quarters. Hopefully, he'll be able to play next week, but if not, we'll have to have the rest of the group step up, and hopefully, get him healed up by after the bye week."
It's a short turnaround on the schedule with the 49ers traveling east to face the Atlanta Falcons, Raheem Morris' former employer.
Shanahan expressed that Evans' judgement on his injury will give an indication on whether he features for Week 7, just before the bye week.
"I mean, if he can play, Mike's got a lot of experience on doing this stuff. Mike's pretty honest with us, too, and my life experience is with him over six games. If he says he's ready to go, I believe him," said Shanahan.
It's the best news possible that Evans' injury isn't worse. He's made an exceptional impact since joining, plus the 49ers are thin at wide reciever.
It would make sense for Evans to miss the Falcons matchup and then assess how he is after the bye week. But his importance these last few weeks shows he can play well despite being injured .

title: 49ers Stock Watch: 5 Players Falling After Week 6 Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders 23-17. While some players did perform well, there were a few reasons why the game was so close. Who on the 49ers saw their stock drop in the win?
Evans was on pace to be the biggest winner of the week before he left with what appeared to be a concerning Achilles injury. It is hard to knock a player for injuries. However, the one obvious concern facing the 13-year veteran was injury. So, when he has been in and out of the lineup all year and left Week 6 with a serious injury, it is hard to say it was not expected, or at least not a recognized concern coming into the game.
The 49ers held onto a six-point lead through the end of the game. Washington had two chances to take a lead with a touchdown. That was because Eddy Pineiro missed an extra point. Pinerio missed two extra points in the 49ers win over the Arizona Cardinals. Three missed extra points is a lot for one season, let alone the first third of the season. This has become a concern for the 49ers.
Cowing has been a poor punt returner. Early in the game, he muffed a punt and retreated into his end zone, giving the team poor field position. Cowing has also been the 49ers' third receiver for the past three weeks due to injury. He has nine yards on 71 routes run. It is hard to find a receiver as inefficient as Cowing this year. Once Christian Kirk is healthy, the team could release him.
Green came into the game with his stock as high as ever. However, the Commanders picked on him at times. Early in the game, Terry McLaurin burnt him on a missed assignment. He added a penalty as well. If McLaurin remained healthy, the 49ers might have been in trouble.
This can include his backup, Ashtyn Davis. Stout was picked on relentlessly in the Commanders' comeback. After giving up a touchdown that took the game from 23-10 to 23-17, the team appeared to have benched him for Davis. Davis was not helpful in ending the game. Blown coverages, missed sacks, and penalties were the name of the game. The slot was an issue.

title: 49ers Grades After 23-17 Win Over Commanders: Offense Stalls without Mike Evans
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just beat the Washington Commanders 23-17. Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy was great in the first half when he completed 17 of 22 passes and posted a 122.2 passer rating. Then, Mike Evans went down with an aggravated Achilles injury. And suddenly, Purdy fell apart. In the second half, he completed just 4 of 7 passes and took two sacks. Without Evans, he didn't look like the MVP. To be fair, his remaining wide receivers were Brandon Cooks, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing. But Purdy still had Hall of Famers at tight end, running back, left tackle and perhaps play caller, and finished the game with three consecutive three-and-outs. Meanwhile, Jayden Daniels outplayed Purdy while working with Stefon Diggs, Rachaad White, Treylon Burks, and a 31-year-old rookie offensive coordinator. Suddenly, it seems like the 49ers' MVP is Evans, not Purdy. More on Evans in a minute.
Christian McCaffrey scored two touchdowns, but also lost a fumble and averaged a pedestrian 4.0 yards per carry and just 5.9 yards per catch. He's still a solid player, but he's not a big-play guy anymore. His longest catch of the game went for 13 yards, and his longest run went for 9. Frankly, he looked better last week when Kyle Juszczyk was out. This week, Juszczyk returned, and McCaffrey's productivity suffered. Odd.
George Kittle was great in the first half when the Commanders defense was focused on stopping Mike Evans. Then, Evans went down, and Kittle made a nice 35-yard catch when he was wide open on the first drive of the third quarter, then he never caught another pass. With Evans out of the game, the Commanders were able to shut down Kittle and force Purdy to look elsewhere, which resulted in Purdy taking painful sacks. Kittle is great, but he can't carry this offense by himself. He needs help from the wide receivers.
Mike Evans had three catches for 94 yards in fewer than two full quarters of action -- he's such a great player when he's healthy. Unfortunately for the 49ers, he aggravated his Achilles tendinitis and left the game before halftime. And without him, the offense fell apart. Brandon Cooks and Jordan Watkins each caught just one pass, and Jacob Cowing caught none. Without Evans, the 49ers might have the worst wide-receiver corps in the league. They need to trade for one immediately. They can't rely on Evans to get healthy and stay healthy this season. He has been playing through injuries since early August.
The 49ers ran the ball decently, but gave up two sacks. Still, the offensive line wasn't the problem.
They sacked Jayden Daniels four times and limited the Commanders to just 3.1 yards per carry. Granted, the Commanders were missing their starting running back. Still, the 49ers defensive line played exceptionally well without their highest-paid player, Nick Bosa. But in the second half, the pass rush got tired when the offense kept going three-and-out, which is understandable. This group needs some help from the offense.
Rookie Jaden Dugger had a team-high 11 tackles filling in for the suspended Dre Greenlaw, and Fred Warner had 8 tackles. I thought Greenlaw's absence would hurt the defense, but it didn't. Dugger has been a revelation.
The cornerbacks weren't good. Renardo Green got exposed and picked on, Deommodore Lenoir gave up a touchdown catch to a running back, Upton Stout gave up a touchdown catch to Stefon Diggs then left the game with a shoulder injury, Ashtyn Davis replaced him and was the worst player on the field. Fortunately for the 49ers, safety Malik Mustapha was one of the best players on the field, and he helped seal the win with multiple big plays late in the fourth quarter. To think that the 49ers had him on the bench until Marques Sigle got injured.
Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point. He misses a kick almost every week. If he keeps this up, he's going to cost the 49ers a game when it really matters. He better figure it out. And the 49ers better replace Jacob Cowing at punt returner. He fielded a punt at his four-yard line -- a major no-no -- muffed it, then recovered it himself. Please get him off the field.
Raheem Morris gets credit for limiting the Commanders to just 17 points, but he couldn't do much to stop Jayden Daniels, who completed 73 percent of his passes and posted a quarterback rating of 110.4. Daniels is the first quarterback the 49ers have faced this season who can run and throw equally well, and they struggled against him. That's something to keep in mind if they make it to the Super Bowl and have to face Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen or Lamar Jackson.
On offense, Kyle Shanahan made things look easy in the first half until Evans went down. After that, he didn't seem so creative. He kept calling long-developing play-action passes on first and second down that resulted in sacks. Considering he had a 20-point second-half lead, he should have been calling runs and quick, safe passes, but this is Shanahan we're talking about. He specializes in passing when he should run while leading late in games -- that's how he lost all three Super Bowls. Tonight, he almost blew a 23-3 lead. Only he can do that.
In addition, Shanahan let Evans play through Achilles tendinitis, and he made it worse. Now, Evans could miss some time that he might not have missed had Shanahan simply not played Evans in this game. Instead, Shanahan let Evans decide whether to play, so of course Evans made the wrong decision. Can you blame him? He's a professional athlete and a competitor. He's not going to shut himself down. That's the head coach's job. Hopefully, this coaching blunder won't cost Evans multiple games, because the 49ers clearly struggle without him.

title: 8 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 6 Win Over Commanders
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers almost fumbled the game away, but pulled through with the 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders . Let's dive into the eight biggest takeaways from the 49ers' Week 6 win.
With the 49ers' defense on its heels and the game on the line with a little more than two minutes left, Malik Mustapha stepped up. It started with a crucial run-stop on third down.
He came in with ruthless aggression to halt running back Jeremy McNichols in his tracks. You would've thought it was Dre Greenlaw who delivered the massive hit.
The very next play, Mustapha broke up a touchdown pass to Treylon Burks, who hauled in the catch, but thanks to Mustapha's physicality, the ball popped out when Burks hit the ground.
He had two primetime opportunities in front of him and capitalized on them. Mustapha treated those pressured moments as if he had been waiting all game for them. What a playmaker.
The main reason the 49ers' defense was on its heels and needed Mustapha to put his superhero cape on was that Kyle Shanahan got too pass-happy.
It started with the final play of the third quarter. Shanahan dialed up a play-action pass, leading to Brock Purdy being sacked for nine yards.
They couldn't save that drive after the sack. Shanahan proceeded to call three straight pass plays on their next possession, causing them to go three-and-out.
Rather than running the ball to settle the game down and drain the clock, Shanahan turned into Sean McVay and acted like the 49ers still had Mike Evans out there. He almost cost his team the game.
What a year Brock Purdy is having. He was sharp from start to finish in this game, despite cooling off in the second half when Evans left the game.
Purdy did what he had to in the second half and took care of the football. But his first-half performance was sensational. He looks so comfortable on every drop back.
He has also perfected his scrambling ability. He knows when to pick his spots to take off and run because every time he does, it leads to a sweet gain.
Purdy scrambled five times, tallying 28 yards. He looks like an incredibly balanced player who can deliver dimes and take off when he needs to. He's become a frustrating player to defend against.
Every week, the 49ers' offensive line continues to amaze me. They've already proved to their doubters that they aren't a terrible unit, as they were made out to be during the offseason.
But now they're proving that they cannot be disrupted. The groove that they're in is astonishing. Purdy has all day to throw and is barely pressured on his dropbacks.
The running lanes when they give it to Christian McCaffrey or rookie Kaelon Black are sizable, if not wide open. What a job they've been doing this season. They're elite.
It wasn't wise of the 49ers to play Evans in this game after he missed practice all week with an Achilles injury. Sure enough, he hurt his Achilles with a minute left in the first half after making a catch.
The 49ers ruled him out for the remainder of the game coming out of halftime, which is the right call. But now you have to wonder how much this has set Evans back, or worse, if it's a season-ending injury.
It feels like he won't play in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons, especially with the Bye Week to follow.  The 49ers must do what they can to keep Evans preserved.
If it wasn't concerning before, it definitely is now. Kicker Eddy Pineiro is a problem for the 49ers. He missed another extra point, making it official that he has the yips.
Pineiro was the reason the final two defensive series were so intense. A touchdown allowed wouldn't have tied the game. The Commanders would've most likely taken the lead with an extra point made.
Pineiro is a liability. Thankfully, the 49ers don't show any signs of slowing down or losing a game soon, but if they get into a tight game, Pineiro will likely be the reason they lose their first game of the season.
For the second consecutive game, the 49ers' pass rush was lethal. They got to Jayden Daniels four times and made him uncomfortable for the majority of the game.
This pass rush is becoming a force. It's a phenomenal development, as their defense was already solid without it. Plus, they're getting players to step up.
Now that it's continued to show life, it makes Nick Bosa's looming return a scary sight. If they were already heating up without Bosa, just imagine how it'll be with him.
What a year that defensive lineman Sebastian Valdez is having. Last week, he made his presence felt against the Seattle Seahawks by being disruptive and tallying a sack.
He did it again tonight against the Commanders. It felt like he popped off the screen on almost every defensive series. Whether it was against the run or the pass, he was making an impact.
Valdez has taken a nice leap this year, and boy, did the 49ers need that with their injury stockpile on the defensive line. Valdez has his stock rising, if not soaring, as a key role player.

title: 49ers Stock Watch: 5 Players Rising After Week 6 Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers beat the Washington Commanders 23-17 to improve to 6-0. Which players on the 49ers saw their stock rise the most in the win?
McCaffrey was still not overused, but this felt more like a vintage McCaffrey game. That is likely because of how impactful he was in the passing game. McCaffrey had nine receptions for 53 yards, both season highs. He also ground out 64 yards on the ground.  He averaged four yards per attempt. The offense ran through him in Week 6.
Williams was far more active and dynamic in Week 6. The team played him a good bit more after easing him back in the week prior. He recorded his first sack of the season and the second sack of his career. He was able to consistently create pressure and had a key deflection that was negated by a penalty. Still, he took a big step. If he can continue on this trajectory, the defensive line has a chance to improve.
Purdy continues to find ways to win. Games like tonight will improve his MVP case .  Mike Evans left the game with an injury. The 49ers entered the game without Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling, Christian Kirk, or Demarcus Robinson. Still, the 49ers quarterback continues to move the ball and produce. Purdy was 20-for-28 as a passer. He threw one touchdown and did not throw an interception. He added 28 rushing yards. These are the types of performances that will continue to keep his MVP campaign alive.
Mustapha has started the past two games, and he might not be giving the role back up. He was a game-changer in the 49ers Week 6 win. On the final drive, he made a key run stuff on third down and followed that up with a strong pass breakup on fourth down. He is a heavy hitter and always seems to be in the right place at the right time.
Dugger had been starting as the 49ers' SAM linebacker. However, with Dre Greenlaw and Garrett Wallow out, the team leaned on the rookie to be an every-down linebacker next to Fred Warner. Dugger added seven tackles, with four being run stops. He also added pressure. Greenlaw will likely be back next week. However, the team has to feel good about Dugger sliding into his starting spot next year.

title: How the 49ers are Already Week 6 Winners Before Playing the Commanders
full_text:
A chance at 6-0 is starting the San Francisco 49ers right in the face. All they need to do is take care of business at home on Monday Night Football against the Washington Commanders .
It's not a game that will challenge them much, given how lowly Washington is. They should be able to get the win and improve to 6-0 , remaining undefeated.
However, as the 49ers enter Monday night's matchup, they're already Week 6 winners before playing the Commanders. How is that possible, you may ask? I'll tell you.
The 49ers' two biggest and only threats in the NFC West, the Seattle Seahawks and the Los Angeles Rams, both lost this week.
The Seahawks were defeated by the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football, while the Rams were upset at home by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.
Seattle's record is 3-3, while Los Angeles' is 2-4.  The two powerhouses of the division are in a hole, with the 49ers above and beyond them.
This alone has made them winners of Week 6. They hold a sizable lead in the division over the Seahawks and the Rams, especially with wins over both.
The Seahawks might be able to rebound, as their loss was more justifiable. They went to Denver on a short week after being in an absolute war four days before that against the 49ers.
As for the Rams, they're in a complete freefall. They look like a team that heard all of the offseason hype about them and bought into it. What a bunch of fools.
The 49ers have a win in Week 6 already, and they haven't even played a game yet. That said, they can capitalize on this massive opportunity.
San Francisco can continue to separate themselves from the Seahawks and the Rams by defeating the Commanders on Monday night.
They mustn't let this chance squander. Now is the time for them to distance themselves further in case they go through a rough patch later in the season.
That way, this lead that they're creating now will be looked at as a major benefit. It will allow them to have room for error and absorb some losses if it comes down to it.
The NFC West is there for the taking for the 49ers. There's still a long way to go, but right now, the 49ers have everything going for them.

title: What it Would Take the 49ers to Trade for DeForest Buckner
full_text:
The 49ers need to find a team that's willing to trade a difference-making defensive tackle before the deadline, and they just might have found one.
The Indianapolis Colts are 2-4 after losing to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. After the game, Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner stood at his locker and answered questions, and he was so upset that his head seemed like it was going to explode.
"I'm pissed off, "Buckner said, "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every..." He paused for a second, choosing his next word carefully. Every day? Every week? Every month?
"Every year," Buckner said in a tone of cold condemnation . This comment made a Colts P.R. person uncomfortable, so he said, "a few more," trying to end the interview before Buckner said anything else that might go viral.
As you probably know, the 49ers drafted Buckner in 2016 and went to the Super Bowl with him in 2019. He was one of their best players. And yet, after they lost the Super Bowl to the Chiefs (the first time), they traded Buckner to the Colts so they could keep Arik Armstead and Jimmie Ward, neither of whom are on the team anymore. Now, the 49ers need Buckner back.
Their defensive line is an issue. Sure, it sacked Sam Darnold five times last week, but it lacks depth and a high-end closer. When the 49ers have a lead late in the game and the opponent has to pass to come back, the 49ers need someone who can sack the quarterback and end the game.
That player is supposed to be Nick Bosa, but he still hasn't fully recovered from this third ACL tear. He currently is out with a calf strain, which could be related to the knee injury. He still hasn't participated fully in practice yet this year, and he might not. It's unclear how he plans to manage his body.
Which means the 49ers have a choice. They could do nothing and simply hope that Bosa returns to full strength after the bye week, and stays healthy the rest of the season and plays like he did three years ago.
Or, the 49ers could be proactive and trade for a closing-caliber player on the defensive line. Someone such as Buckner.
Face it, they never should have traded Buckner in the first place. Trading Buckner for a first-round pick, which they spent on Javon Kinlaw, was one of the biggest blunders the 49ers have made in 10 years under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch. They've been trying to replace him ever since.
Meanwhile, Buckner still is one of the best defensive tackles in the league. You just wouldn't know it, because the Colts haven't won more than nine games in a season since he arrived in 2020. They wasted his prime.
Now, they might trade him. That's because they're going nowhere, he's 32, he'll be a free agent at the end of the season and they could save millions of dollars if they trade him before the deadline. Plus, they might as well get something for him as opposed to receiving nothing in return if he leaves in free agency, which he will. Just listen to him.
So, what would it cost the 49ers to trade for Buckner? Probably no more than a fourth-round pick. Most teams probably wouldn't want to give away picks for half a season of Buckner. The 49ers are different. They're the Super Bowl favorites, and their Super Bowl window is closing as their stars get older. They need to win this season, and they know it.
The 49ers just have to decide if defensive tackle is their biggest need. Given the emergence of Gracen Halton and Sebastian Valdez, and the lingering questions regarding Bosa's knee/calf, the 49ers could decide to trade that fourth-round pick for an edge rusher such as Khalil Mack instead.
Stay tuned. The 49ers almost certainly will do something big before the deadline.

title: 49ers Christian McCaffrey Plan Is Paying Off
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are getting a more efficient version of Christian McCaffrey in 2026 than they did in 2025. His yards per attempt is up from 3.9 to 4.7, and his success rate went from below 50% to 55.6% in 2026. One of the biggest reasons the team has been able to get a more efficient version of McCaffrey is that they are using him a bit less .
McCaffrey played 80% of the offensive snaps last season. He is only playing 69% of the snaps this year. What is most important is the manner in which they are able to rest him.
The 49ers have 26 short-yardage snaps . McCaffrey has played just 16 of them. They subbed him out for two goal-line snaps as well. Beyond that, when the 49ers have a multi-score lead, they find ways to rest him.
He has played just one snap in what is deemed garbage time. So, just taking 23 snaps and giving them back to McCaffrey would have him closer to 78% of the snaps. That is back in line with what he was doing last year.
The 49ers are able to sit McCaffrey more in these scenarios because they have faith in rookie Kaelon Black. Black is not producing impressive stats. Brian Robinson averaged 23 yards per game last year, and Black is at 27 yards per game this year.
Still, the difference is efficiency. Black has a 56% success rate on his carries this year. Robinson was at 46% last year. So, he was converting the short-yardage snaps into positive plays nearly s often. It made it harder for the 49ers to lean on the depth behind McCaffrey.
It took away from the efficiency of McCaffrey because he was being asked to do the dirty work. So, even when he was converting plays, it was not pretty and not for big gains. Then, he was worn down for the chances to hit the explosive.
Now, McCaffrey still plays in the two-minute drill and long downs and distances. When they need big plays, he is there, and he is well rested. The stats of Black and McCaffrey might not be as impressive from a volume perspective this year. However,the team is going to look much more efficient, and it could give them a higher ceiling heading into the playoffs.

title: Assessing the 49ers’ Management of Christian McCaffrey’s Workload
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers’ front office has repeatedly stated this season that it wants to monitor Christian McCaffrey’s workload.
It's five games into the new season, with three tough opponents in the form of the Seattle Seahawks, the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos.
This is a perfect time to assess whether McCaffrey's workload has made him better.
McCaffrey faced the most intense workload in his career in 2025. He had a career-high 311 carries and 102 receptions throughout the season. On the one hand, it's an impressive effort, as he went through the entire season without picking up any injuries.
That said, McCaffrey’s workload was way too excessive. He recorded the second-most carries in the league, while his average dropped to 3.9 yards per carry. Although that figure is not necessarily poor, it represents a significant decline from the 5.4 yards per carry he averaged during his 2023 Offensive Player of the Year season.
But compared to 2024, winning the Comeback Player of the Year award was completely deserved.
McCaffrey has only had 61 carries across five games this season, putting him on track for around or just over 200 for the season. Let's be honest, that's a massive reduction.
Credit to the 49ers for this. After drafting Kaelon Black in the third round this season, he's done well to remain healthy and help reduce McCaffrey's output. He's averaging 3.7 yards, which is a solid return from a rookie.
In truth, it's proven so far that they've made the right call. McCaffrey has averaged 4.7 yards per carry, with 286 rushing yards and has also recorded five touchdowns.
While many of those touchdowns have come from close range, McCaffrey has shown a noticeable improvement in explosiveness compared to last season.
The 49ers have also utilized him more heavily toward the end of games, which appears to be a smart approach to managing his workload while maximizing his impact when it matters most.
He's tied sixth in the league for touchdowns and 18th overall in rushing yards. Most of his explosive performances this season have been against tougher opponents, averaging 6.8 per carry against the Rams and 6.2 yards against the Seahawks.
So he's still a massively bright spark on that offense still, but he's simply being managed properly, which the front office to their credit have done very well.

title: The Buccaneers’ Sack Leader Is On The Bench, And That Has To Stop
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 1-5 on Sunday with a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, giving them sole possession of the worst record in the NFC. There have been a few reasons why Tampa Bay has fallen behind this season, and the pass rush is certainly one of them.
The Buccaneers rank 31st in pressure rate and 23rd in sack rate, per Sumersports. Their pass rush has been considerably lacking once again, despite bringing in two edge rushers in first-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. and free agent Al-Quadin Muhammad.
There's one edge rusher the Bucs have on the roster that has been shining, though. He's been getting an increased number of snaps every week because of his play — but should he be getting even more snaps than he is?
The Buccaneers drafted David Walker in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. He tore his ACL that year in training camp and did not play, so this year is his first bit of NFL action. And boy, is he making the most of it.
Walker has indisputably been Tampa Bay's best pass rusher this year so far. He has a 28% pressure rate on 50 snaps, with the next highest player on the team being linebacker Alex Anzalone at 10.4% — the next highest defensive lineman is Calijah Kancey at 10.1%, and the next highest edge rusher is Anthony Nelson at 7.1%.
Walker's snaps have been steadily increasing each game, and he had the third-most snaps of the team's edge rushers against the Pittsburgh Steelers. But there's a very good argument he should be starting for the Buccaneers, as the team's two starters, Bain and Yaya Diaby, both have a pressure rate of just 6.6% and have just one sack between the two of them.
Head coach Todd Bowles isn't quite ready to commit to Walker starting, though. When asked about Walker on Monday, he said that the amount of snaps Walker can get from game to game are gameplan dependent.
"Yeah, game plan-wise, we ramp it up every week – he's been playing that well," Bowles said. "We give him the plays we can give him, but it's been ramped up every week. Depending on the game plan and what the other team does and personnel-wise, you want to see him get more reps in there. We intend to do that, but sometimes it doesn't work out that way depending on the game."
The Bucs are 1-5 and are already on the brink of oblivion (if they aren't there already). A solid pass rush can be the difference-maker when it comes to beating teams, and Walker gives the Bucs the best chance to have one so far this season. He's been playing more and more every week, but at this point, with how much better he's been playing than anyone else in the edge room, he should be starting.
The Bucs will face off against the Carolina Panthers in a crucial division game next Sunday. When they do, it will be interesting to see how much participation Walker has in the game, especially after his performance against the Steelers in Week 6.

title: Mike Evans Explains Why He Left Buccaneers for 49ers in Free Agency
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 1-5 this season after dropping their most recent game to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. It's the first season they've played in 12 years without wide receiver Mike Evans, who became a franchise legend with the Bucs throughout his tenure in Tampa Bay.
Evans, though? He joined up with the San Francisco 49ers in free agency this offseason, and the move has certainly paid off so far. The 49ers are undefeated at 5-0 and Evans is producing, with 24 receptions for 326 yards and three touchdowns so far this year.
Evans recently spoke on the reason why he made his move to the 49ers, and while his comments about the Bucs aren't outwardly said, he certainly seemed to imply a few things about Tampa Bay and where it's at as an organization.
Evans said in an interview with KNBR that he feels "rejuvenated" by his time in San Francisco, but there are a few other things of note he talked about that are interesting.
“This team rejuvenated me and probably added a few more years to my career," Evans said, per the Tampa Bay Times' Rick Stroud. "They had everything I needed and checked every box. They’re trying to win now. The quarterback, great skill players, great defense, great coaching staff, and lastly, a great organization.”
The Bucs are not directly mentioned here. However, he says that the 49ers "had everything he needed and checked every box", and that San Francisco is "trying to win now" — it isn't hard to assume that Evans could be implying that Tampa Bay did not have those things at the time that he left the organization in the offseason.
There are plenty of reasons Evans could have left Tampa Bay. He was likely set to get a decreased target share with players like Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan on the roster. The 49ers had certainly been more successful over the long term than the Bucs were, and he'd simply played for the Bucs for a very long time and could have been looking for a change at the tail end of his career.
There certainly seemed to be a few things left unsaid in how he described the 49ers in this interview. But whatever the reason, Evans is not a Buccaneers player anymore. In his absence, Tampa Bay has failed to establish a true No. 1 wide receiver, and while the offense has a multitude of problems, they certainly have suffered for it.
The Bucs won't play the 49ers this season unless both teams make it to the playoffs. That's looking almost impossible for Tampa Bay right now, and they desperately need to win their upcoming Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers next Sunday to stay alive in the NFC South.
Evans and the 49ers will play an NFC South team of their own when they face the Atlanta Falcons on the road at 1 p.m. in Week 7.

title: Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Raymond James Stadium After Beating Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to the Pittsburgh Steelers 26-19 on Sunday, moving down to 1-5 on the year. The Bucs held the edge throughout the half, but the Steelers turned it around and gave Tampa Bay another close loss, this time in overtime.
The Steelers were led by quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who will go down as one of the best to ever play the game. Rodgers has played in Raymond James Stadium a few times over the years, and while this will almost certainly be the last time, he had a parting shot for the stadium in his post-game press conference.
Rodgers may have gotten the win, but he made his displeasure known about a certain aspect of playing football in Tampa Bay.
Rodgers told Steelers media after the game that he thought the playing surface at Raymond James Stadium is one of the worst in the NFL.
"It's gotta be one of the worst surfaces in the league," Rodgers said Sunday. "We're talking about player safety. I'm very thankful to not get hurt — I've gotten hurt twice on this field, in my opinion, because of this turf. I know USF plays here, I believe. That surface, you know, I don't think it's very safe."
#Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers calls out Raymond James Stadium for being “one of the worst surfaces in the league.” pic.twitter.com/Rc2eaJOGR3
The evidence from the last NFLPA report card backs up Rodgers' claim. In the anonymous survey, the Buccaneers' field was ranked F-, tied for worst in the NFL. Five teams earned an F- — three of them were turf, and the only other grass field was, ironically, the Steelers' Acrisure Stadium.
As Rodgers mentioned, USF playing its home games at the stadium the day before probably contributes in a big way to this problem. The turf also often hosts bowl games, too, so it gets a lot of use from teams that are not the Buccaneers.
Rodgers has played on that field at Raymond James Stadium seven times against the Buccaneers. He's 3-4 after his win on Sunday, and it will likely be the last time he ever plays in the stadium.
The Bucs won't be playing on that field next Sunday, as they'll play their first NFC South rivalry game of the year when they face off against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte.

title: The Best and Worst Position Groups in the Bucs' 26-19 Steelers Loss
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost another matchup, this time in overtime against the Pittsburgh Steelers. There was a lot of good and bad in this one, with certain groups doing much better than others.
Let's go over the grades for the Bucs' Week 6 loss:
It was a very rough game for Jalon Daniels. The Steelers knew how to rattle the rookie, and Daniels finished 22 of 43 passing for 164 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.
Daniels also had 39 rushing yards on the day and was sacked five times. One thing that won't show up on the stat sheets is the bad missed passes late in the game to open players like Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving.
After a great game against the Dallas Cowboys, Bucky Irving came back to earth in this game. Irving finished with 21 touches for 49 yards and zero touchdowns.
Kenny Gainwell didn't do much better with three touches for 24 yards, and we saw no opportunities for second-year back Josh Williams.
Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin combined for 24 targets today for 11 receptions, 85 yards and a single touchdown from Egbuka.
Ted Hurst also finished with three receptions for 40 yards as well. However, there were a couple of drops in this game with Egbuka, Godwin and Tez Johnson all having at least a single drop in this game.
The Bucs offensive line continues to struggle to protect the quarterback. That's not fully their fault, as the Steelers blitzed a ton that day. However, the team was not able to run block either in this matchup.
David Walker was an absolute star in this matchup and finished with seven total tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits.
We also saw A'Shawn Robinson get his second interception this season, which is absolutely insane. Rueben Bain Jr. got his first sack of the season and had the deflection on the pass that Robinson intercepted. Finally, you had other big contributions from guys like Yaya Diaby and Al-Quadin Muhammad.
Josiah Trotter looked good in this game, leading the defense with 12 total tackles and one pass deflection that should've been a pick-six for him.
Christian Rozeboom also had a great pass deflection in this game as well and has earned more playing time. Alex Anzalone, however, still missed multiple tackles in this game and was a bit of a liability towards the end of the game.
Zyon McCollum led the way for this group with 11 total tackles and one pass deflection. However, the star of the group was Keionte Scott, who had eight tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss and a quarterback hit.
Jacob Parrish was yet again solid with six tackles, one tackle for loss and two passes deflected.
The positive is that kicker Chase McLaughlin was awesome, making all of his kicks and keeping the Bucs alive going into overtime. The negative was that Riley Dixon was really bad in this game, and the team still needs to look at a new punter going forward. Yes, the game was windy, but it was not an issue for McLaughlin in this game, so I see it as no excuse for Dixon.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' OT Loss to the Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers came into this Week 6 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers knowing it was one they had to have. After going 0-4 to start the season, the Bucs were desperate to win consecutive games for the first time in over a year. Doing so would be a necessity to climb back up the standings in the NFC South.
Unfortunately, despite appearing to be in full control while holding a16-3 lead in the fourth quarter, the Buccaneers managed to squander a golden opportunity to turn their season around and fell to the Steelers at home in overtime, 26-19.
Let's take a closer look at the good, the bad, and the ugly that transpired in this demoralizing loss for the Buccaneers.
A'Shawn Robinson recorded his second sack of the interception in the first half of this game, and without checking the stats, I'd be confident in suggesting he is the only 300+ pound defender in the NFL leading his team in interceptions.
Beyond his role as a hefty ballhawk, Robinson's power, aggression and relentless style of play have been a welcome addition to Bowles' defensive line. Robinson has been one of the league's most impactful interior defenders so far this year, especially against the run, and his presence was felt again on Sunday.
Both David Walker and Rueben Bain Jr. recorded sacks for the Buccaneers in this game. For Bain, it was the first of his NFL career, and in addition to coming against a future Hall of Famer in Aaron Rodgers, it should feel like a weight lifted off his shoulders as everyone expected this milestone to come much earlier in his NFL career.
First-career sack for @ruebenbainjr 😡 📺: #PITvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/Q2Hta1d6FN
David Walker has been a menace whenever he's on the field for the Buccaneers this season. His two sacks today increased his season total to four, which leads the Buccaneers by a healthy margin. After missing his entire rookie year because of a torn ACL, this has been Walker's true rookie season, and the impact he's made despite limited opportunities has been outstanding. He has been the Bucs' best pass rusher throughout the first 6 weeks of the season, and it hasn't been particularly close.
David Walker records his second sack of the game, dropping Aaron Rodgers for a nine-yard loss. Walker's 4.0 sacks are tied (With Curt Jarvis) for the third-most by a Buccaneer through their first six career games since at least 1982.
McLaughlin was four-for-four on his field goals in this game, and he is now a perfect 14-for-14 on the season. McLaughlin has been one of the NFL's best kickers since joining the Buccaneers, and even though many of his teammates have not met expectations this season, that does not apply to him.
McLaughlin is a real weapon in the kicking game, and it's unfortunate his consistently exceptional performance is being wasted by an otherwise inept offense.
The Buccaneers led 16-3 at the half, and Daniels looked like the player we saw in Dallas on Thursday Night Football up until that point. Unfortunately, he looked like a completely different player as the game went on.
After halftime, Daniels was 8-for-20 passing with two interceptions. Not only was he throwing the ball to the Steelers, but he wasn't anywhere close on the passes intended for his own receivers for the majority of the second half and OT, air-mailing passes and missing receivers by several feet. Daniels finished the game 22-for-43 for 164 yards through the air.
The offensive collapse by the Buccaneers was largely because of Daniels' inability to execute, but his wide receivers got absolutely bullied by the Steelers DBs for the majority of the game. Former Buccaneer Jamel Dean looked like an All-Pro, and he was all over whichever Tampa Bay receiver he was covering at the time.
As good as both Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. have been in the past, neither player is explosive enough or consistent enough when it comes to creating the separation needed to be a team's No. 1 wide receiver. Life without Mike Evans is difficult for everyone in Tampa, and the Buccaneers' current group of receivers is making that abundantly clear to anyone who hadn't yet recognized it.
It's always unfortunate to see empty seats in a stadium, but it's even worse for a home team when you see more of the opponents' colors in the crowd than your own. Because of the beautiful weather in Tampa, Raymond James Stadium is notorious for attracting visiting fans. However, when an iconic franchise like the Steelers is in town and the Bucs are struggling, the 'home field disadvantage' can become that much more of a factor.
That was certainly the case today, as a sea of yellow terrible towels dominated much of the Stadium, creating an environment that surely helped fuel Pittsburgh's fourth quarter comeback in this game.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Overtime Loss to Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost their fifth game of the season to the Pittsburgh Steelers, falling 26-19 in overtime. The Bucs go to 1-5 with the close loss, and they fall even further down the division ladder.
The Bucs started out strong with a 16-3 lead, but the momentum massively shifted in the third quarter and Tampa Bay fell behind, eventually losing in overtime to Pittsburgh. It was the first overtime game the Bucs played since 2024.
Here are our three overreactions to Tampa Bay's game:
The Bucs may have lost the game, but Tampa Bay's defense has been looking strong ever since its game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 2. And it showed up again in a big way on Sunday.
The Steelers had just 2.2 yards per attempt in the first half of this game, shutting down Aaron Rodgers completely. The team racked up multiple sacks, including from Miami rookies Rueben Bain Jr. and Keionte Scott, and they were largely able to contain the run game as well.
This Bucs team stifled Pittsburgh at every turn. While the team still needs work and they weren't challenged at all downfield, Tampa Bay's defense deserves a lot of credit on Sunday — and the last few weeks — for being a stout unit.
Unfortunately, the offense did the Bucs no favors, tiring out the defense with frequent three-and-outs. But the Bucs held the Steelers to multiple field goals on the day and did their job, which is encouraging for the team going forward.
It's been tough sledding for Buccaneers punter Riley Dixon. Heading into Week 6, Dixon ranked 33rd of 33 qualifying punters in net yards per punt (37.1).
This game against the Steelers wasn't much better. Dixon averaged just 40.8 yards per punt against the Steelers, putting the Bucs' defense in bad situations throughout the day. It's only a matter of time before it impacts Tampa Bay in a big way going forward, and it arguably did in the loss to Pittsburgh on Sunday.
The Bucs should at least take a look at what else is out there so far — and they should at most make a change going forward this season.
Feels like we say this way too often. Walker has three sacks this year with limited snap time, and he got another on Aaron Rodgers in a big way to stop what could have been a scoring drive for Pittsburgh. He got another late to force the Steelers to kick when the two-minute warning hit.
He also had a nice pressure to get Al-Quadin Muhammad a sack, and he made a tackle for loss to force a Steelers field goal on that same drive. Walker has been a disruptor every time he's been on the field, and it's about time that he gets starting reps in this offense.
So far this year, he's proven he's the best pass rusher on the team. The Bucs should realize that and give him the starting reps he deserves going forward.

title: Buccaneers Running Back Inactive vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers need to stack as many wins as possible to save a season already on the brink. The Bucs are 1-4 and trying to move to 2-4, but the Pittsburgh Steelers are coming to Raymond James Stadium in hopes of knocking them down to 1-5.
Tampa Bay's offense played well last Thursday in a 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys, and the running game particularly excelled behind the legs of Bucky Irving. Running back Kenny Gainwell plays behind Irving, but Tampa Bay will not have their RB3 against the Steelers when they play on Sunday afternoon.
Here's who's inactive vs. the Steelers in Week 6:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be without running back Sean Tucker for their game against the Steelers, the team announced Sunday. Tucker, who was questionable to play with a quad injury, is inactive — he did not practice Wednesday but was a limited participant on Thursday and Friday.
Week 6 inactives for the Bucs: DL DeMonte Capehart G Luke Haggard QB Baker Mayfield CB Benjamin Morrison G Billy Schrauth RB Sean Tucker S Antoine Winfield Jr.
Tucker only has eight carries for 28 yards, averaging 3.5 yards per carry. He does have a touchdown, though, and he got eight yards on a 4th & 1 carry the play prior to set that touchdown up. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has mentioned wanting to get him more carries, but with Tucker hurt, he'll have to wait.
In Tucker's place will be running back Josh Williams. Williams has already been elevated to the practice squad once before this in Week 1, so this is his second elevation — the team's other elevation, Easton Stick, will now have been called up three times and can no longer be called up unless he's signed to the active roster.
Cornerback Benjamin Morrison is also inactive, as he was doubtful to play with a quad injury of his own. Morrison has missed significant time this season, missing the last two games with a quad injury. Cornerback Ayden Garnes, questionable to play on Friday's injury report, will replace him.
The Bucs' rushing attack will lean on Irving and Gainwell, just as it has even with Tucker available to play. The Bucs will have to try and break through a vaunted defensive line that includes standouts like T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and more.
The Bucs play the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Steelers Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking to get their second win in a row, and they'll get the opportunity back home when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday.
The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers.
As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out:
The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers.
I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays.
I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win.
I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend.
So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week.
Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon.
Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win.
This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh.
I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season.
I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better.
The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters.
On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too.
The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it.
The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year?

title: Steelers Cornerback Who Won Super Bowl With Buccaneers Talks Return to Tampa Bay
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are facing the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, and when they do, they'll see two familiar faces.
One of those faces is very familiar, because he was a Buccaneer two weeks ago. Cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting was on Tampa Bay's practice squad at the start of the season, but now he's on the Steelers' 53-man roster after Pittsburgh signed him two weeks ago.
Murphy-Bunting will reunite with the other familiar face, and that's cornerback Jamel Dean. Both of them won a Super Bowl with the Bucs in 2020, but Dean played with the Bucs until 2025. He hit free agency afterward and signed with Pittsburgh, and now, he's already making his homecoming to Tampa Bay after seven seasons with the Bucs.
Dean will have to go up against players he was teammates with just last year. This week, he's spoken on what it will mean to return to Tampa Bay — and how he's been helping the Steelers out.
Dean spoke to Penn Live reporter Nick Farabaugh about returning to Tampa Bay. Dean called it a "bittersweet moment", and he seems particularly excited to go up against his former head coach and defensive coordinator, Todd Bowles.
“It kinda feels like it’s going to be student finally going against the teacher.  I can’t wait to see how everything unravels," Dean said . "It’ll be a bittersweet moment for me. When I go into the stadium, hopefully I don’t go on autopilot and walk into their locker room.”
That's not all, though. According to ESPN reporter Brooke Pryor, Dean has also been trying to give the offense some tips on how to go up against Bowles' defense — he just doesn't think he'll be much of a help against his former head coach.
"I gave [the Steelers offense] little nuggets of what could possibly happen," Dean said . "But knowing [Bowles], he's probably planning for this right now, so won't be much use."
Dean has played good football so far this year. He's already had two forced fumbles, 14 combined tackles and he hasn't allowed a passing touchdown yet this season.
The Bucs will reunite with Dean when they play the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday, but they'll hope he goes back to Pittsburgh with a loss as Tampa Bay tries to move to 2-4 on the year.

title: New Report Reveals When Baker Mayfield Could Return for Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. When they do, they won't be playing their starting quarterback.
Undrafted free agent rookie has been deputizing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for the last two games as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. Daniels hasn't been bad in the role, and he's set to play another game on Sunday under center as Mayfield continues to recover.
This is Mayfield's team, though, and the team's three-year, $165 million extension of him this offseason proves it. Mayfield has been itching to get back to action ever since his injury, and one NFL insider pinpointed the exact game that could happen — and it's coming up very soon.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that there's "optimism" in Tampa Bay that Mayfield could return for the team's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers.
Bucs QB Baker Mayfield will miss a third consecutive game since dislocating his thumb in Week 3. But there’s optimism he’ll return next week — just in time for Tampa Bay’s first division game of the season at Carolina. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/hVvUAJDNjT pic.twitter.com/HwpFcNzTQY
Mayfield tried to throw on Wednesday afternoon after Bucs practice. It's unknown how that throwing session went, but the team clearly did not think he was ready enough to get back to practice this week, so Daniels gets the start once again for Tampa Bay.
This return timeline makes sense for a lot of reasons, however. To begin, Bowles' initial assessment of Mayfield's injury was three weeks minimum — it will be past that assessment once the Bucs play the Steelers this Sunday, so Mayfield's window has opened up.
Additionally, this will be Tampa Bay's first NFC South game. The team, despite being 1-4, is one and a half games out of the NFC South lead, so it's crucial to gain some ground in that division. Tampa Bay will want its starting quarterback out there when it does, so it's understandable that Mayfield would try to get back in time for it.
Finally, Mayfield used to play for Carolina in 2022, and the experience was an overall negative one for him. He's made it very clear that he pays particular attention to revenge games on the schedule, so there's probably some extra incentive there as well.
Before he got hurt, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He's struggled in a few different respects, though, as he's fumbled the ball three times this year and lost all of them. He'll look to bounce back from his recent stretch of play when he gets back under center for the Bucs.
Tampa Bay — led by Daniels — will play the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium. But don't expect Mayfield to be away for long.
